From our opening verse, Isaac "pleaded" with the Lord. This does not mean he begged; instead, it means he earnestly prayed and made his request. God responded by blessing him and Rebekah with twins. If your situation feels impossible,
whether it is related to health, finances, or any other challenge, simply ask God. He is always ready and willing to meet your needs and fulfill your requests.
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for the privilege to approach You in prayer. I ask boldly and confidently in the name of Jesus, knowing my requests will be granted. My joy is made complete because You always hear and answer me. Amen.
furtherStudies: Mark 11:24, Matthew 21:22, James 5:16
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Have Received Grace upon Grace
verse: For of His fullness we have all received, and grace upon grace.
body: ut of God's fullness, He has given you an overflow of grace - grace piled upon grace. This signifies abundance and sufficiency. No wonder "My grace is sufficient for you." (2 Corinthians 12:9 ESV) reminds us that His grace is enough. It is not just provided, but it is sufficient for every circumstance. Your responsibility is to activate and utilize this grace.

When God calls you for an assignment, He supplies all the grace you need to fulfill it. Similarly, when He promotes you, He provides the grace needed to sustain you at that level. This does not mean challenges will not arise, but the grace to overcome them has already been made available. As "Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in the heavenly realms with every spiritual blessing in Christ" (Ephesians 1:3 NIV) affirms, your blessings and grace are stored in the heavenly places.
To see these spiritual blessings manifest in your daily life, certain spiritual disciplines are necessary. Prayer, studying the Word of God, fasting, and making faith declarations help
release these blessings into the physical realm when you need them.

You see, you have grace heaped up for you. Think of it like water nearby when soap gets into your eyes while bathing. You do not need to panic or scream for help. Instead, you simply rinse your eyes with the water. Likewise, believers should not wander around looking for solutions to their challenges when God's grace is already available. His grace is sufficient for every situation you face.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for lavishing Your grace upon me. I am grateful for the abundance of grace You have made available. I choose to utilize this grace to impact my world and change circumstances around me.
furtherStudies: 2 Timothy 2:1 KJV, 2 Corinthians 12:9 KJV, Titus 2:11 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Offense is Dangerous
verse: But when you are praying, first forgive anyone you are holding a grudge against, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your sins too.
body: f or a while, the Lord has been pressing it upon my heart to write on the subject of offense. Often, believers find themselves weighed down because they are holding onto offenses caused by others. Offense arises from a perceived insult, disrespect, or disappointment. Other words associated with offense include anger, resentment, indignation, wrath, and vexation. These emotions can harm your spirit, soul, and body.

A few years ago, I met a Christian brother who was easily angered. When I asked him why he behaved this way, he said it was “holy anger.” However, whether anger seems holy or unholy, it is important to understand that it does not align with the recreated human spirit. God may lead you to feel displeasure toward unrighteousness or evil, but it is vital to act under the Spirit's guidance and not from the flesh.

The Bible reminds us, "Human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires" (James 1:20 NIV). Decisions made in anger often lead to destruction. Many have ruined their homes, marriages, relationships, and opportunities because of
uncontrolled anger. Self-control helps you stay calm during pressure and unfavorable situations.

Proverbs 25:28 (NLT) says "A person without self-control is like a city with broken-down walls." When the walls of a city are broken, it becomes vulnerable to attacks. Similarly, when you lack self-control, you are easily hurt by people's words and actions. Offense does not harm those who offend you; it only hurts you. Holding onto offense can lead to unforgiveness, which hinders your prayers (Mark 11:25 KJV) and leaves you spiritually vulnerable, especially during spiritual battles. I pray that the Lord will give you the grace to let go of every hurt and resentment. May He strengthen your heart to forgive and release every burden, in Jesus' name.
prayer: Dear Lord, I ask for Your forgiveness for the hurts and resentment I have held in my heart. Help me to forgive those who have wronged me and to walk in self-control. Teach me to live free from offense and to remain calm in every situation, in Jesus' name.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 25:28 TPT, Proverbs 16:32 KJV, 1 Samuel 20:30 KJV, Proverbs 22:24
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Being Born Again
verse: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of Incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.
body: In John 3:3-7, we see a conversation between Jesus and Nicodemus, a religious leader who wanted to know how to be saved. Jesus told him, "Unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God." To be "born again" means a change of heart, a spiritual renewal that only God can give.

Being born again is an act of God where eternal life is given to those who believe in Jesus. It is often referred to as being saved. Romans 3:23 (ESV) says, "For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God." Sin brings punishment, but God sent His Son, Jesus, to take your place and bear the consequences of sin. When you believe in Jesus, God promises salvation as stated in Romans 10:9: "If you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved."

From that moment, you are a new person. 2 Corinthians 5:17 (NLT) declares, "This means that anyone who belongs to Christ has become a new person. The old life is gone; a new life has begun." God sees you without a past, and He calls you to make a conscious effort to live for Him. This includes joining a Bible-
believing church to help guide you on your journey with God.
prayer: Precious Lord, thank You for the gift of Your Son, Jesus, who has brought salvation to my soul. I am a new creation in Christ, and I will continue to walk in the realities of who I am in Him. I choose to be a vessel of righteousness, bringing glory to Your name. Amen.
furtherStudies: 2 Corinthians 5:17, Ephesians 2:8-9, 1 John 2:29, 1 John 5:18
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Hold on to His Word
verse: Then Rachel told him, 'Take my maid, Bilhah, and sleep with her. She will bear children for me, and through her, I can have a family too.
body: t he stories of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob show how each patriarch faced challenges when their wives experienced delays in conceiving. Their responses to these difficulties varied. Abraham followed Sarah's advice to have a child with Hagar, which led to complications and a bitter experience.

Isaac, however, prayed to the Lord for his wife, Rebekah, and God answered his prayer, enabling her to conceive (Genesis 25:21 NIV). Jacob repeated a mistake similar to Abraham's by accepting Rachel's suggestion to have children through her maid, Bilhah, which also brought challenges (Genesis 30:3 (NLT)).

Despite these struggles, God's promise to Abraham to make him a father of many nations and to bless his descendants remained unshaken. However, the devil actively challenged these promises, demonstrating that spiritual opposition often comes after God gives a word or promotion. This reminds us to stay spiritually alert and hold firmly to God's word during times of testing.

Abraham's response to pressure is a model for us. As stated in Romans 4:19-21, "He did not waver at the promise of God through unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God." Abraham trusted God's word, despite his circumstances. When it seems like God's promises are delayed, remain steadfast. Act like Abraham by holding on to God's word until His promises are fulfilled in your life. As Jesus taught in Luke 8:15 (KJV), "But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience."
prayer: My faith is alive in God. I am not moved by what I see or hear, but only by the word of God. I hold on to His promises until they are fulfilled in my life. In Jesus' name, Amen! FURTHER
furtherStudies: Genesis 17:2, Romans 4:19-21, Hebrews 10:23-25
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Have Been Ordained to Receive Answers to your Prayers
verse: I tell you, you can pray for anything, and if you believe that you have received it, it will be yours.
body: m any believers hesitate when called to pray because they feel God no longer answers prayers or doubt the effectiveness of prayer. However, Jesus clearly commanded in Mark 11:24 that we should pray for anything, believe we have received it, and it will be ours.

The main challenge lies in not truly believing in the answers to our prayers. This lack of faith can make prayer seem uninteresting and unfruitful. Yet, as children of God, we are ordained to receive answers to our prayers. The one who answers prayers lives in us, expecting us to come to Him in faith. God finds joy in hearing and answering our prayers because it is an opportunity for fellowship with Him (1 John 1:3).

Jesus emphasized this in Matthew 21:22 (NIV), saying, "If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer." Similarly, Matthew 7:11 reminds us of God's willingness to give good gifts to those who ask Him. God is waiting for you to pray.
When you believe and ask in faith, you will receive answers that bring joy and fulfillment to your heart.
prayer: Precious Father, I thank You for the privilege of prayer and the assurance of receiving answers. I am confident in Your word and will always believe in Your power to grant all of my desires when I pray. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Philippians 4:6, James 5:16, Mark 11:24
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Your Name Affects your Destiny
verse: Your name will no longer be Jacob," the man told him. "From now on, you will be called Israel.
body: n ames are significant and can greatly influence your destiny and outcomes in life. A name can reflect aspects of a person's birth, the reactions of parents, or the circumstances surrounding their arrival. Names may also communicate a message from God, signify family ties, or establish authority and identity in an individual's life.

Jacob's life was marked by struggle. He wrestled with his brother Esau for blessings, worked tirelessly to marry Rachel, endured hardships for his family, and fought to maintain peace with Laban. Even his prayer in Genesis 32:26 highlights his persistence as he wrestled all night with God for a blessing. Despite his successes, Jacob's struggles revealed that his name, meaning “supplanter” or “deceiver,” was a hindrance to his destiny.

It wasn't until Jacob encountered God and his name was changed to Israel that his destiny shifted (Genesis 32:28). This divine intervention transformed his life, releasing him from the cycle of struggle and opening a new chapter of grace and
fulfillment.

God has changed names throughout the Bible to reflect new purposes and destinies. Abram, meaning “exalted father,” became Abraham, meaning “father of many nations” (Genesis 17:1-5). Similarly, Sarai's name, which symbolized barrenness, was changed to Sarah, meaning “mother of nations” (Genesis 17:15-16).

In 1 Chronicles 4:9-10, Jabez, whose name means “sorrow,” prayed to God for a change in his story, and God answered him. Your name carries significance and has the potential to influence your life and destiny. If there is a name you bear that doesn't align with God's purpose for you, it is time to trust Him for a change.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for revealing to me the effect of my name on my destiny. I thank You for the name of Jesus upon my life and the blessings it brings. Daily, I experience the fullness of the finished work of Christ in every aspect of my life. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: John 1:42, Genesis 17:1-5, Genesis 17:15-16
author: Apostle Chuks

title: His Love is Unfailing
verse: For the LORD is good and his love endures forever; his faithfulness continues through all generations.
body: Ilove the way our opening verse is rendered in the New Living Translation: "For the Lord is good. His unfailing love continues forever, and his faithfulness continues to each generation." God's love is truly unfailing. Unlike human love, which is often fickle and can change depending on loyalty or interests, God's love remains constant.

There are times when I have seen believers feeling depressed and deeply worried because they thought their mistakes were so grievous that God would have difficulty forgiving them. At times, they even feel they have exhausted God's love and mercy. However, God's love for you endures forever. This means His love has endurance, is never exhausted, and is everlasting. “I have loved you with an everlasting love; I have drawn you with unfailing kindness” (Jeremiah 31:3).

In Romans 8:35, 38-39, Paul asks, “Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or hardship or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword? For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor demons, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor

depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” God's love for you is eternal, and nothing can separate you from the love of God in Christ Jesus. His love for you endures forever and continues through all generations.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for loving me with an everlasting love. Your faithfulness reassures me that nothing can separate me from Your love. Help me to extend Your love to others, regardless of how they treat me. I walk confidently in the knowledge of Your unfailing love. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: 1 John 4:7, Matthew 5:45, Ephesians 2:4-5
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Have an Unction from God
verse: But you have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things.
body: t he Amplified Bible explains the above verse in detail: “But you have an anointing from the Holy One [you have been set apart, specially prepared by the Holy Spirit], and all of you know [the truth because He teaches us, illuminates our minds, and guards us from error].” The word "anointing" translates to "chrisma," the same term used for "unction" in 1 John 2:20 and 1 John 2:27. It refers to the Holy Spirit's work in the believer's life.

The pronoun "ye" in 1 John 2:20 emphasizes the difference between true believers and those who do not believe that Jesus is the Son of God. This experience is exclusive to believers. When you received the Holy Spirit, you received the anointing. This anointing equips you to live a victorious Christian life.

This anointing of the Holy Spirit brings light to your heart and clarity to your mind, helping you discern truth. It reveals divine insights and enables you to know things that no one else can teach you. This "knowing" comes from the Spirit within, offering guidance and protection from deception.

The unction of the Holy Spirit helps you navigate life, making it difficult for anyone to mislead you. It is a gift that transforms your spiritual walk, but you must remain aware of it. God does not want you to be ignorant of this unction. Instead, He desires that you grow in it by yielding to the Holy Spirit and engaging in activities that foster spiritual development, such as prayer, fasting, and studying the Bible. As you do, you will move from one level of glory to another.
prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for filling my heart with Your precious Holy Spirit, who guides, teaches, counsels, and illuminates my life. I yield myself to His ministry and will always seek to grow in His guidance. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 13:11, John 14:26, Acts 10:38, 1 John 4:13
author: Apostle Chuks

title: All Things Work Together for Good
verse: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
body: There are a few questions you need to ask yourself: (1) Do you love God? (2) Are you called according to God's purpose? If your answer is "yes," then certainly all things will work together for your good. This means you cannot be disadvantaged, regardless of what challenges you may be facing. God can turn your story around and bring you out of that situation, even when you feel bad.

In Genesis 45:4-8, Joseph recognized how God allowed everything to happen the way it did for a better and bigger plan. I like what Joseph said in verse 8: "So it was God who sent me here, not you! And he is the one who made me an adviser to Pharaoh - the manager of his entire palace and the governor of all Egypt" (ALT).

Although Joseph's brothers had wanted to get rid of him, God used their evil actions to accomplish His ultimate plan. He sent Joseph ahead of time to preserve their lives, save Egypt from famine, and prepare the path for the nation of Israel to evolve.

God is supreme, and His purposes cannot be restricted by human actions. When others plan evil against you, God will turn their plans into instruments and channels that will favor you. I pray for you today that all the devil planned for evil will be turned around for your good. Your miracle will become a testimony in Jesus' name. Amen.
prayer: I declare that all things are working together for my good, my joy, and my peace. I cannot be disadvantaged. Everything I face in life brings me closer to God's ultimate plan for my life. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: READINGBIBLE Genesis 45:4-8 ALT, Romans 5:3-4 KJV, Romans 9:11 KJV, Romans 9:23-24 KJV.
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Dealing with Hurt
verse: Make allowance for each other's faults, and forgive anyone who offends you. Remember, the Lord forgave you, so you must forgive others
body: w e all have feelings and emotions. There are things that could affect your feelings and make you feel hurt when ill-treated. There are certain circumstances and people that will always try to make you feel hurt, but it is important to deal with the situation wisely, according to the principles of the Word of God.

God wants your joy to be full. "These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full" (John 15:11 KJV). God will not bring you any hurt or harm. People get hurt when offended. Offense is a trap that can lead you into a rabbit hole of resentment. "Do not give the devil a foothold" (Ephesians 4:27 NLT).

To deal with hurt, the first thing to do is to surrender the right to seek revenge. "Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against anyone" (Leviticus 19:18). Rather, allow God to justify the situation. "Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28). Jesus understands that the situation can burden and wear you out, so He is asking you to pray and commit the situation to Him. He will give you His
peace and freedom, taking away the burden of hurt from you.

One of the amazing things about committing the situation to God is that He will heal you, take away the bitterness, and clean up the bad memories, leading you to wholeness. Since you have committed it to God, you have to let go because God is handling the situation. It is just like after a car collision; the insurance company gets involved in settling the claims and compensating the parties. You no longer have to bother yourself or try to justify who was right or wrong.
Lastly, repent of any sinful anger you may have harbored in your heart before committing the situation to God.
prayer: Dear Father, this day, I repent of every anger I have harbored in my heart. I forgive everyone who has hurt me. Heal me of every hurt, and help me to let go of all offense and bitterness. I release them all right now. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 12:19-21 KJV, Deuteronomy 32:35 NKJV, Romans 12:14-17 KJV.
author: Apostle Chuks

title: All Things Were Created for His Glory
verse: For everything comes from God alone. Everything lives by his power, and everything is for his glory. To him be glory evermore.
body: p salm 24:1 (NIV) says "The earth is the Lord's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it." The entire world and all creation belong to the Lord, for He made everything for Himself. The ultimate purpose of the universe is to reveal the glory of God.

The glory of God is who He is; it is the essence of His nature and the radiance of His splendor. It is the atmosphere of His presence, reflecting His goodness and all His eternal, intrinsic characteristics.

Everything God created reveals His glory in one way or another. You can literally see God's glory in all creation - through the air, the wind, the land, and both animate and inanimate things. "The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands" (Psalm 19:1 NIV).
Your desire should be to live to glorify God. Ensure that your thoughts, words, actions, the places you go, and the things you do glorify Him. This fulfills the purpose for which you were
created. "So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God" (1 Corinthians 10:31 NIV).
prayer: Precious Father, I rejoice and thank You for creating me in Your glory and for Your glory. I thank You for the understanding and knowledge I have received from Your Word. From today onward, I will live my life to glorify You. Let my light shine brightly so others can glorify You too. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 16:4 (NLT), Psalm 19:1 (KJV), Hebrews 1:3 (KJV), Matthew 5:16 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Greatest Achievement in Life
verse: All who are called by my name I created for my glory, whom I formed and made.
body: Isaiah 64:8 (NKJV) says "But now, O Lord, You are our Father; we are the clay, and You our potter; and all we are the work of Your hand." God is the potter, and we are the clay. He molds and shapes us into whatever fulfills His purpose, all for His glory. His satisfaction lies in creation serving its purpose and bringing Him glory.

God gave human beings the power of choice - the ability to choose between good and evil. You have the choice to live for His glory or not. The Creator is delighted and satisfied when He sees His creation fulfilling its purpose as a reflection of His glory.

What use is a vessel if it does not serve its purpose? Living for God's glory is the greatest achievement any person can accomplish. It is the reason He created you. "Everyone who is called by my name, whom I have created for my glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him" (Isaiah 43:7 NKJV).
Proverbs 16:4 says, "The Lord has made all for Himself." Therefore, let your utmost desire be to glorify God. When you live to satisfy the purpose for which you were created, He will be
pleased with you.
prayer: I am the glory of God. I reflect the glory of God in all my ways. I was created in God's image for His glory. I have been bought with a price, and I will always live to please and satisfy the reason God made me.
furtherStudies: Psalm 8:1 (KJV), Romans 11:36 (KJV), Hebrews 2:10 (KJV), Revelation 4:11 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Slow to Anger
verse: My dear brothers and sisters, take note of this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry.
body: a nger is not good for you, and because of the disasters that accompany it, God is calling you to order. "He whose spirit is without restraint is like a city broken down and without walls" (Proverbs 25:28 ASV).

You are the temple of God, and His Spirit lives in you. As 1 Corinthians 6:19 (NKJV) says, "Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you?" There is a hedge around you that provides protection. Many people break this hedge through anger, making themselves vulnerable to the enemy's attacks. "Whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake" (Ecclesiastes 10:8 KJV).

The snake refers to the devil, and he can only attack when the walls are broken down. By default, a Christian should not be victimized or defeated. "No weapon formed against you shall prosper" (Isaiah 54:17 NKJV). However, many times the reason the devil succeeds in his attacks is that people have broken their walls of defense through anger, resentment, and unforgiveness.

"Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger resides in the lap of fools" (Ecclesiastes 7:9 NIV). James admonished the brethren to be slow to anger. Anger reveals a person's foolishness. The more offended or angry one becomes, the more foolishness takes over their life. God has filled us with the spirit of wisdom; therefore, do not give room for foolishness like anger.
prayer: I declare that the spirit of wisdom is at work in me. I do not accommodate foolishness. I am slow to anger. I have self- control, and my walls of defense are well-fortified, protecting me from the enemy.
furtherStudies: Nehemiah 9:17 (KJV), Proverbs 15:18 (KJV), Proverbs 14:17 (KJV), Proverbs 14:29 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Let your Light Shine
verse: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
body: m atthew 5:14 (ESV) says, "You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden." As a believer, you are the light of the world, a city on the mountaintop that cannot be hidden. You are light, so stop trying to hide yourself.

To hide simply means not manifesting. There are so many graces and abilities God has bestowed upon you. Many believers are not impacting their world with these blessings of God. They are either ignorant of this truth, do not know how to manifest, or something is stopping them from manifesting.

Firstly, I want you to understand that God is light, and when you got saved, you received the light of life. "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life" (John 8:12 ESV). Because the light of life resides in you, it makes you a light. Secondly, God expects you to transform the lives of others.
To manifest means to shine. Since God's expectation is for you to shine, how do you do this? "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path" (Psalm 119:105 KJV). God's word is the

key. As you study God's word, it brings clarity to your life and shows you which areas of your life He wants you to manifest. It will produce good works that will be obvious, and people will begin to glorify God.

From Matthew 5:16, your shining might be thoughts and inspirations that God places in your heart. Feel free to share them with others. It could be ideas - go ahead and document them as books and share them with others. As you do this, you are letting your light shine.

There are many other ways to manifest; just ensure they are benevolent to all, just as Jesus went about doing good. "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and He went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil" (Acts 10:38 NKJV).
I pray for you today, may the Lord cause your light to shine brightly, and may anything hindering your manifestation be broken in Jesus' name. Amen!
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for making me the light of the world and a city set upon a hill that cannot be hidden. I pray that from today henceforth, my hunger for your word will increase, and your light will illuminate my path and shine through me. In Jesus' name, amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 5:14-16 (KJV), Matthew 4:16 (KJV), Isaiah 60:1-5 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: His Love is Unconditional, Unlimited, and Complete
verse: So we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
body: God's love is unconditional, unlimited, and complete. "We have come to know and believe the love that God has for us. God is love" (1 John 4:16 ESV). There are several kinds of love, but none of them compare to God's love. God's love is the highest form of love, known as Agape in Greek.

Agape is a profound, sacrificial love that surpasses circumstances. It is unconditional and has no limitations. In both good times and challenging times, His love remains the same. Whether you are saved or not yet saved, His love for you is constant. You might wonder why God extends His love to sinners and unbelievers. The answer is in Romans 2:4 (NLT): "Don't you see how wonderfully kind, tolerant, and patient God is with you? Does this mean nothing to you? Can't you see that His kindness is intended to turn you from your sin?" God's love is an act of kindness, and His intention is to turn hearts to Him.
God's love is unlimited. This means His love has no boundaries; it is eternal and unending. "I have loved you with an everlasting
love" (Jeremiah 31:3 KJV). His love is everlasting.
God's love is complete; it is perfect and whole. There is nothing missing in His love for us, and there will never be any love greater than His. Therefore, rest in His love.
prayer: Precious Father, thank You for Your great love towards me, shown in the sacrifice of Your Son Jesus so that I might be saved. Thank You for such endless, unlimited, unconditional, and complete love. I am eternally grateful to You. In Jesus' name, amen!
furtherStudies: Ephesians 3:19 (KJV), Romans 8:37-39 (KJV), Romans 5:8 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Seek His Kingdom First
verse: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you.
body: t o seek the Kingdom of God simply means to live a devoted life to God, prioritizing His ways in every area of your life. It also means allowing your desires and pursuits to be focused on God and His kingdom. When you prioritize God in this manner, He will prioritize you and guide you in righteousness.

Many people try to live life without God. They put God and all that concerns Him in a corner or a box. Instead, they struggle and chase wealth, fame, their careers, and everything else that defines success according to human standards. True success, however, is a life of fulfillment, and it can only be found and accomplished in God. Anything apart from that is vanity.

If you really want to achieve your ambitions, commit them to God. He will guide you and direct your path and efforts toward success, especially according to His definition of success. As detailed in Proverbs 16:3 (AMP), "Commit your works to the Lord [submit and trust them to Him], and your plans will succeed [if you respond to His will and guidance]." Today, God is saying to you, "Seek my kingdom first," and in all your ways,
acknowledge Him. "He will make your path straight" (Proverbs 3:6 NIV).
prayer: Heavenly Father, I will continue to seek You and Your kingdom. The work of Your kingdom prospers in my hands. Thank You, Lord, for You lead me in the path of life and bring all my plans to fruition. In Jesus' name, amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:31-33 (KJV), Luke 12:31 (NIV), 1 Chronicles 28:9 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Bitterness: The Poison of the Soul
verse: Look after each other so that none of you fails to receive the grace of God. Watch out that no poisonous root of bitterness grows up to trouble you, corrupting many.
body: Offense refers to a state of being hurt, upset, or angry. When a person is offended, they develop a strong negative emotional reaction to whatever triggered the situation. If you get offended easily, you tend to become angry very quickly. Prolonged anger leads to hatred, and hatred leads to bitterness. It does not just end there; bitterness is cancerous.

“Catch all the little foxes, those little foxes, before they ruin the vineyard of love, for the grapevines are blossoming!” – Song of Solomon 2:15 NLT. Bitterness is one of the little foxes that destroy lives. It troubles you and causes you to sow seeds of bitterness into the lives of those around you, corrupting many others (Deuteronomy 29:18).

In Jeremiah 20:9, Prophet Jeremiah describes his bitterness as fire in his bones. Bitterness spreads like fire and works like cancer. It robs you of peace and affects your health. Proverbs 14:30 AMP says, “A calm and peaceful and tranquil heart is life and health to the body, but bitterness and envy are like
rottenness to the bones.” Choose to have a calm, peaceful, and tranquil heart so that you can live a healthy life.
prayer: I choose joy, peace, meekness, and happiness. My heart is full of joy. I rebuke the spirit of bitterness and anger, and I command you to get your hands off of me. I do not give room for unforgiveness, malice, anger, or bitterness. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Deuteronomy 29:18 BYV, Deuteronomy 32:32 KJV, Proverbs 14:30 NLT, Lamentations 3:4 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Establishing God’s Will on Earth
verse: For I know the plans I have for you,” declares the Lord, “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.
body: g od's will refers to His desires, plans, and intentions. When we pray, saying “Your will be done,” we are asking God to accomplish His desires on earth (Matthew 6:10 NIV). During creation, God was purposeful; He had a clear desire and will for everything, and He still seeks for His purposes to be fulfilled on earth.

In Matthew 26:39, Jesus prayed, “Let Your will be done,” in the Garden of Gethsemane before His crucifixion. Though He had a choice, He submitted to God's desire, proving His dedication to seeing God's will accomplished.

Scriptures like Ephesians 4:15 (“Speak the truth in love”), Ephesians 5:18 (“Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery”), and 1 Corinthians 6:18 (“Flee from sexual immorality”) reflect God's will for His creation. Praying “Your will be done” means asking God to increase righteousness on earth, turning hearts away from sin and toward a deeper knowledge of Him.

Jeremiah 29:11 and 3 John 1:2 reveal that God desires for you to prosper, to remain healthy, and to enjoy a beautiful future. If you are not yet experiencing these blessings, it is time to pray fervently for God's will to be done. Such prayers will cause God's plans and desires to manifest in your life.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for Your great desires for my life and for the earth. I submit to Your Lordship. Let Your will be done in my life and not mine. Let Your righteousness increase, and may Your kingdom reign on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name, amen!
furtherStudies: 3 John 1:2 (KJV), 1 Thessalonians 1:3-10 (KJV), Matthew 26:42 (KJV), Psalm 103:20 (NLT)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Christ Gives you Rest
verse: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
body: In Matthew 11:28, Jesus extends an open invitation to everyone. He says, “Come unto me, all of you who labour and are carrying heavy burdens, and I promise to give you rest.” The labour referred to here is not the work of your daily job or endeavors but the toil of living in vanity, serving sin, and being enslaved to Satan.

For every labour, there is a reward (Proverbs 31:31, Proverbs 12:14). When you labour or render service to Satan, his reward comes in the form of affliction, troubles, and eternal condemnation unless you repent and accept salvation. Similarly, labouring for Jesus involves taking up His yoke, which is light. His reward is salvation, which brings the blessings of divine providence on earth and prepares you to spend eternity with God the Father in heaven. In heaven, you will receive your full reward for serving the Lord.

Here, Jesus calls out to everyone in trouble, distress, affliction, or enslaved by sin. He offers to make things right for you and give you rest. In His rest, you will experience peace. As Hebrews 4:10 (NLT) says, “For all who have entered into God's
rest have rested from their labours.” This rest is the assurance Jesus gives when you receive Him into your heart as your Lord and Savior.
For more information on how to be saved or to rededicate your life to the Lord, kindly check the last few pages of this devotional.
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank You for the rest I have in You. I declare that because I am in Christ, the troubles, sickness, limitations, and afflictions I experience cease now in Jesus' name. I will continue to walk in righteousness and live for You. Amen!
furtherStudies: Hebrews 4:10 (AMP), Matthew 11:28-29 (KJV), Isaiah 53:2-3 (KJV), Isaiah 45:22-25 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Bearing Good Fruits
verse: A tree is identified by its fruits. If a tree is good, its fruits will be good. If a tree is bad, its fruits will be bad.
body: Atree is identified by its fruits. If a tree is good, it will produce good fruits. If a tree is bad, it will produce bad fruits. Your words and actions are your fruits. As Matthew 7:20 says, “So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.” Through your actions and words, one can tell who you are and what you are made of. You cannot fake it. Even if you try, time and light will reveal your true identity.

Galatians 5:19-20 points out the fruits of the flesh, and these fruits are very unpleasant to God. Anyone who bears such fruits will not inherit the kingdom of God. As Galatians 5:16 (NLT) says, “So I say, let the Holy Spirit guide your lives. Then you won't be doing what your sinful nature craves.” When you yield to the Holy Spirit, you can bring forth good fruits (Matthew 3:8- 10).

Galatians 5:22-23 (NLT) says, “But the Holy Spirit produces this kind of fruit in our lives: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.” By these fruits, it will be clear that you are a true believer and are yielding to the Holy Spirit. These fruits are different from the signs that
follow believers (Mark 16:17).

As John 15:4 (ESV) says, “Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in me.” God is calling you to yield yourself to His word and His Spirit. When you do so, His manifested presence will abide in you, and you will produce good fruits.
prayer: Dear Father, I thank You for Your Spirit that dwells in me, causing me to exhibit Your nature and bear fruits of righteousness. Through Your Spirit, I bring forth good fruits to the glory and praise of Your name. Amen!
furtherStudies: John 8:31 (NLT), Galatians 5:16-26 (NLT), Luke 6:43 (NLT)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Don’t Be Lukewarm
verse: Anyone who isn't with me opposes me, and anyone who isn't working with me is actually working against me.
body: a re you truly for God or against Him? Are you laboring with Him or against Him? There is no middle ground. You have to choose where you stand with God. You do not necessarily need to make a bold declaration to be against Him, but your words and actions will reveal on whose side you are. As Matthew 7:16 says, “By their fruits we know if they are with Christ or not. From our opening scripture, the phrase “actually working against me” implies not laboring for Him. Laboring for the devil produces fruits of unrighteousness and the flesh.

A lukewarm Christian is unstable and unenthusiastic about their faith in God. Jesus warned against lukewarm behaviors. As a true believer, you have no business living like someone who is not saved. It is sad to see believers still going to ungodly clubs, engaging in inappropriate activities in the name of fun or cooling off, or even consulting diviners or psychic readers. God does not condone such things, and He wants you to change your ways (Acts 17:30-31).
It is impossible to be neutral with God. Any person who is not

actively following Jesus is working against Him. As Matthew 6:24 (NKJV) says, “No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other.” Make a decision to serve the Lord, be enthusiastic about your faith in God, and live to please Him.
prayer: I am burning, active, and aglow for the Lord. My love for the Lord will not wax cold. I am consistent, and I boldly stand firm in Christ Jesus. Amen.
furtherStudies: Luke 9:62 (NLT), Psalms 78:8-9 (KJV), Philippians 3:13 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Flee from Every Appearance of Evil
verse: Abstain from every form of evil
body: f rom the opening Bible verse, the word abstain refers to staying away or not getting close. It also means to flee. Apostle Paul was addressing the Christian community in Thessalonica, which is present-day Greece, instructing them to stay away from anything that appears to be evil. Don't get close to anything that looks like evil; stay away from anything ungodly, immoral, or unscriptural.

There is a Persian proverb that says, “Don't play with the tail of a lion.” This means certain situations are very dangerous. Abstain from every form of evil because it is very dangerous. “And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out” – Genesis 39:12 KJV.

This refers to Joseph. When faced with the seduction of Potiphar's wife, he quickly ran away. Joseph didn't have to find out if it was truly an attempt because it was the appearance of evil. He fled. He didn't walk away but ran. This reveals no tolerance for evil. Don't play with or tolerate anything that appears to be evil. This includes communication, association, relationships, neighborhood, thoughts, and anything else that

appears like evil. “Run away from the evil that people long for. Try hard to do what is right. Have faith, love, and peace. Do these things together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart” – 2 Timothy 2:22 NIRV.

Reuben, as a young man, accommodated evil, and it cost him dearly. “And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: and Israel heard it” – Genesis 35:22 KJV. Although the consequences of his sin were not immediate, they were severe. As the oldest son, he was supposed to receive a double portion of the family inheritance and a place of leadership among his people. However, his blessings were given to someone else because he defiled his father's couch by lying with his father's concubine.

The consequences of evil often plague us long after the sin has been committed. We may think we can escape unnoticed, only to discover later that the sin has been quietly breeding serious consequences. Finally, flee from sin as you would from the face of a serpent, for if you come too near it, it will bite you.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for the cleansing effect of your Word. Forgive me for any form of sin I have committed because I didn't flee from it. Thank you for filling my heart with your Word so I may not sin against you. Your Word will always guide my thoughts and actions. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 6:18 KJV, 2 Timothy 2:22 KJV, Proverbs 3:7 KJV, Proverbs 4:14 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: He Lives in You
verse: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own.
body: w hen you got saved, God came to make His home in your heart. You have become God's residence. God lives in you now through the Holy Spirit. “Don't you realize that all of you together are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God lives in you?” – 1 Corinthians 3:16 NLT. God wants you to come to the realization and be conscious that you are His dwelling place.

Since He lives in you, it is important to permit Him to regulate your life because He is the Lord of your life. He is trustworthy, and He will guide you in the path you should go: the path of life, victory, and success. The presence of God in your life will be your inner light and guide. He will bear witness of Himself to you. He will grant you a good sense of judgment and discernment.

Because He lives in you, you are in a place of advantage. Hallelujah! “To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory” – Colossians 1:27 KJV.

Because He lives in you, you have hope - hope for joy, peace, victory, and wholeness. This hope is not just for this present world but also for a glorious future. We have a future; we have a home where we will spend eternity with the Lord, and that place is Heaven. Christ in you is your hope of glory.
prayer: Dear Lord, thank you for choosing to make Your home in me. I thank You for the glorious hope You have brought into my life. I will forever trust and submit to the leadership of Your Spirit in me. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 3:16-20 KJV, 2 Corinthians 6:16 KJV, John 14:17
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Have you Found Jesus?
verse: And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
body: m atthew 2:1-12 reveals how the Magi, also known as wise men, searched for Jesus when He was born. When they found Jesus, they worshiped Him and presented gifts to Him. As they were about to depart, God warned them in a dream not to return to Herod, and they obeyed the Lord. The key emphasis here is yielding to the Lord.

What has happened to you since you got saved? Have you been yielding to the Lord since you found Him? When the wise men found Jesus, they took a different direction. Finding Jesus might mean that your life could take a new direction. Your desires and aspirations might need to align with His purpose for your life.

In the book of Acts, “As he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven” – Acts 9:3 KJV. Saul, who was on a mission to persecute Christians, encountered Jesus, and the Lord told him, “Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do” – Acts 9:6 KJV. Saul's life and assignment took a new direction for the purpose of the Master.

Finding Jesus requires being open to His word and leadership. In what ways has Jesus affected the direction of your life? Jesus is the Lord of your life, and the word "Lord" means Master. As your Master, cultivate the attitude of yielding to Him, His purposes, and His directions.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the Master of my life. My heart and my whole being will always yield to Your leadership and direction. I will trust You at all times. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 3:5-6 KJV, Galatians 5:16 TPT, Acts 26:19 KJV, Romans 8:29 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: True Worship
verse: But a time is coming and is already here when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit (from the heart, the inner self) and in truth; for the Father seeks such people to be His worshipers.
body: j ohn 4:24 explains that God is a Spirit, and He created man to have a spirit, soul, and body. The spirit of man enables him to communicate with God. Your spirit was designed to interact with God, and true worship must come from the spirit - not from the flesh (body) or the soul. This means worship must be spiritual.

Many have thought that the "spirit" in John 4:24 refers to the Holy Spirit. However, it refers to the human spirit. This is the part of man's being where he bears the image of God and where the Holy Spirit dwells ("Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities..." – Romans 8:26 KJV).

It is vital to understand that worship in spirit is different from mere physical rituals, sacraments, or routines such as postures, washings, or recitations. Worshiping God in truth means doing so with revelation and understanding of who He is. God is eternal and sovereign. He is the Almighty, deserving of all glory and honor.
Understanding His majesty and glory transforms how we

worship him. His word is truth ("Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth." – John 17:17 KJV). As you study the Word of God, you will gain deeper insight into who God is. This understanding will help you worship Him in spirit and in truth.
prayer: Thank You, Father, for giving me an understanding of who You are and the kind of worship You expect from me. I will always worship You in spirit and in truth. As I continue to grow in Your Word, I will become more effective in offering You the worship You deserve. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: John 4:23-24 KJV, Philippians 3:3 KJV, John 1:14 NIV, Psalm 119:160 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Diligent
verse: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
body: t o be diligent means to show care and meticulous attention in your work or duties. It involves putting in your best effort in any task or assignment given to you. Even if you realize your effort is not good enough, strive to acquire new skills to improve your performance.

Diligence applies not only to satisfying your earthly master or boss but also to serving God, your ultimate Master. As you show diligence in your physical responsibilities, also be diligent in your prayer life and dealings with the Lord. Do not settle for less or remain at the baseline.

I once heard the story of a young boy whose performance in school was poor. He scored 40%, and when questioned by his parents, he replied that others also scored the same. This is not a good place to be - encouraging yourself with poor performance just because others did the same.
From our opening verse, we learn that the services of a diligent person will be sought after by kings, presidents and royalties, and not by commoners. When you are diligent, great people will

seek you out. Proverbs 21:5 says, "The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance and advantage, but everyone who acts in haste comes surely to poverty." This means the diligent person will have abundance, wealth, and profit, while one who does things carelessly will end in poverty. Make up your mind to be diligent today.
prayer: I have an excellent spirit within me, enabling me to be diligent, unique, and to produce works of excellence. I refuse to settle for less. Kings and great men seek my services always. I will never be average. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 10:4 KJV, Proverbs 6:6-8 AMP, 2 Peter 3:14 LB, Proverbs 12:27
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Practice Forgiveness
verse: For I will forgive their wickedness and will remember their sins no more.
body: t he New Oxford American Dictionary defines forgiveness as "the action or process of forgiving or being forgiven." I have heard people say things like, "I will forgive but I will not forget." The downside of forgiving and not forgetting is that whenever you remember what happened, it tends to reopen old wounds. The scar might remain, but you are still in bondage. God has the ability to make you whole. Why not pray to God to help you totally forgive, forget, and let go? When this happens, you will realize the scars are gone, and you will be free.

Forgiveness requires letting go of grudges and bitterness. It is more spiritual than physical. When you forgive, you experience a sense of peace. This peace comes from making the right decision to forgive. As Philippians 4:7 KJV says, "And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.”
In Genesis 45:17-20, Joseph was rejected, enslaved, falsely accused, and imprisoned. His brothers hurt him deeply and caused him great suffering. Many in his position would have
sought revenge, but Joseph graciously forgave his brothers, loved them, and repaid their evil with good. Joseph's actions reveal how God forgives us.

Forgiveness is a virtue and a fruit of the recreated human spirit. Emulate Joseph by practicing forgiveness. Do not wait for people to apologize before you forgive them. Forgive ahead of time so nothing holds you back. Some people may not know they hurt you, while others might refuse to apologize. Regardless, forgiveness liberates your soul. As detailed in Colossians 3:13 NIV, "Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance against someone. Forgive as the Lord forgave you."
prayer: Thank you, Father, for your nature of forgiveness at work in me. I will always bear with others and forgive their shortcomings. I will love others and see them from your point of view. I will be gracious and kind to others as I have obtained grace and kindness from you. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:14 NIV, Ephesians 4:32 KJV, Mark 11:25 KJV, Matthew 18:21-25 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Kind to Others
verse: But show me unfailing kindness like the LORD's kindness as long as I live, so that I may not be killed.
body: k indness is an attitude marked by acts of generosity, compassion, consideration, and rendering help to others without expecting praise or reward in return. From 1 Samuel 20:14, God's kindness towards us is unfailing. He also expects us to show an unfailing kindness to others.

Acts of kindness are not only in actions but also in words. "Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down, but a good word makes him glad." – Proverbs 12:25. When you say kind words to people, it uplifts them, makes them glad, and gives them hope. Simple kind words like "You look beautiful," "I love you," "Thank you," and "God bless you" can go a long way to cheer someone up. Supporting others, offering gifts, and performing acts of service are other ways to show kindness.

2 Timothy 2:24 AM says “And the Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, not resentful.” Be kind to everyone. Do not limit your kindness to only family members, friends, or well-wishers. Kindness is a generous act, so extend it even to those who have not treated
you well. This act of kindness can win their hearts for the Lord.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for your nature in me. Thank you for your love shed abroad in my heart by your Spirit. I will love everyone and show kindness to others through my words and actions. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Luke 6:35 NKJV, Romans 12:8 KJV, Galatians 5:22 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Earthly Permission for Heavenly Interference
verse: Verily I say unto you, whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
body: n othing just happens on earth. Before anything manifests here, it has already been approved in the spiritual realm. The spiritual realm operates either through the Kingdom of Heaven or the kingdom of darkness. For God to intervene in earthly matters, man must give Him permission because He has made man the custodian of the earth (Genesis 1:26). This permission is called prayer.

When we pray, we give God the authority to intervene. The New Living Translation renders Matthew 18:18 as: "I tell you the truth, whatever you forbid on earth will be forbidden in heaven, and whatever you permit on earth will be permitted in heaven." From this scripture, we understand that it is man's responsibility to grant permission for divine intervention.

As a believer, you have the power to forbid negative circumstances and permit God's will in your life through prayer. God watches over the earth, sees what you are going through, and waits for your permission to intervene. Jesus highlighted this truth in Luke 13:16 KJV, saying: "And ought not this

woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?" This woman was afflicted because Satan had bound her, but when she encountered Jesus, He loosed her from the bondage, and she was healed.

As a believer, you can use the name of Jesus to loose yourself or anyone else from any form of bondage or affliction. Mark 3:27 KJV explains: "No man can enter into a strong man's house and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house." This teaches us that to address negative situations, you must first bind the devil behind them.

When you bind or forbid Satan in prayer, God receives the permission to act on earth concerning your situation. As you loose or permit God's will, He brings about the desired change. Use the name of Jesus today to effect the change you desire.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for the power of attorney in the name of Jesus. As I pray and decree using the name of Jesus, I grant you the permission to intervene in my situation. Thank you for the resulting change and for making my joy full. In Jesus' name,
furtherStudies: 2 Matthew 12:29 KJV, Isaiah 49:24-26 KJV, Matthew 16:19 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Don’t Reject the Name of Jesus
verse: There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
body: a cts 4:12 clearly states that no one else can provide salvation other than Jesus. The careful choice of words in this scripture highlights a few important truths. The phrase "under heaven" refers to the earth, and the word "mortals" signifies human beings who are alive. Apostle Peter emphasizes that there is no other name on earth, given to humanity, by which we can be saved. The acceptance and use of the name of Jesus are for people on earth.

He did not say "beneath the earth." Beneath the earth refers to those who are dead. That is why Peter boldly declared that the only name that can save those who are alive is the name of Jesus. When a person dies, they cannot accept Jesus or use His name. This is why people who die without accepting Jesus cannot receive a second chance to believe in Him or use His name. They face eternal separation because they rejected Him while alive (Luke 16:24-29).
2 Corinthians 6:2 ESV says: "For he says, 'In a favorable time I listened to you, and in a day of salvation I have helped

you.'Behold, now is the favorable time; behold, now is the day of salvation." Indeed, now is the favorable time to accept Jesus and His name. This is the perfect opportunity to accept Him, live by His name, and allow Him to guide your life before it is too late.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for loving me and sending Jesus to die for me so that I might be saved. I reaffirm the lordship of Jesus over my life, and I will always live to the glory and praise of your name. In Jesus' name, amen!
furtherStudies: Joel 2:12-13 KJV, Isaiah 55:6-13 KJV, Luke 16:24-30 KJV, Acts 10:43 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Love your Enemies
verse: Bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
body: The command to love our enemies is profound. Our opening scripture makes it clear that those who hate, curse, and persecute us are regarded as our enemies. There are two categories of enemies: physical and spiritual.

Physical enemies are individuals who hate or mistreat you without using spiritual forces against you, as seen in Matthew 5:44 and Luke 6:28. Joseph's brothers hated him, but they did not employ divination or enchantments against him. When dealing with physical enemies, approach them with caution, but still love them.

Spiritual enemies, on the other hand, are those who antagonize and fight against you using dark spiritual forces, such as witchcraft, divination, or enchantments. These are your true adversaries. It is important to note that some people may act under the influence of such satanic forces, opposing you unknowingly. Such cases are spiritual warfare, and they require a different approach (Ephesians 6:10-18). You can love these individuals by praying for their salvation but avoid sharing your secrets or forming close relationships with them.

In Matthew 5:44, Jesus was specifically referring to physical enemies. He teaches us not to retaliate when they do us harm. Instead, we should love and pray for them. By doing so, we overcome evil with good. Loving your enemies and treating them kindly is evidence that Jesus is guiding your life.

Do not say you cannot love your enemies because of the wrongs they have done to you. "The love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit" (Romans 5:5). Depend on the Holy Spirit to help you love and treat your enemies well. Loving your enemies can bring them to the Lord and even inspire them to love you in return. Love conquers all, including people and challenging situations (1 Corinthians 13:7).
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for your love and for giving me the nature of love. Your love in me enables me to love everyone, regardless of what they may have done to me. I will continue to treat my enemies rightly and pray for them. I ask that you touch their hearts and bring them to salvation so they can know Jesus. In His name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 5:43-48 KJV, 1 Samuel 24:17 KJV, Proverbs 25:21 KJV, Luke 23:34 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Glorify God in your Body
verse: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own.
body: a s a believer, your body is God's dwelling place through the Holy Spirit. You are not your own; your body belongs to God. For this reason, you cannot treat your body however you want.

Think of it this way: if your boss gave you $500 USD for a specific task, you would not use the money for something unrelated. Similarly, your body, which belongs to God, must be used only in ways that glorify Him. "You were bought with a price (you were actually purchased with the precious blood of Jesus and made His own). So then honor and glorify God with your body" (1 Corinthians 6:20 AMP).

Honor God by using your body in ways that please Him. Avoid actions that dishonor your body, such as sexual immorality, drunkenness, smoking, and gluttony. These activities do not glorify God and can destroy your body. "Flee from sexual immorality. All other sins a person commits are outside the body, but whoever sins sexually sins against their own body" (1 Corinthians 6:18 AV).

It is important to refrain from things that defile your body. Some believers engage in inappropriate conversations, visit ungodly places, or participate in evil actions. Even consuming worldly and ungodly content, whether by watching, listening, or reading, misuses your body. These actions do not glorify God.

If you did not know this before now, God has given you an opportunity to repent. "And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men everywhere to repent" (Acts 17:30 KJV). Since your body has been bought at a price, glorify God in everything you do with your body.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for making me a temple where you dwell. I am grateful for your Lordship over my life. I commit to glorifying you in my body at all times. Through your Spirit, I will mortify the deeds of my body and subject it to your will. In Jesus' name, amen. FURTHER
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 KJV, Romans 12:1 KJV, Philippians 1:20 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Perfection in Christ
verse: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
body: t he Amplified version of Matthew 5:48 renders this verse in clearer terms: "You, therefore, will be perfect (growing into spiritual maturity both in mind and character, actively integrating godly values into your daily life), as your heavenly Father is perfect."
God is perfect, and He desires us to grow into perfection as He is perfect. While we are not there yet, He calls us to work towards it. Perfection is a process that requires our active involvement.

The perfect believer is one who has grown into maturity in Christ. "And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ" (Ephesians 4:11-13 KJV).
We are all works in progress. As Paul said, "I don't mean to say that I have already achieved these things or that I have already
reached perfection. But I press on to possess that perfection for which Christ Jesus first possessed me" (Philippians 3:12 NLT).

The question often arises: how can a believer become perfect? Here are key ways: 1. Holiness: Separate yourself from the world and its sinful values. Let your desire be to please the Lord rather than to satisfy the desires of the flesh. 2. Growing into Maturity: God expects us to "press" forward. This means putting in full effort into activities that enhance our development in Christ and our character. 3. Walking in Love: "The love of God is shed abroad in our hearts" (Romans 5:5 KJV). This love motivates us to obey God's Word and spend more time with Him. As we do this, the desires of the flesh begin to fade, and He reveals Himself to us more deeply. This increases our desire to grow into His perfection.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for your perfect nature in me. It causes me to desire and press towards becoming a perfect reflection of Christ. As I continue to know you, I am continuously transformed into the fullness of Christ. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: 2 Corinthians 7:1 KJV, Ephesians 5:1-10 NLT, Philippians 3:12-13 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: May Your Kingdom Come!
verse: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.
body: m ay your kingdom come" is part of the Lord's Prayer. The Lord's Prayer is a model of prayer that Jesus taught His disciples and all future believers. The disciples observed how Jesus prayed and asked Him to teach them how to pray.

To understand the phrase "May your kingdom come," it is essential to know a bit about kingdoms. There are two kingdoms: the Kingdom of God, also known as the Kingdom of Light, and the kingdom of Satan, also known as the Kingdom of Darkness (Matthew 12:26 KJV).

From the beginning, Satan has rebelled against God, leading to a conflict between the Kingdom of God and the kingdom of Satan. "And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force" (Matthew 11:12 KJV).
Jesus came to establish God's Kingdom and His government on earth. Before leaving the earth, He gave us the assignment
to share the message of God's Kingdom. Those who accept Jesus into their hearts gain access to the Kingdom of God (John 14:12, John 14:36, Romans 10:9 KJV).

However, Satan continues to fight against God's Kingdom and His purposes for the earth. This is why Jesus taught us to pray, "May your kingdom come and your will be done on earth." Praying for God's Kingdom to come invites His rule into the hearts of men and women. It paves the way for His ultimate will (that all men be saved) to be accomplished on earth. As we anticipate Christ's return, let us pray fervently in this manner: "Even so, come, Lord Jesus" (Revelation 22:20 KJV).
prayer: Our Father, all honor and praise be to You. Let Your Kingdom come and Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Let Your work prosper on earth, and I pray for the unsaved. May they be freed from the bondage of the devil and come to the knowledge of Your Word and be saved. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:10 KJV, Revelation 22:20 KJV, Isaiah 14:12-15 KJV, Ezekiel 28:11-17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Have Self-Control
verse: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
body: d ominion means exercising control or having power over a particular thing or situation. Sin should not control you; rather, you should exercise dominion over all types of sin. Today's article focuses on self-control, a vital behavioral pattern that God desires in your life. God wants you to be in control of yourself - your thoughts, feelings, emotions, words, and actions. The ability to be in control of yourself is called self-control.

From Romans 6:14 KJV, we learn that it is possible to live a sin- free life while walking on this earth. The key to living a sin-free life is self-control. The Holy Spirit enables you to exercise self- control (Galatians 5:22-23 KJV).

The Holy Spirit gives you the ability to exercise restraint and discipline when faced with conflicting desires and pressures. Conflicting desires may include the lust of the flesh or fame, which do not glorify God. Pressures may come from peers, family, or society. For example, there may be pressure to prove a point, respond to online trolls, or lash out when offended.

However, through the Holy Spirit, you can choose not to respond negatively. You can remain calm in traffic, avoid yelling when provoked, and maintain discipline in other challenging situations. As the Bible says, "But if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live" (Romans 8:13 KJV). It is only through the Spirit of God that you can subdue and discipline your impulses, desires, and deeds of the flesh.
In addition, devote yourself wholly to God's Word so that your mind will be renewed and strengthened to live according to His will.
prayer: The Holy Spirit enables me to subdue the desires and actions of the flesh. I have dominion over sin and its corrupting influence. Through the Spirit, the old nature is crucified. I will continue to give myself to the Word of God. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 8:12 KJV, 1 Corinthians 9:27 KJV, Colossians 3:5 KJV, 2 Timothy 1:7 ESV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Refuse to Worry
verse: Can all your worries add a single moment to your life?
body: t he word worry comes from the Greek word merimnao, which means to be anxious, concerned, or bothered. Worry often stems from a lack of peace and trust in the Lord. It arises when we try to figure out solutions on our own and doubt the possibility of God's Word coming to pass in our lives (Proverbs 3:5).

Anyone who puts their full trust in the Lord will experience peace. Worry, on the other hand, adds nothing to your life. As Matthew 6:27 reminds us, "Can all your worries add a single moment to your life?"

People worry about many things today, but worrying will never solve problems. Proverbs 23:4 NLT says, "Don't wear yourself out trying to get rich. Be wise enough to know when to quit." This applies not only to riches but to all aspects of life. Worrying will only wear you out.

In engineering, the term "wear" refers to gradual deterioration or damage caused by stress. Similarly, worry can wear you down over time. When you face challenges and begin to feel overwhelmed, be wise and shift your focus from the situation to
God's Word.

Isaiah 26:3 KJV says, "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee." Focus on God's promises, and He will give you peace that replaces worry. You will find the burdens lifted, and the anxiety will fade away.
prayer: I refuse to be anxious about anything. I cast all my cares upon the Lord, for He cares for me. My mind will always stay on the Word of God, and I experience perfect peace. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Psalm 55:22 AMP, 1 Peter 5:7 KJV, Matthew 6:25-34 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Intimacy with God
verse: My soul (my life, my inner self) longs for and greatly desires the courts of the LORD; My heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
body: Intimacy is a deeper form of friendship. It is not a casual or surface-level relationship. God desires us to have an intimate relationship with Him. Have you ever noticed moments during your prayer time when, just as you are about to end, you feel prompted to continue? At such times, do not stop. Continue the fellowship because God is enjoying the connection with you.

Rick Warren once said, "There is nothing, absolutely nothing, more important than developing friendship with God." This highlights the essence of intimacy with God. David understood this deeply. His passion for intimacy with God was his priority. That is why he said in Psalm 84:2 AMP, "My soul (my life, my inner self) longs for and greatly desires the courts of the LORD."

In 1 Samuel 13:14, God called David a man after His own heart. David knew how to please God, and you can become a person after God's own heart too. Develop intimacy with Him, and He will be pleased with you. This deep connection will prompt God to manifest Himself in your life in special ways.

John 14:23 NIV says, "Jesus replied, 'Anyone who loves me will obey my teaching. My Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.'” When you build intimacy with God, He will dwell with you, and your life will reflect His presence.
prayer: Father, thank You, for in You I live, move, and have my being. Strengthen me to know You and the power of Your resurrection. My desire for You will continually grow. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: John 14:21 KJV, Psalm 63:1 KJV, James 4:8 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Don't Be Like a Hypocrite
verse: Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people in order to be seen by them, for then you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
body: The Strong's Concordance defines a hypocrite as an actor under an assumed character, a stage actor. A hypocrite is a person who pretends to possess attributes they do not genuinely have. Such individuals say or do things to gain approval and praise from people, but their intentions are different. Their actions, words, and beliefs contradict what is in their hearts.

In Matthew 23:13-33, you will find Jesus challenging the Pharisees for their hypocrisy. Instead of acknowledging the truth and repenting, they schemed against Jesus, leading to His crucifixion. The Pharisees viewed the law from a legalistic perspective, but Jesus taught them that what matters is the motive of the heart and not outward displays of sanctimonious behavior.

In your walk with the Lord, why do you do the things you do? Why do you pray, fast, give, or practice generosity? Proverbs 16:2 GNT says, "You may think everything you do is right, but the Lord judges your motives." Similarly, Proverbs 30:12 KJV states, "There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes,
and yet is not washed from their filthiness.
As you serve the Lord, always examine your heart to ensure that all you do for Him is out of love, not for selfish purposes or the applause of people.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You for Your word that has come to me today. Help me to serve You with a perfect heart and to worship You in spirit and in truth. Enable me to examine my motives in my dealings with others too. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:2-9 KJV, Matthew 15:7-9 KJV, Romans 12:9 NKJV, 1 John 4:20 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Developing Intimacy with God
verse: Jesus answered, "If anyone (really) loves Me, he will keep My word (teaching), and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our dwelling place with him.
body: From John 14:23 AMPL, we need to pay attention to two key clauses: “My Father will love him” and “make Our dwelling place with him.” John 3:16 reveals to us that God loves us, and 1 Corinthians 6:19 also reveals that God dwells in us. Jesus' statement in our opening verse shows there is a deeper level of love called intimacy and a higher degree of His manifestation in the life of anyone who keeps God's word. This is because there are believers who do not keep God's word, but that does not mean they are not loved by God or that He does not dwell in them.

God wants to fully express Himself and manifest Himself mightily in a believer's life. The only way this can take place is when you develop an intimate relationship with Him, and this begins when you have a strong desire to know God more. This desire will stir you to start seeking God. Anyone who seeks the Lord will find Him (Matthew 7:7).
Seeking the Lord involves anything you do that helps you develop an intimate relationship with Him. Your relationship with

God is as close as you choose it to be. Intimacy is not accidental; it is your personal choice, and you must decide to be intentional about it. Spending quality time studying God's word, praying, fasting, fellowshipping with other believers, and yielding to the Holy Spirit will help you develop intimacy with God. Decide today to seek Him, and He will reveal Himself to you.
prayer: Dear Father, I want to know You intimately. Reveal Yourself to me. Stir up in me an unquenchable hunger for the things that concern You. Guide me to walk in Your preordained pathway for my life. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Philippians 3:10-11 NIV, John 17:3 KJV, Matthew 7:7-8 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Pray for the Unsaved
verse: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
body: In Genesis 19:24, Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed because of their iniquity. The inhabitants of these cities did not know God, and they wallowed in sin. Lot lived there, but he was unable to win them to the Lord. When destruction came, he was affected because he lost his wife, became displaced, and ended up in a cave, losing all his possessions.

God does not want anyone to have the same experience. Rather, He wants us to intercede for the unsaved in our neighborhoods, cities, and nations. Pray for them that they may receive eternal life and “know the only true God, and Jesus Christ” (John 17:3 KJV). God is not willing that any sinner should perish; instead, He wants them to repent (2 Peter 3:9).

Many unbelievers desire to know God and accept Jesus, but the enemy has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts (John 12:40). This is one of the strategies the devil uses to stop them from accepting the truth of the gospel. Without prayer, you can preach to them from morning to night without making an impact. It is in the place of prayer that you table them before God for Him to open their hearts and deliver them from the bondage of the
enemy. Take this time to pray for a family member, friend, or anyone you know who is yet to be saved.
prayer: Dear Father, I thank You for Your love for everyone and Your desire for all to be saved. I pray for the unsaved that they may be loosed from the bondage of Satan. Grant them a new heart so they can receive eternal life and live to serve You all the days of their lives. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: John 8:16-17 KJV, John 6:47 KJV, John 3:36 KJV, John 5:24 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Renewal of Strength
verse: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
body: a man or woman who has not waited upon the Lord does not know (by experience) what divine strength is. Renewal of strength comes from God and not from motivational speeches. While waiting upon the Lord, you will mount up with wings as an eagle. There are different kinds of birds, but an eagle is used here because it is special. It is a high flier and has the ability to soar above the turbulence of the wind.

To wait upon the Lord is to hope and trust in Him.
