It requires your faith, patience, humility, and endurance regardless of what comes your way, and it also requires acting on the Word of God (James 1:22). As you wait on the Lord, you will have to encourage yourself with His Word. Psalm 27:14 says, “Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: Wait, I say, on the LORD.”

When you wait on the Lord, you will receive strength in your finances, body, mind, and spirit, as well as in all aspects of your life. Suddenly, you will have strength to overcome the things that once limited you. Renewal of strength comes with the ability

to withstand and resist the adversary and the pressures of life. In Genesis 49:24, God strengthened Joseph's arms. His arms were made agile against the arrows and pressures of his enemies. He remained strong and did not have to fight back.

If you want to receive strength and fly above your dissatisfaction and troubles, then you must wait upon the Lord. Psalm 18:32 KJV says, “It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.”
prayer: Thank You, Father, for giving me the opportunity to renew my strength through waiting on You. Help me to wait upon You the right way. Equip me with strength, guide me rightly, and enlarge my capacity. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Psalm 18:32 KJV, Psalm 28:7 KJV, Micah 7:7 KJV, Habakkuk 3:19 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: How to Wait upon the Lord
verse: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
body: Do you desire a positive change in your relationship with God, your health, family, ministry, career, or any aspect of your life? If your answer is yes, then the solution is to wait upon the Lord. God knows that a time will come in your life when you will be dissatisfied with your current state and need a change. Your current situation might be discouraging, but Psalm 27:14 KJV says, “Wait on the LORD: be strong, and let thine heart take courage; yea, wait thou on the LORD.”
Many people desire to wait on the Lord, but they are unsure of how to go about it. Here are ways to wait upon the Lord:

Firstly, trust in the Lord. This is the same as having faith in God. God wants you to come to the place where your trust and confidence are in Him. He needs your absolute dependence. Hebrews 11:8-10 TLB tells us that Abraham trusted God.
Secondly, pray and wait. Lamentations 3:25 KJV says, “The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.” Pray and wait. Keep praying and keep waiting
until you see the change you desire.
Thirdly, study the Bible always. Studying the Bible will help you maintain focus, strengthen your faith (Romans 10:17), and become transformed (2 Corinthians 3:18).

Finally, fasting. Fasting positions you to receive from God, and there are some situations that will not change except through fasting. Matthew 17:21 says this clearly. I will teach more about fasting soon.
prayer: My strength is renewed daily as I wait upon the Lord. I develop the ability to fly above the turbulence and pressures of life. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Psalm 130:5 KJV, Psalm 37:7 KJV, Hebrews 11:8-10 TLB
author: Apostle Chuks

title: God is your Provider
verse: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah Jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.
body: Over the years, I have heard people refer to the person who caters to the needs of the family as the breadwinner. That always sounded funny to me because it stems from ignorance. God is your provider. The moment you realize this, your trust will be in God, and He will always provide for you using several means and people.

From Genesis 22:14, we see Abraham use the word Jehovah Jireh, which means “God will provide.” This shows that he trusted God. You too can trust God to provide for you regardless of the pressure, even if it is at the last moment. God is your Father. He is your provider and sustainer, and it is His responsibility to supply all your needs.

Philippians 4:19 AMP says, “And my God will supply (fill until full) your every need according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.” Are you in need of anything today? Simply ask God, and He will be delighted to provide for you and meet your needs. Ephesians 3:20 KJV tells us, “Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us.”
prayer: Thank you, Heavenly Father, for always meeting my needs and granting my desires. Thank you for providing all that I need that pertains to life and godliness. Unto you be glory and praise forever, in Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Isaiah 41:10 KJV, Matthew 6:32 KJV, 2 Corinthians 9:8 KJV, Psalm 23:1 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Use the Name of Jesus to Effect Change
verse: Whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.
body: You can use the name of Jesus to effect the change you desire. Jesus Christ gave us a blank cheque for unlimited withdrawal. The word “whatever” in the opening scripture refers to all things, excluding nothing. Psalm 24:1 says, “The earth is the Lord's and all that dwell therein.” The Lord owns the earth and everything in it, and He is ready to give you all things you request in the name of Jesus, as long as it aligns with His purpose for your life. This is because He will not give you anything that will lead to destruction.

Psalm 2:8 KJV says, “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” God wants you to ask Him for whatever you need. What area of your life do you need a change? Is it your health, marriage, finances, career, or city? Just make your request to God, and He will grant it to you.
John 16:24 KJV says, “Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full.” Are you worrying and complaining? Have you asked the Lord?

Jesus is saying, “Until now, you have asked me nothing.” Go ahead and make your request to God using the name of Jesus. He will grant your requests so that your joy will be full and that He may be glorified.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for giving us the name of Jesus as a key to effect changes and for always being faithful in answering our prayers. Thank you for the joy that is made full whenever we make requests to You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 7:7-8 KJV, James 4:2-3 KJV, John 15:11 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Have you Tried Fasting?
verse: Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.
body: From Matthew 17:21, we find a rule to engage stubborn situations and forces. Fasting is a spiritual exercise and plays a significant role in your walk with God. It invites heavenly interference in earthly matters. You do not necessarily need to fast to have an angelic visitation or interference, but certain difficult situations can only be handled by angels of higher ranks like the archangels. To provoke certain changes, you need to include fasting in your prayers.

In Daniel 10:12-13, the angel sent to deliver answers to Daniel's prayers was intercepted, but because Daniel continued fasting, God had to send Angel Michael to deliver his answers. Angel Michael is a higher rank of angel, an archangel. Daniel was dealing with stubborn forces of darkness. Has your healing or deliverance been delayed for a long time, regardless of your prayers? Try fasting! Add fasting to your prayers and do not stop until you receive your miracle.

“Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.” – Ephesians 6:13 KJV. There is definitely an evil day that awaits every believer. The evil day is when the devil shows up to tempt you. It comes with a lot of opposition and pressures.

The temptation of Jesus by Satan was His evil day, and Jesus withstood and defeated Satan because He fasted (Matthew 4:1-11). Finally, it is better to add fasting to your prayers in order not to meet the evil day unprepared.
prayer: I declare that I am strengthened in my inner man by the Holy Spirit. I will always keep watch and pray. Thank you, Lord, for always causing me to triumph over every temptation and challenge that shows up. I give myself to fasting and prayers always. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Matthew 4:1-11 KJV, James 1:12-16 KJV, Matthew 26:41 KJV, Mark 14:38 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Jesus Healed them All
verse: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with Him.
body: From the above scripture, let us focus on two key phrases: “healing all” and “oppressed by the devil.” The healing described involves the spirit, soul, and body. Sickness is not from God; rather, it is an oppression from the devil.

Some people may fall sick due to complications, mistakes, or carelessness. For example, someone who has been careless with their health and is fond of smoking could develop lung cancer. Additionally, the devil can take advantage of an existing health situation. For instance, a wound that should have healed within a week might linger for months or even years.

On the other hand, some illnesses are caused by a direct affliction from the devil, with no known cause. For example, a person might wake up with ear pain, and even after medical consultations, the pain persists, leading to deafness despite a healthy lifestyle.
Both scenarios are afflictions aimed at disrupting your joy and peace. The enemy comes to kill, steal, and destroy (John 10:10). However, Isaiah 53:5 declares, “By His stripes you are

healed.” I pray for you today: I break the affliction of the devil over your life and command Satan to release you now. I command every sickness to leave you, and I declare you healed in Jesus' name. Amen!
prayer: Thank You, Father, for bearing all my sins and sicknesses so that I may be healed. I affirm that by Your stripes, I am healed. I am free from every sickness and disease. Thank You, Lord, for healing me. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: 1 Peter 2:24 KJV, Isaiah 53:5-6 KJV, Isaiah 54:4-5 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Are Valuable to God
verse: Look at the birds of the air; they do not sow or reap or store away in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?
body: You are of great value in God's eyes. It does not matter what is happening around you right now. In all things, God still values you. You are not worthless. To enjoy the great benefits God has for you, it is important to see yourself differently: see yourself the way God sees you. You are valuable to Him.

1 John 4:10 says, “This is love: not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins.” The punishment for sin is death, but because you are valuable to God, He sent His only Son to die in your place.

Not only did Jesus die for you, but God also filled you with the Holy Spirit. This is the very essence of God Himself (Ephesians 1:13). You are worth the blood of Jesus and the indwelling presence of God's Spirit. After you got saved and were filled with the Holy Spirit, God made you His ambassador (2 Corinthians 5:20). He believes in you and has chosen you to represent Him on earth by giving you the ministry of reconciliation, to win more people to His Kingdom.
Finally, Jesus is coming back for His church, and you are part of His church (1 Corinthians 15:51-52). Rejoice because you are valuable to God.
prayer: Thank You, Father, for loving me with an everlasting love. I am thankful because You value me so much that You sent Jesus to die for me. Thank You for saving me, filling me with Your Spirit, and making me Your ambassador. I will go about telling everyone of Your love for humanity. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:26 KJV, Romans 10:9-10 KJV, 1 Thessalonians 4:15-17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Where is your Heart?
verse: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
body: w here is your treasure? Where are your valuables? And what are your valuables? Storing your valuables in the wrong place has the ability to control your heart and lead it to the wrong place. The things you treasure the most have a way of attaching your heart to them.

Matthew 6:21 NLT says, “Wherever your treasure is, there the desires of your heart will also be.” The things you treasure the most can become like a god to you. Many times, people unknowingly practice idolatry in their hearts. It could be material possessions, your spouse, your job, or self-love. These things become so valuable to you that they take the first place in your heart, instead of God.

Consider how much time people spend on their phones or social media, always curious to check their devices. For some, it becomes the last thing they look at before sleeping and the first thing they check upon waking, even before their morning devotion.
Let your heart focus on things that have eternal value. Colossians 3:2 AMP says, “Set your mind and keep focused

habitually on the things above (the heavenly things), not on things that are on the earth (which have only temporal value).” The earthly things that consume your time and energy are temporary. You will leave them all behind when your time on earth ends.
Set your heart right by seeking the Lord your God (1 Chronicles 22:19).
prayer: Dear Lord, my mind will always be stayed on You. I will meditate on Your Word and do all it says. I set my heart on things above and will not entangle myself with things that are unprofitable to You and Your agenda. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Luke 12:34 KJV, 1 Chronicles 29:3 KJV, Matthew 6:19 KJV, Matthew 6:33 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Expect Persecution
verse: Blessed are you when they revile and persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely for My sake.
body: As a believer in Jesus Christ, you should expect persecution. The persecution is not meant to tear you down because you are never alone. God is with you, even in the midst of the persecution. Rejoice, because the Bible calls you “blessed” when people revile and persecute you for the sake of the kingdom of God and your faith in Him (Matthew 5:11).

Jesus performed diverse kinds of miracles because He had compassion on the people afflicted by the devil. Yet, the Pharisees accused Him of blasphemy, disrespecting religious values, forming friendships with sinners, and using satanic powers to cast out demons (Matthew 9:34). They did not have sufficient evidence against Jesus, but they politically charged Him to death.

In the days to come, there will be an uprising against the body of Christ and those who believe in the name of our God. There will be governmental policies designed to persecute Christians. But I say to you: rejoice and be glad, for blessed are you. Matthew 5:12 says it is an honor to be persecuted for the Lord: “Rejoice
and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven.”

Similarly, Philippians 1:29 KJV reminds us, “For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on Him, but also to suffer for His sake.” You are not only a believer but also called to partake in His sufferings. Do not turn back, do not hide, and do not stop declaring your belief in Jesus.
prayer: My belief in Jesus will always remain firm, even in the midst of persecutions. I am courageous and full of strength as I face diverse trials. I thank You, Lord, because You are with me, and greater is He that is in me than he that is in the world. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Acts 14:22 KJV, James 1:2 NLT, Acts 5:41 KJV, Romans 5:3 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Jesus is Coming Again
verse: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you unto Myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
body: Oour Lord Jesus is coming again. He left us with a message to share with those who have not heard and to remind other believers of His return to take us home. Therefore, let us be watchful and prudent to avoid erring. Ephesians 5:15 KJV says, “See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise.”

1 Peter 1:17 NLT reminds us, “And remember that the heavenly Father to whom you pray has no favorites. He will judge or reward you according to what you do. So you must live in reverent fear of Him during your time here as temporary residents.”

The phrase “temporary residents” refers to sojourners. Sojourners are people who have temporary residence; they do not consider a place their permanent habitation. We should always remember that we are sojourners on earth, and our ultimate destination is Heaven. When we get to Heaven, God will reward us according to how we lived our lives and our works on earth. Therefore, let us walk circumspectly by living according to the Spirit and forsaking all works of
unrighteousness (1 Corinthians 6:9-10).

As you live on this earth, strive to please God above all else. Even as you endeavor to make your family or others happy, remember that pleasing God is what matters most. You will be accountable to Him.
prayer: Thank You, Father, because there is no condemnation for me as I am in Christ Jesus. I submit to You and walk in the Spirit always, not after the flesh. Through Your Spirit, I mortify the desires and deeds of the flesh. I walk circumspectly as I await Your return. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: John 14:28 KJV, 1 Peter 2:11 KJV, 2 Corinthians 6:1-3 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Overcoming Temptation
verse: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him that loved us.
body: Temptations are different from testing. Testing is to prove your faith, while temptations are meant to entice you to disobey God's will. The sources of temptation are the world, the flesh, and the devil. They usually show up with various kinds of pressure. But one thing is certain: God is faithful, and He will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, and He will always provide a way of escape that you may endure it.

Everyone faces temptation at various points in life – even Jesus was tempted, yet He overcame the tempter and his temptations. The devil often tempts us with deceptive schemes, so subtle that we might not even realize what is happening. That is why Proverbs 3:5 says, “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.”

God is the One who strengthens you at all times to overcome the tempter (Satan) and his temptations, for we are overcomers in this world (1 John 5:4). One way to overcome temptation is through prayer: “Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.” (Matthew 6:13) Jesus' prayer reveals the effective way of dealing with temptation. Secondly, rely on the Holy Spirit and
declare God's word to yourself. Declaring God's word strengthens you, and it is one of the ways to resist the devil.

James 4:7 says, “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” No matter the pressures and temptations that come against you, be rest assured and say to yourself, “In all these things, I am more than a conqueror through Jesus Christ.”
prayer: I have been made more than a conqueror in this world. No matter the pressures and enticements of the devil, I will not give in. Greater is He that is in me than the temptations in this world. Thank You, Lord, for You will always deliver me from all temptation, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 10:13 KJV, Matthew 6:13 KJV, James 4:7 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Qualities of True Worship
verse: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.
body: The opening Bible verse teaches us some qualities of true worship during the dialogue between Jesus and the Samaritan woman at the well. Worship must be spiritual. It has to come from your spirit. True worship should not be carnal. Just because the choir sang well, the voices were great, and you felt good does not mean it was done in the spirit. Worship proceeds from your spirit and not from the flesh.

Secondly, worship must be in truth. God's word is the truth. Worship has to be based on the truth revealed about God in the Scriptures. This means you need to understand who God is through the Scriptures to offer Him true worship (John 8:31- 32).

In Matthew 2:11, the Magi worshipped and honored God with their gifts. Worshiping and honoring God for who He is requires your willingness to give Him what is valuable to you, such as your resources and time.
Worship should be heartfelt. Psalm 63:4-5 TPT says, "I will

worship you passionately and with all my heart. My arms will wave to you like banners of praise." Not only should worship be heartfelt, but it also involves lifting holy hands to the Lord (Psalm 141:2), singing, and making melodies with the fruit of your lips (Hebrews 13:15). If you notice, the last few qualities of worship involve your body. That is why you should be intentional about what you do with your body. Romans 12:1 KJV says, "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.”

Finally, let your life be an instrument of worship unto God by doing good works and reflecting Christ in all you do. Matthew 5:16 says, "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven."
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for making me a light that shines brightly to all men, reflecting Your glory through my good works. I will worship You with all my heart, time, and resources. I will live for You and always present my body as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 6:13 KJV, 1 Corinthians 6:20 KJV, Psalm 69:30-31 KJV, Psalm 19:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: A Worry-Free Life
verse: Therefore, I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
body: Someone might ask, "Is it possible to live a worry-free life?" The answer is yes. Jesus instructs us to live without worry. It has never been heard that worrying has any benefits; rather, it is harmful to the spirit, soul, and body.

The effect of worry on the human spirit is fear. Fear makes you lose confidence and trust in God. A person cannot receive anything from God when fear dwells in them. It makes an individual vulnerable to the fiery missiles of the adversary. Ephesians 6:16 NLT says, "In addition to all these, hold up the shield of faith to stop the fiery arrows of the devil.”

Worrying leads to anxiety, and when prolonged, it might result in depression. This affects the neurochemistry of the brain and impacts a person's overall performance. God wants you to be at your best. He never worries about anything, and He made you in His image and likeness (Genesis 1:27). Represent God well by exhibiting His nature in you: a worry-free life.
I understand that there are times when certain pressures might

arise. God knew such days would come, and His solution is found in Philippians 4:6 GNT: "Don't worry about anything, but in all your prayers ask God for what you need, always asking him with a thankful heart." Always take your matters and concerns to God in prayer with thanksgiving, and He will grant your requests.
prayer: I refuse to worry about anything. I cast all my cares upon the Lord, for He cares for me. In all things, I bring my requests and supplications to God, and He daily loads me with great benefits. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Luke 12:22-34 KJV, 1 Peter 5:7 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Persistent in Prayer
verse: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
body: l uke 18:1-8 talks about a widow who repeatedly made requests to a judge for justice after he rejected her during her first attempt. Because of her persistence, the judge agreed to grant her request to avoid being bothered further. Our Lord Jesus recommends such an approach in our prayer life. Be persistent until your request is granted.

Matthew 7:7 says, "Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." To ask means to make a request. If after making a request, the answer is not given to you, then move to the next level, which is to seek. Seeking involves putting in more effort to find or search for what you are looking for. Let's say you prayed and did not receive the answers you desired, then you begin to seek or search the scriptures to know what the Bible says about the subject, pray at night, and so forth.

If you do not find answers after asking and seeking, do not give up. Then, knock. Knocking involves force and intensified effort. You knock by including fasting, increasing your prayer time, sowing seeds, increasing Bible study, and repeating these
activities. These actions increase the force field, and eventually, the closed doors will open. You will have a testimony. Do not give up.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for You always hear me and always want my joy to be full. I am persistent in prayer. I am strengthened in my inner man by Your Spirit to continue making my requests with thanksgiving. My faith is alive in You, and it produces the right results. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Ephesians 6:18 KJV, James 5:16 NLT, Thessalonians 5:17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Blessings of the Lord Make You Rich
verse: The blessing of the LORD, it makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow to it.
body: t he blessing of the Lord is what makes you rich, not your struggles or the so-called hustle. Your life will take an entirely different shape when you understand this truth. True riches come from the Lord. The word "rich" as used in the scripture above means to be prosperous, to have in abundance, and to lack nothing. To be prosperous goes beyond money and material possessions. It is an all-inclusive package that involves having good health, peace of mind, spiritual growth, and financial increase. God wants you to prosper in every area of your life.

One of the ways to recognize the blessing is that it adds no sorrow. It does not come with affliction or regrets. Many have thought that their hard work will make them rich, but that is not true. Hard work is good, but all it can do is make you have money. However, having money alone is not the true definition of riches; it is just one aspect.
Proverbs 10:22 GNT says, "It is the LORD's blessing that makes you wealthy. Hard work can make you no richer." When the blessing of the Lord is upon your life, it causes you to
prosper. Every little effort of yours produces great increase. No wonder many struggle and work so hard, yet their results do not measure up to their efforts.

Deuteronomy 8:18 KJV says, "But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God; for it is He that giveth thee power to get wealth." There is a power and a grace to make wealth, and it comes from God. May God bless you on every side.
prayer: I am the seed of Abraham. I am blessed beyond measure. No curse is permitted to work in my life. I will enjoy Your blessings every day, and there shall be no sorrow in my life. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Deuteronomy 8:17-18 NIV, Proverbs 20:21 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Gate to the Kingdom of Heaven
verse: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no one comes to the Father except through me.
body: J ohn 17:3 NKJV says, "And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent." Indeed, Christ is the way to eternal life. He is the only way to the Father. When someone gets saved, there is a path the person needs to walk in order to spend eternity with God, and it is called the gate to the Kingdom of Heaven.

Matthew 7:13-14 NIV says, "Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it. But small is the gate and narrow the road that leads to life, and only a few find it." Jesus calls the gate that leads to the Kingdom of Heaven narrow. He did not mean that it is difficult to be a Christian, but that the only path that leads to eternal life with God is through Him. There is a requirement for that, and only a few choose to meet it.
To walk through the narrow gate, one has to be saved and begin living according to the ways of the Lord. It may not be popular or easy, but it is the right way. It requires living in holiness and
submission to the Lord.
Psalms 118:20 NKJV says, "This is the gate of the Lord, through which the righteous shall enter." Glory to God for providing us a way to be with Him in eternity.
prayer: Thank You, Father, for the gift of eternal life You have given me. This life makes me exhibit Your nature and character. Through Your Spirit, I will always walk in righteousness and live to please You. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Isaiah 35:8-10 NKJV, Revelation 22:14 KJV, Proverbs 16:25 NIV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Don't Be Deceived
verse: See, I have warned you about this ahead of time.
body: In Matthew 7:15, Jesus warns us about false prophets and teachers. He said, "Beware of false prophets who disguise themselves as harmless sheep but are really vicious wolves." They appear harmless, but their true intention is to destroy the body of Christ.

Jesus warned us about this ahead of time, telling us about the emergence of false prophets and teachers in the last days, and we are now in those days. In Matthew 7:16, Jesus tells us how to identify them and be careful, saying, "By their fruits, you will recognize them." There are key differences between true prophets and teachers and false ones.

Firstly, their source of information is very important. False prophets may sound accurate, but their source is either divination or human wisdom. They rely on carnal interpretations of the scriptures. "For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life" (Jeremiah 28:16, Jeremiah 14:14).
Secondly, consider their motivation. True prophets and teachers are loyal to God above everything else, while false
ones are driven by self-interest, personal gain, and a desire for fame. 1 Kings 22:13-14 shows the difference in motivation.

The focal point of true prophets is Jesus. They want Christ to be glorified, and their words align with God's will. Lamentations 3:37 reminds us that only God's words will be fulfilled. However, the fulfillment of a prophecy does not always mean it is from God.
Finally, discernment is needed in these last days. You must know the scriptures for yourself. Through the Word of God and the Holy Spirit, you can identify falsehood and avoid deception.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You for Your Spirit that leads and guides me. I am full of Your wisdom. I have received an unction from the Holy One, and I know all things. I will never be deceived. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Jeremiah 14:14 KJV, Jeremiah 23:25-32, Jeremiah 6:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Name of the Lord is a Strong Tower
verse: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is safe.
body: The phrase "the name of the LORD" refers to the name of Jesus. The righteous run into it and are safe. This simply means that in Jesus, there is safety. Whoever comes into Christ is safe. Safe from what? Safe from all the evil in this world. To come into Christ is to be born again. The man who is born in Christ has a different experience from the world.

Psalm 91:2-4 KJV says, "I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust. Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence." There is nowhere else that is safe except in Christ Jesus.

Acts 4:12 KJV says, "Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved." There is no other place where you can find safety except in Christ Jesus. That is why Jesus is calling on you today. "Come to me, all of you who are tired from carrying heavy loads, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28 NIV).

Are you tired of carrying the heavy burdens of insecurity, disease, financial difficulties, inflation, natural disasters, and uncertainty about the future? Come to Jesus. His arms are wide open for you. In Him, you will find rest, peace, and safety. If you are not in Christ yet, or if you want to make peace with God, kindly see the back pages of this devotional or reach out to us through the contact information provided. God bless you.
prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, I thank You for the name of Jesus, which is my strong tower. In You, I have peace, joy, love, rest, and safety from evil and the corrupting influences of this world. I will always walk in Your protection and safety. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: 2 Samuel 22:3 KJV, Psalm 91:1-12 KJV, Matthew 1:21 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Day of Reckoning
verse: And that servant, which knew his Lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.
body: The day of reckoning is also known as the judgment day. It is the day when everyone will give an account to God of how they lived their lives on earth. It will be a day of reward for those who lived rightly before the Lord and a day of condemnation for those who rejected Jesus and continued in iniquity.

Sin and iniquity are often used interchangeably to describe lawlessness as defined by God. However, iniquity is a premeditated choice to continue in sin without repentance. There are many who believe that a believer can continue to walk in sin and still be raptured and spend eternity with God. That is false. Any believer who deliberately continues to live in sin without repentance is a worker of iniquity.

Several believers have abused the teaching of grace. Romans 6:1 KJV says, "What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?" The judgment day is coming, and everyone will give an account to God of how they used the grace given to them after being born again. One thing is certain: God

will reward all believers who faithfully served Him, but He will also say, "Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity," to those who continued in sin and those who rejected Christ. They will be sent to the place of weeping and gnashing of teeth (Matthew 7:18-23).
Prepare for that day of reckoning by forsaking every way of life that is displeasing to God.
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank You for saving me. Help me to always live in a way that pleases You. I will stay focused on serving You and living for Your glory. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Luke 19:11-19 KJV, 1 Corinthians 3:12-15 KJV, John 5:28-29 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Price of Following Christ
verse: A scribe approached him and said, 'Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.' Jesus told him,'Foxes have dens, and birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.
body: f rom our opening Bible verse, the phrase "the Son of Man has no place to lay His head" does not necessarily mean that Jesus was poor or homeless. Jesus made that statement to correct the scribe's misunderstanding of what it means to be a follower of Christ. The scribe had the wrong motivation, expecting earthly grandeur and wealth. Jesus was informing him that following Him comes at a cost.

Following Christ is not always easy or comfortable. It usually comes with a price and requires sacrifice. It might cost you friendships, habits, and lifestyle. Although the price is high, the reward is much greater.

When you got saved, Jesus became the Lord of your life. He became your Master, and you are to submit to Him wholeheartedly. Song of Solomon 7:10 ALT says, "I am my lover's, and he claims me as his own." Jesus claims you as His own, and you are to live for Him. Galatians 2:20 ESV says, "I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by
faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.”

There are great benefits in paying the price to follow Christ. You received eternal life when you said the prayer of salvation (Romans 10:9, John 6:47). Salvation is God's gift to you. It includes forgiveness of sins, freedom from sin, divine health, authority over demons, deliverance, victory, protection, prosperity, divine provision, and all spiritual blessings. Those who are saved are entitled to all that comes with salvation.
Above all, you will spend eternity with God and receive a reward for your service to Him.
prayer: I declare that I am fully committed to Jesus. I have made up my mind, and I will not turn back from following Christ. I will joyfully serve the Lord with all my heart at all times.
furtherStudies: Matthew 19:21-22 KJV, Romans 6:4-6 KJV, Luke 9:61-62 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Peace that Emanates from God
verse: This is the message of Good News for the people of Israel, that there is peace with God through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
body: The message of Good News is the gospel of Christ. Romans 1:16 KJV says, "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes." The power of God that leads people to salvation is in the gospel.

When you got saved, you also received justification. This justification brought you peace with God. Romans 5:1 KJV says, "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." Peace with God means being reconciled with Him.

Another peace that emanates from God is the peace of God. This is the inner calmness and tranquility that comes from a personal relationship with Him. The Holy Spirit brings this peace to your heart, and it is beyond human understanding (Philippians 4:6-7).

There is also peace as a sign of God's approval. Due to your relationship with Him, when you feel this peace, it can be a sign that God approves of your actions. No wonder people become restless when they are about to make a wrong decision. Focusing on God's Word and trusting Him will help you experience perfect peace. Isaiah 26:3 NLT says, "You will keep in perfect peace all who trust in you, all whose thoughts are fixed on you.”

Finally, since we have peace with God, we should restore peace between God and others. This is called reconciliation, and God has made us ministers of reconciliation. Preaching the gospel to others is the way to accomplish this (2 Corinthians 5:18).
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You, for I have been justified by faith, and I have peace with You. I refuse to be anxious about anything. As I focus my mind on You, I experience perfect peace. Amen.
furtherStudies: Psalms 29:11 KJV, Romans 15:13 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: God’s Word in your Heart
verse: Your word I have treasured and stored in my heart, that I may not sin against you.
body: In our opening Bible verse, we see that when God's Word is treasured and stored in a person's heart, it enables them to abstain from sin. Psalm 37:31 says, "The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not falter." It matters what dwells in your heart and what you feed your heart with. The moment you begin to ponder on God's Word at all times, it will guide your steps, keep you from erring against Him, and help you make the right choices in your daily life.

Isaiah 59:19 KJV says, "When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the Lord shall lift up a standard against him." God raises a standard, a banner, or an armed resistance against the opposition of the enemy.

The Lord does this in several ways. One way is by stirring up stored scriptures in your heart to counter any situation. For instance, when faced with opposition, the Lord may stir up 1 John 4:4 in your heart, which says, "Greater is He that is in you, than he that is in the world." At that moment, God expects you to proclaim the scripture He has placed in your heart, for that is the banner against such opposition.

God expects you to store up scriptures in your heart through meditation so He can draw from that resource to raise banners for you in times of trouble. That is why Colossians 3:16 says, "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly." Also, God's Word in you provides a firm foundation and resistance against the challenges of life.
prayer: God's Word will not depart from my mouth. I will meditate on God's Word always. My delight is in God's Word, and it guides my path in life. Amen. FURTHER
furtherStudies: Matthew 7:24-27 KJV, Deuteronomy 11:18-20 KJV, Luke 2:19 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Christ is Also a Place
verse: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
body: Christ is the name of the Son of God, and He is also a place. Proverbs 18:10 says, "The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe." The phrase "run to it" indicates a location. This means that the name of the Lord (Christ) is the strong tower that saves all who run to it.

2 Corinthians 5:17 KJV says, "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new." The word "in" expresses someone being enclosed within a place or location. The believer is enclosed in Christ. That is why Colossians 2:3 says, "In whom (Christ) are hid (enclosed) all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge."

Ephesians 2:6 says, "We have been made to sit together in heavenly places in Christ." This position is far above all principalities, power, might, dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world but also in that which is to come (Ephesians 1:21).

In John 14:2-3, Jesus said, "I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you unto myself, that where I am, there ye may be also." Jesus was not referring to heaven when He said, "I go to prepare a place for you." Heaven was already prepared. The place He went to prepare for us is called Christ, our place at the right hand of the Father. This is where we are now because we are saved.
prayer: I am a new creation in Christ Jesus. My life is hidden in Christ and enclosed in God. Therefore, I am shielded from all forms of evil because I am seated with Christ in heavenly places, far above all powers of darkness. Amen.
furtherStudies: Hebrews 12:22-23 KJV, Ephesians 2:10 KJV, Ephesians 2:13 ESV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: True Productivity
verse: That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God.
body: There are times when some people keep moving in circles, thinking they are making progress, without realizing they are returning to where they started. In life, real progress and fruitfulness can only be found in Christ. The more time you spend with God's word and His presence, the more you will experience what true productivity is.

1 Timothy 4:15 KJV says, "Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all." This is not about showing off or publicly displaying your productivity. Rather, it means that when you wholly give yourself to God's word, you will make significant achievements and progress in life.

In your Christian walk, distractions may arise, and you might feel pressured at times, but you must give yourself completely to God's word. That is where you will find inspiration and guidance to navigate your way through. Worries, conflicts, and excessive busyness can keep Christians from studying God's word deeply and growing from it (Matthew 13:22). Being too busy with work or other things can shift priorities, making it
difficult to live a truly productive life.
True productivity is a life that continually produces real value to God and to yourself.
prayer: I am a tree planted by the rivers of water; I bear fruit in every season. I will continually give myself wholly to God's word, and my life bears witness unto God.
furtherStudies: Colossians 1:6-11 KJV, Ephesians 2:10 KJV, John 15:8-16 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: What Kind of Soil Are You?
verse: The seed that fell on good soil represents those who truly hear and understand God's word and produce a harvest of thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times as much as had been planted.
body: The different types of soil where the sower sowed his seed represent the different responses people have to the word of God. When God's word is shared with people, their individual response is based on the readiness of their hearts. The sower is the preacher, the seed is the word, and the soil is the human heart (Matthew 13:18-28).

Some have hardened hearts. A hardened heart causes disobedience to God's word, which leads to unproductivity. That is why Hebrews 3:15 NIV says, "As has just been said: 'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as you did in the rebellion.'" Others have shallow hearts, meaning they are not well-rooted in God's word, and when problems and persecution arise, they fall away easily. Some do not allow the seed of God's word to produce results in their lives because of the worries of life and the lure of wealth. These distractions hinder the productivity of the word.
Matthew 7:24-27 says, "Anyone who listens to my teaching and follows it is wise, like a person who builds a house on solid

rock." Spending more time with God through prayer and meditation on His word will help you develop deep roots. This will make your heart good soil, capable of producing a bountiful harvest (Matthew 13:23).
prayer: Thank you, Father, for your word builds me up, establishes me, and makes me unshakable. The pressures and distractions of this world will not take me away from your presence. Your word will not depart from my mouth, and I will meditate on it always, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 7:24-28 TPT, 2 Timothy 2:19, Joshua 1:8-9 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Share the Good News
verse: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believeth.
body: t he gospel is good news: the glad tidings about Jesus Christ (Mark 1:1). Good news is meant to be proclaimed. When the Lord does something great for you, He expects you to share it with others. Sharing the good news will encourage them in their walk with God and cause others to believe in Jesus.

In Mark 5:19-20, after Jesus healed the madman of Gerasenes, the man became sane and requested to follow Jesus. However, the Lord's response was, "Go home to your family and tell them everything the Lord has done for you and how merciful He has been." The man then went into the towns to proclaim the great things Jesus had done for him. Through his testimony, the Gentiles came to know God, making him the first missionary to the Gentiles.

Sharing the good news of the Lord is testifying of His goodness. Revelation 12:11 KJV says, "And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony." Sharing the good news is one of the ways to retain your miracles. Be
bold to testify about what God has done for you.

Mark 5:27-29 shows that the woman with the issue of blood heard about Jesus, acted on her faith, and received her miracle. She probably heard the good news of what Jesus had done for others. When you share the good news with others, you not only make them believe in God, but you also prepare them for a supernatural experience. The good news, which is the gospel, carries the power of God and has the ability to change lives (Romans 1:16). Go and share the goodness of God with others.
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank you for your grace, mercy, faithfulness, kindness, and goodness in my life. I will not keep quiet anymore. I will go about sharing the good news of your goodness. I thank you for the many lives that will be saved and transformed by the testimony of your goodness. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Mark 16:15-16 KJV, 1 Corinthians 15:1-2 KJV, Acts 1:8 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Can Stop that Storm
verse: For verily I say unto you, that whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea, and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith.
body: Storms are unfavorable situations in life. They are circumstances that pose a threat to you. Storms are obstacles, and if you do not stop them, they might overwhelm you.

Not long ago, I saw a write-up that said, "Some storms are from God." I was dissatisfied with that statement. From the definition of storms, they all have negative attributes and are not good. James 1:17 NIV says, "Every good and perfect gift is from above." Storms are not good. However, what God does is convert storms to work for your good, as seen in Genesis 50:20, "That which the devil intended for evil, God has turned it around for good." At times, He might permit a storm to get your attention, refine you, and make you better, but He is not the initiator.
Since storms represent turbulence and adversity, God wants you to know that you can stop them. A storm could be in your
marriage, health, finances, job, neighborhood, or even your nation.

In Mark 4:37-39, the storm became life-threatening, and the disciples were afraid. But Jesus said unto the sea, "Peace, be still." The wind ceased, and there was a great calm. Jesus rebuked the source of the storm, and it stopped.

God has given you a great tool to stop any challenge you are going through. That tool is the name of Jesus. Use the name of Jesus to stop any unfavorable situation in your life. Command the storm to cease, and it will cease. You will experience peace again.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for the power in the name of Jesus. I decree in the name of Jesus, Satan, take your hands off my life, my home, my family, my health, and everything that concerns me. My life experiences perfect and complete peace. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: READINGBIBLE Mark 4:39 NKJV, James 4:7 KJV, Matthew 17:20 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Are Not Different from your thoughts
verse: For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
body: Matthew 12:35 ESV says, "A good person out of his good treasure brings forth good, and the evil person out of his evil treasure brings forth evil." Thoughts are conceived first before they are eventually expressed through words. Your words reveal what you have in mind and what you are truly made of.

Until you speak, others might not know what is in your heart. Although, sometimes, nonverbal communication such as body language can give others an idea of your thoughts. These reflect who you are and your personality. No wonder some people struggle with bad habits and negative responses such as harsh words and unpleasant behaviors.

When your heart is occupied with negative thoughts, it will produce negative words and actions. An example is when someone says, "Something is eating me up." If such thoughts are not controlled, they can have a corrosive effect on you.
Control your thoughts and regulate what you permit into your heart. As detailed in Proverbs 4:23 GNT, "Be careful how you
think; your life is shaped by your thoughts."

You can begin today by replacing the wrong things in your heart with positive things. Replace negative movies, news, articles, skits, and thoughts with God's word. Whenever negative thoughts try to rise within you, boldly say to yourself, "I have the mind of Christ" (1 Corinthians 2:16). "Therefore, negative thought, I command you to cease from my heart in Jesus' name."
After a while, you will notice your thoughts taking a new shape. You will experience a peaceful and positive life filled with pleasant words and actions.
prayer: I declare that I have the mind of Christ. I think the thoughts of Christ, and my mind is renewed daily. God's word will not depart from my mouth, and I will meditate on it at all times. God's word dwells in me richly, shaping me into the full stature of Christ. Amen.
furtherStudies: Philippians 2:5 KJV, Colossians 3:16 KJV, Romans 12:2 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: He Unveils Mysteries
verse: He answered and said to them, Because it has been given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven...
body: Mysteries are hidden truths that are not unveiled by human intellect but by divine teaching and revelation. Life should not be mysterious to a believer who is filled with the Holy Spirit and knowledgeable in the scriptures. The Holy Spirit is the revealer of secrets. There is no reason for a believer to walk in the dark.

In the New Covenant, the word "mysteries" is usually used in matters of God's redemptive plan and the unfolding of God's kingdom. These are truths that were once hidden but have now been revealed through Christ. "The mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to his saints" (Colossians 1:26-27 ESV).

As a believer, you have an advantage. Always rely on the Holy Spirit whenever you are faced with issues that seem mysterious. The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of wisdom and revelation, and he can grant you deeper understanding and insight concerning any matter (Ephesians 1:17).
Refuse to walk in confusion. Refuse to walk in darkness. Refuse
to live in uncertainty because you have the light of life, who reveals hidden things to you.
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for the anointing of the Spirit in my life. The Holy Spirit guides, teaches, and reveals all hidden truths to me. I have received the light of life; therefore, hidden and dark things are made known to me. Your light shines brightly in all areas of my life, revealing all truth to me. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: John 2:20 KJV, 1 Corinthians 2:12 KJV, Ephesians 1:17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Productive
verse: To those who listen to my teaching, more understanding will be given, and they will have an abundance of knowledge.
body: In Matthew 13:18-23, we find the parable of the sower, who sowed seeds on four different types of soil: the footpath, the rocky soil, the thorns, and the good soil. The first three types of soil had unproductivity as a common denominator. The fertile and productive soil was outstanding because it yielded results.

From the parable, the different kinds of soil represent the different kinds of people who receive the word, while the sower represents the preacher. The seed that fell on the fertile soil was productive because, "The seed that fell on the good soil represents those who truly hear and understand God's word..." (Matthew 13:23 NLT). In line with this parable, the fundamental key to productivity is continuous listening and studying of God's word, which will grant you more understanding and an abundance of knowledge (Matthew 13:12).

From the beginning of the world, God commanded man to be productive (Genesis 1:28). This does not only apply to increasing in material things but also to allowing the word of God to produce its fruits in your life. As evident in John 15:16 KJV, "You have not chosen me, but I have chosen you and
ordained you, that ye should bring forth fruit...”
God has ordained you to be fruitful. Your role is to give attention to God's word, and you will be productive like the fertile soil.
prayer: I declare that I will always be productive and bear fruits unto the glory of God. In all I do, I will continue to grow in the knowledge and understanding of God's word. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: John 15:5 KJV, John 15:8 KJV, Colossians 1:5-6 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Blessings of the Lord Make you Blessed
verse: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and he adds no painful effort to it.
body: To be blessed is to be approved by God. It means to be favored by the Lord. The blessings of the Lord work better for those who truly understand them. True blessings come from God, and they cause others to favor you. Since blessings come from God, those who acknowledge Him in all their ways experience His blessings.

The Brenton Septuagint Translation of Proverbs 10:22 says, "The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous; it enriches him, and grief of heart shall not be added to it." Abraham was a righteous man who acknowledged God. He not only experienced the blessings of God, but he was also a blessed man and became the father of a blessed generation (Genesis 24:1).

A believer is the seed of Abraham. "And through your offspring, all nations on earth will be blessed..." (Genesis 22:18 NIV). Many are blessed but unaware of their blessings, while others repeatedly experience negative situations. That does not mean you are cursed. You must begin and continue acknowledging
God in all your ways and consciously declare: "I AM BLESSED, AND I EXPERIENCE GOD'S BLESSINGS EVERY DAY!”
prayer: I am blessed, and I experience the blessings of God always. Through me, others will be blessed. Everything I have been experiencing that is inconsistent with the blessings of God is terminated now, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Acts 3:25 KJV, Genesis 12:3 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Your Labor for the Lord is Not in Vain
verse: Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
body: Apostle Paul, in 1 Corinthians 15:58, was encouraging the brethren to labor for the Lord. To labor for the Lord means to put in effort, commitment, and hard work to advance God's kingdom. This includes giving your time, ideas, resources, and dedication through evangelism, intercession, volunteering, missions, and other ways of serving in God's work.

Laboring for the Lord can be demanding, but it is meaningful and rewarding. Sometimes, the earthly results may not seem to match the effort put in, but the labor is never in vain. Many years ago, when I started evangelism, I went from door to door and street to street, preaching the gospel and inviting people to church. Most times, I started in the morning and continued until evening. On Sunday mornings, out of the many I invited, only a few would show up. Yet, I did not allow myself to be discouraged.
From 1 Corinthians 15:58, the phrase "always abounding" means to go beyond the minimum and exceed expectations in

our service to the Lord. Instead of growing weary, we should do more for the Lord. Hebrews 6:10 NLT says, "God is not unjust. He will not forget how hard you have worked for him and the love you have shown him..."
As you continue to labor for the Lord, do it passionately, wholeheartedly, and with a perfect heart. There is a great reward waiting for you in heaven (Matthew 5:12).
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank you for making me a co-laborer with You. I thank You because no labor of love for You is in vain. As I continue to strive for the furtherance of the gospel, I will do all with a perfect heart. I remain steadfast and will do more for Your kingdom, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: 2 Corinthians 4:17 KJV, 1 Thessalonians 1:3 KJV, 1 Peter 4:13-14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: He Has Great Plans for You
verse: But more than anything else, put God's work first and do what he wants. Then the other things will be yours as well.
body: God has great plans for you. He wants you to prosper and dwell in peace (Jeremiah 29:11). God's thoughts for you are good, and they will come to fulfillment in Christ Jesus. However, seeking Him is necessary for the manifestation of these great plans. Matthew 6:33 says, "But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you." All of God's plans for you will become a reality when you seek Him first.

You might be wondering, "If God's plans for me are great, then why am I still facing this situation? Why have I not seen those great plans yet?" You will start experiencing them when you seek Him. As detailed in Matthew 7:7 NASB, "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you." Press on to seek Him, and you will find Him. God's love is unlimited. This means His love has no boundaries; it is eternal and unending. "I have loved you with an everlasting love" (Jeremiah 31:3 KJV). His love is everlasting.
2 Peter 1:3 NIV says, "His divine power has given us everything

we need for a godly life through our knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and goodness." God's divine power is not trying to give us everything; rather, it "has given" us everything. God has fulfilled His part, and the responsibility is now yours. If you truly want to experience His plans, you must seek God and His kingdom. As you seek Him, you will discover how to possess all that He has made available for you and fulfill your purpose in Christ.
prayer: I delight myself in the Lord always. I put God first and above all other things. I am blessed with all the good things of life and everything I need to live uprightly. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: 1 Peter 1:2-3 KJV, 3 John 1:2 KJV, Matthew 6:32-33 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Mean So Much to God
verse: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
body: God loves the world because you are in it. He sent His Son to die for you, all because you mean so much to Him. In Genesis 1:27, God created you in His own image and likeness. He crafted you specially, just like Himself. This proves how much you mean to Him.

God has given His angels charge over you to guide and protect you because He values you greatly (Psalm 91:11-12). Not only do His angels watch over you, but He Himself watches over you (Psalm 12:5-8). In all His sovereignty and majesty, He still looks after you because you are His precious child.

In John 16:23, God wants your joy to be full. That is why He listens to you and answers your prayers. He has also promised to take care of you so that you will have no reason to worry about anything (Isaiah 51:12).
Indeed, you mean so much to God. In all that you do, always be conscious of this truth.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for Your great love and provision for me. Thank You for revealing how valuable I am to You. I will always worship You and live for Your glory.
furtherStudies: 1 Peter 5:7 KJV, John 14:14 KJV, Psalm 40:28 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: What Does God Require From You?
verse: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
body: In Hosea 6:6, the word "mercy" is better understood as "love" (dutiful love). This implies love for God and love for mankind. In Luke 10:27, "He answered, 'You must love the LORD with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind; and love your neighbor as yourself.'”

The focus from our opening scripture is this: "I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings." God desires and craves our love. He has an appetite that can only be satisfied by our love for Him. Beyond loving others, He expects us to prove our love for Him through obedience to His Word and His will.

In 1 Samuel 15:22 KJV, "And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams." Obedience is an act of submission to the will of God. It is a recognition of His sovereignty. This shows that you truly honor God.

God is saying to you today that He wants you to honor Him by obeying His Word and following the leading of His Spirit. He desires to guide you on the right path to the glorious destination He has planned for you. You can know God through the scriptures, prayer, and yielding to His promptings. As you do so, He will reveal Himself and the riches of His glory to you. Hallelujah!
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for the inspiration and blessing of Your Word. From today, I yield myself to Your will. I will obey all You want me to do. I am strengthened in my inner man by Your Spirit to delight in doing what pleases You, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: 1 Samuel 15:22-23 KJV, Psalm 40:6-8 KJV, Jeremiah 7:21-23 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Stop Running Away from your Assignment
verse: I was born and for this purpose I have come into the world, to bear witness to the truth...
body: Ephesians 2:10 NIV says, "For we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God has prepared in advance for us to do". Your works are considered "good works" only when they are acceptable to God. Being acceptable means they meet God's specifications, which are based on what He has predestined for you.

In Ephesians 1:11, "In Him we have obtained an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things." Every individual has been predestined by God for a purpose. This purpose is your assignment on earth. Your works will only be classified as good when you begin to fulfill this assignment.

God sent Jonah to the Assyrian city of Nineveh, but Jonah tried to run from his assignment. Nineveh was known as a violent and cruel nation. However, when Jonah chose to fulfill his assignment, God used him to bring about a great revival. The entire city repented and turned to God. Who knows how many people, destinies, cities, and nations will be saved from
darkness when you stop running from your assignment?

In John 18:37 ESV, "You were born to bear witness to the truth." This does not only mean preaching but also reflecting Christ through your life. By doing so, you will testify that Jesus Christ is Lord, and many will be saved from poverty, sin, disease, and affliction because of you.
prayer: I am the light of the world, a city set on a hill that cannot be hidden. I will not be hidden from bearing witness to the Lordship of Jesus. I will fulfill my purpose and ministry in Christ Jesus. Amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 5:14-16 KJV, Isaiah 55:4 KJV, Ephesians 1:11 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Reasons Some Prayer Requests Are Not Answered
verse: Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
body: Mark 11:24 NIV says, "Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.” This is Jesus giving us a blank check to make demands on anything we desire. He also guarantees that we will receive what we ask for. However, this is not the case for everyone, as some people do not consistently receive answers to their prayers. God is not partial or inconsistent, and our experiences do not invalidate the word of God.

There are several reasons for unanswered prayers. First, many ask amiss. Such requests are inconsistent with God's will. God knows that granting such prayers may not benefit you and could even lead to destruction (1 Samuel 8:4-22).

Secondly, there is a time for everything (Ecclesiastes 3:1). In God's calendar, there is an appointed time for Him to manifest what you have been asking for. When that time comes, your answers will appear, and it will be to the glory of God (Exodus 23:29). Often, when there is a delay in receiving answers, God may be teaching you persistence while building patience in you.
God expects you to ask and receive in faith (Matthew 21:22).
Finally, the condition of your heart is crucial. If you harbor unforgiveness, God will not answer you (Mark 11:25).
prayer: Thank You, Father, for You always hear me when I pray. Through the scriptures and Your Spirit, Your will is made known to me. I do not ask amiss. I will always ask in faith and with a pure heart. Amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 7:7 KJV, Matthew 18:19 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Power of Choice
verse: I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.
body: We are free moral agents. The word "free" implies the privilege to enjoy certain rights. The word "moral" refers to right conduct, while "agent" describes someone who exercises the power to make a choice (Genesis 2:17). From our opening scripture, life and death are placed before humans, yet God desires that you choose life. He does not impose it on you, but there will surely be consequences for whatever choice you make.

The choices we make are either acts of obedience or disobedience to God. Through the scriptures, we understand what pleases God and the path He wants us to follow. However, when we choose not to obey Him, it is disobedience.

In Matthew 7:13-30, Jesus highlights examples of the choices we need to make: the narrow gate or the broad road, the good tree or the bad tree, true or false discipleship, and the firm or weak foundation. The choice is yours to make.
Before making any choice, always remember that your decisions will determine your destiny and destination.
prayer: Dear Lord, guide me on the path of life that You have destined for me. Continue to lead me to make the right choices that will bring glory to Your name. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Genesis 3:1-6 KJV, Deuteronomy 4:1 KJV, Deuteronomy 30:15-16 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Have Authority Over Demons
verse: Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
body: God has given every believer authority over demons. You should not allow demons to take control of your life. They come to steal, kill, and destroy (John 10:10), but by default, the new creation is above demons, and their activities should not harm you.

You are seated with Christ at the right hand of God, far above all principality, power, might, dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world but also in that which is to come (Ephesians 1:21 KJV). This is your identity in Christ. Today, you can put an end to Satan's oppression in your life.

God has given us a special tool to enforce dominion over the works of the devil, and that tool is the name of Jesus. When you use the name of Jesus, no devil or power can resist it. Philippians 2:10 KJV says, "That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth.”
Exercise your authority by commanding the devil to take his hands off your faith and life in the name of Jesus. God bless you.
prayer: Thank You, Father, for the authority You have given me to use the name of Jesus. Thank You because I am seated with Christ, far above all principality, power, might, dominion, and every name that is named. I declare that I am immune to every work of the devil, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 28:18 KJV, Ephesians 1:20-22 NKJV, Philippians 2:10 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Identified with Christ
verse: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of Man be ashamed, when He shall come in His own glory.
body: J esus, in Luke 9:26 KJV, was speaking about being identified with Him. Some people, although saved, do not want to be associated with Jesus or His words. They hesitate to speak boldly for God, even at their workplace, for fear of losing friends. Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea secretly followed Jesus because they did not want the Jews to see them with Him, except for their support during His burial.

Many believers today cannot even quote scriptures during conversations because they feel it is old-fashioned. The phrase "if anyone is ashamed of me and my words" in Luke 9:26 highlights the importance of living boldly for Christ and not being ashamed of God and His words, regardless of persecution and societal pressure.

It is essential to prioritize your relationship with God over worldly acceptance. Apostle Paul, who once disliked and persecuted early Christians, came to realize this truth and became bold for Christ, no matter the cost. Romans 1:16 KJV says, "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God unto salvation for everyone who believes.”
Make up your mind to stand for Christ against all odds, like Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. It is an honorable thing to be identified with the King of the universe.
prayer: Thank You, Father, for the privilege to serve You and to be called Your own. I thank You, Lord, for in You I live, in You I move, and in You I have my being. I will not be ashamed to be identified with You, and I will boldly declare Your name and word to everyone around me, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Hebrews 2:11 KJV, 1 Peter 4:16 NIV, 2 Corinthians 12:10 KJV, John 15:18-21 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Walking in Dominion
verse: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
body: All victories over Satan and his agents are obtained through the power derived from Jesus Christ. Colossians 2:15 NIV says, "And having disarmed the powers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross." Jesus defeated Satan and his cohorts, and every believer in Christ benefits from these victories.
In Luke 10:19, we have the authority to exercise dominion over the enemy. However, many believers are still affected by the devil today. To walk in dominion, here are a few things you should do:

1. Pray: Make your request and use the name of Jesus to resist the devil from interfering in your life. Philippians 2:10 NIV says, "That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth." 2. Act in faith: Do not allow fear to grip you. Maintain your composure and trust in what God's word says concerning that situation. Mark 9:23 NIV says, "Everything is possible for one who believes." 3. Do not be ignorant: The enemy will always test how much of God's word you know. Jesus was able to overcome Satan's temptation because He knew the Scriptures. Colossians 3:16 KJV says, "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly." Also, Daniel 11:32 KJV says, "But they that know their God shall be strong and do exploits." The word "exploits" refers to walking in dominion. Know God's word for yourself. 4. Walk in obedience: The devil is the accuser of the brethren. He knows when you do not comply with God's words and instructions. You cannot expect to walk in dominion when you live in immorality and sin. Romans 6:16 KJV says, "Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?" Purge yourself of all ungodliness, and you will experience a great manifestation of dominion in your life.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for giving me the authority in Your name. I will continue to exercise dominion and ensure Your purpose is accomplished in my world. In the name of Jesus, I will always bring every negative situation and all things to the obedience of Christ. Amen!
furtherStudies: Hosea 4:6 KJV, Luke 17:6 KJV, 1 John 3:4-8 ESV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Lord Reigns
verse: The Lord reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad.
body: The Lord reigns” is a recurring phrase in the Bible, especially in the book of Psalm. It emphasizes the sovereignty of God Almighty over all creation. It reveals God's ultimate authority and control over the universe. "The Lord is king! He is robed in majesty. Indeed, the Lord is robed in majesty and armed with strength. The world stands firm and cannot be shaken" (Psalm 93:1 NLT).

God's authority is in no way comparable to that of earthly rulers. Someone might ask, “The Lord reigns, but what has that got to do with me?” The answer is, it has a lot to do with you. Start by allowing the Lord to reign in your life. The word “Lord” means master. God is your Maker and your Master. You allow Him to reign in your life by acknowledging Him for who He is and accepting His Lordship. This is done in two stages: by believing and by declaring that Jesus is Lord.

Romans 10:9 AMP says, "Because if you acknowledge and confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord (recognizing His power, authority, and majesty as God), and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved." As your

Lord and Maker, you are subject to Him. God made you for His glory (Revelation 4:11). Permit His Lordship to extend into every area of your life by allowing Him to be glorified in your thoughts, words, and actions.

You may ask, “How can I allow God to be Lord over my thoughts?” This is simple. Ensure that you do not permit thoughts that are unpleasant to God to run through your mind. Philippians 4:8 gives us the guide. Whenever ungodly thoughts show up, declare to yourself, "I have the mind of Christ."
You can apply this same principle to regulate your words and actions. By doing this, you are allowing Him to reign over your life.
prayer: Heavenly Father, I thank You for Your word that has been sown in my heart today. You are indeed the Lord of my life and over all that concerns me. You made me for Your pleasure, and I will live to please You always. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Isaiah 40:28 KJV, Romans 11:36 KJV, Acts 17:24-25 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Declare the Lord’s Favor
verse: May the favor of the Lord our God rest on us; establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands.
body: The King James Version renders the above verse as: “And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us…” This scripture is a prayer for God's favor and blessing. The favor of the Lord is closely linked to His presence and approval. From the same verse, “establish the work of our hands for us” is a request for God to grant permanence and success in one's life.

As we see, the phrase “establish the work of our hands” was repeated. This shows that without God's intervention, human effort is limited and cannot achieve lasting success. Do not rely on your intelligence, wealth, or connections. All these amount to nothing without the favor of God. Even King Solomon, the wisest and richest king with all his influence and connections, acknowledged his dependence on God. Proverbs 3:5 says, “Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.”
Have you tried all you could and it didn't amount to anything? Are you at a crossroad in life where it seems you don't know

what to do next? Has all you tried failed and everyone given up on you? Jesus is the only one worthy of your trust. Simply declare the Lord's favor upon yourself: “May the favor of the LORD my God rest upon me and establish the work of my hands” in Jesus' name.
Today, I pray for you specially. May the hand of God be mighty upon your life. May His face shine upon you. May He be gracious to you. May the Lord establish and settle you, in Jesus' name, amen.
prayer: I declare the Lord favors me. I have been accepted by God. The Lord establishes me. The Lord promotes me. The Lord enlarges my coast. The glory of the Lord is upon me. The Lord makes my life beautiful at all times. My trust is always in God. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Psalm 119:135 KJV, Psalm 80:3 KJV, Isaiah 61:7 NIV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Persistent in Prayer
verse: For many are called, but few are chosen.
