body: This is a general invitation to salvation extended to all humanity. Ephesians 2:10 NIV says, “For we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.” God had a plan for you before you were born. This plan is His purpose for your life, and it can only be accomplished in His own way and in Christ Jesus.

God knows that you cannot fulfil His plans for you without Christ Jesus. And now, He has given you Christ so you can be saved and do all that He planned for you to do. This is known as Christian service.

From Matthew 22:14 KJV, there is a distinction between being called and being chosen. Being called is a general call for salvation, and it is vital that you recognize this call and respond to it. Being chosen implies that God selected you for a specific ministerial role. This is also referred to as ministerial calling or the fivefold ministry, as we see in Ephesians 4:11-12 KJV: “And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the
edifying of the body of Christ.”

The chosen are elected by God to equip the called in order to help them discover and fulfil their purpose in Christ and for Christian service. Being chosen by God is not about favoritism. Rather, God expects you to answer this call with faith, obedience, and faithfulness.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for your precious gift of salvation. I thank you for calling me with a holy calling by your purpose and grace. I will always set my focus on you as you guide me in your preordained pathway, in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Ephesians 4:1-2 KJV, 2 Peter 1:10 KJV, 1 Corinthians 1:29 KJV, 1 Corinthians 12:28-29 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Learn to Serve
verse: The greatest among you will be your servant.
body: J ohn 13:14-15 KJV says, “If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.”

The word example in the context of this scripture is from the Greek word hypodeigma, which means a model or pattern to be followed. Jesus shows us a model of leadership that involves serving others. He was humble and selfless.

In the Christian context, leadership is servant leadership. Jesus served His disciples, and this is worthy of emulation. 1 John 3:16 NKJV says, “By this we know love, because He laid down His life for us. And we also ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.” You lay your life down for others by serving them. This comes from sacrificial love and humility.

There are great rewards for serving others, and also for rendering services to God. 1 Peter 4:10 NIV says, “As good servant managers of God's grace in its various forms, serve one another with the gift each of you has received.” Whenever you
serve others and God, do so with a faithful heart. Do it willingly and in any capacity you can, as though you are working for God and not for man (Colossians 3:23).
Finally, do not always wait for others to serve you. Rather, take up responsibilities that will benefit others. Look out for ways you can be useful in your local assembly, family, and community.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for such a privilege we have to serve. Give me a humble heart and the right motive to always serve you and others. Help me, Lord, to always serve with joy. I thank you for the great reward that awaits me in Heaven, in Jesus' name.
furtherStudies: Ephesians 6:7 KJV, Matthew 25:21 KJV, Proverbs 19:17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: God’s Word is Forever Sure
verse: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
body: Our opening verse emphasizes the temporary nature of all creation, but God's word remains unchanging and eternal. God values His word even above His name. Psalm 138:2 KJV says, “For thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.”

2 Corinthians 1:20 KJV says, “For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.” This shows God's faithfulness and unchanging nature. You can hold on to His word. He is faithful to the end and able to do all He has promised you. No matter the pressure you face, do not lose faith in His word. Even if everything else fails, His word is forever sure.

Romans 4:20 KJV tells us, “He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God.” Abraham's confidence was in God's word, and it came from God's word. You too can put your confidence in God's word. This confidence is called faith. As your faith in God's word
remains firm, His word will prevail over whatever situation you may face. God's word is truly reliable. Trust it and make it the foundation of your life.

Lord, I live by your word and I will remain steadfast in faith. As I hear and study your word, my faith is strengthened. I will not be shaken by contrary situations, and I thank you because your word prevails in my life, in Jesus' name. Amen.
prayer: Lord, I live by your word and I will remain steadfast in faith. As I hear and study your word, my faith is strengthened. I will not be shaken by contrary situations, and I thank you because your word prevails in my life, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Luke 12:45 KJV, Hebrews 10:23 KJV, Psalm 119:89 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Hospitality is an Art
verse: Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it.
body: Hospitality literally means to love strangers, and to generously care for guests or those you do not know. In Jesus' teaching in the gospel of Luke 10:25-37, He instructs us to love our neighbours. Leviticus 19:34 also emphasizes the importance of caring for foreigners and the marginalized.

Romans 13:8 KJV says, “Owe no man anything, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” You are called to love not only family and friends, but strangers as well. This act of loving strangers is what is called hospitality. It is an art. You must be skillful about it, and it involves knowing the best way to care for people. A hungry stranger needs food. Offering such a person a ride is not the help they need. Providing a meal and refreshment is the appropriate response. That is how hospitality works; you meet the need with care and wisdom.

Hospitality is seen throughout the Bible. God provided manna for the Israelites in the wilderness. Abraham cared for strangers. The Shunammite woman offered food and shelter to Elisha. Jesus fed the multitude.

Do you show hospitality to guests? And what kind of hospitality do you offer them? Jesus once visited the home of Mary and Martha. Mary gave Jesus the attention He needed, while Martha was more concerned about cooking. Though both made efforts to receive Jesus, what He needed at that moment was their attention.
Today, Jesus still longs for hospitality from you. Give Him the attention He deserves by listening to His word and worshipping Him.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for your love that is shed abroad in my heart by your Spirit. It moves me to love and care for others. I will be consistent and skillful in hospitality to others, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Peter 4:9 KJV, Luke 14:12-14 KJV, Genesis 18:1-15 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Test in the crucible of Adversity
verse: Peter said to Him, “Even if I have to die with You, I will not deny You!” And so said all the disciples”.
body: Peter's strong declaration of loyalty, where he insisted that he would never abandon Jesus, stands in sharp contrast to his eventual denial. This fulfilled Jesus' prophecy in Matthew 26:34. When Peter faced opposition, he denied Jesus. Not only Peter, but all the disciples scattered in fear, despite their earlier declarations that they would rather die than deny Him.

It is easy to declare that you are a Christian, but when challenges arise, will you be able to maintain your declaration and stand firm in faith? Will you stay strong in Jesus? Will your faith remain steady when tested in the crucible of adversity? Is your faith strong enough to remain firm under the trials of life and persecution?

Romans 8:37 KJV says, “Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.” In the face of opposition, do not stagger at God's promises concerning you. Rather, be strong in faith like Abraham. Anchor your faith in God and in His word. When you do, you will stand strong and emerge
victorious.

Adversities and challenges are tests of life and they help to develop your character. Do not be discouraged by them. James 1:2-3 says, “Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.”
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for my light afflictions which are temporary. They are producing for me a glory that far outweighs them. I thank you because I have the victory. I remain strong in faith and my faith prevails, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 10:13 ESV, Psalm 34:19 KJV, Isaiah 41:10 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Response to the Distress of the Soul
verse: And I am in deep distress. How long will it be?
body: Psalm 31:9 KJV says “Have mercy upon me, O LORD, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly”. David, in this psalm, was in great distress. This was a state of severe unrest. The psalmist acknowledged the human condition and the need for God's intervention.

From David's prayer and language (“mine eye,” “my soul,” and “my belly”), we can see that the distress he experienced was total. It affected every part of his being. The soul represents the inner self or life force, while the body represents the physical aspect. His words show that the impact of the distress was not just spiritual or emotional, but physical as well.

In Matthew 26:38 KJV, “Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me,” Jesus expressed a similar emotional distress. It was a deep turmoil of the soul, just like David's experience. Have you ever felt such unease, distress, or trouble in your soul, where you could not even figure out what it was?

Jesus gave us the answer in Matthew 26:38-39: “tarry ye here and watch...” Whenever you experience such distress, go and pray. Be spiritually alert and vigilant. That burden could be a spiritual weight that needs immediate attention. Praying immediately could avert a danger or bring peace to the situation. Do not stop until the burden lifts.
prayer: I am spiritually sensitive. I am fervent in prayer. Whenever I pray, things get settled in sensitive quarters in the realm of the spirit. I thank You, Lord, for Your Spirit helps us by making intercession whenever the need arises. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: James 5:16 KJV, Ephesians 6:18 KJV, 1 Thessalonians 5:17-19 KJV, Romans 8:26-28 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You are Acceptable to God
verse: Therefore, if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new”.
body: It is important to know how God sees you. The way God sees you is your true identity. The scripture shows us what was in God's mind when He formed and fashioned you for His glory and purpose. Many people suffer from low self- esteem, depression, and a sense of rejection because they lack knowledge of who they are in Christ (Hosea 4:6).

2 Corinthians 5:17 AMP says, “Therefore if anyone is in Christ [that is, grafted in, joined to Him by faith in Him as Savior], he is a new creature [reborn and renewed by the Holy Spirit]; the old things [the previous moral and spiritual condition] have passed away. Behold, new things have come [because spiritual awakening brings a new life].”

The moment you said the prayer of salvation, you became a brand new person. God sees you as new. Sometimes, the devil may try to bring back thoughts of your past in order to make you feel guilty over things that the blood of Jesus has already washed away. The devil is the accuser of God's people (Revelation 12:10). He goes about projecting thoughts of guilt,
fear, condemnation, and rejection.

Romans 8:1 AMP says, “Therefore there is now no condemnation [no guilty verdict, no punishment] for those who are in Christ Jesus [who believe in Him as personal Lord and Savior].” Condemnation and rejection are now over. You are now acceptable to God. Similarly, Romans 5:17 KJV says, “Much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” As a believer, you have received the gift of righteousness from God. By this gift, you are acceptable to Him.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You for Your grace and my acceptance in Christ. Thank You for choosing me and for making me a royal priesthood. I thank You because the old is passed and the new has come. I walk in the newness of life to the glory of Your name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 8:1-2 KJV, John 3:18 KJV, Galatians 5:16-18 KJV, Ephesians 1:6 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Keep Watch and Pray
verse: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak”.
body: The phrase watch and pray emphasizes the importance of being vigilant and prayerful as a believer. This is a command to remain spiritually alert and awake. The combination of watching and praying forms a defense system against the strategies and traps of the enemy (Psalm 59:3).

When you watch and pray, you will receive strength and grace to help you resist temptation. This is the grace to overcome the tests and trials of life. God wants you to stand firm against the evil day (Ephesians 6:13).

Watching and praying will strengthen your faith so that you do not fail in the day of adversity. Myles Munroe described prayer as man giving God permission to interfere in the affairs of the earth. By watching and praying, you are giving God the access and permission to intervene in your life.

In Matthew 26:41, you will notice that Jesus called and prompted His disciples to watch and pray the first, second, and third time. Yet they still could not keep watch, and then the enemy struck. One thing is certain: if the disciples had listened
to Jesus and remained vigilant and prayerful, they would have withstood and overcome the devil. They would not have scattered after Jesus was arrested, and Peter would not have denied Jesus.
Today, God keeps calling your attention to pray and remain alert. But when you keep ignoring the call to prayer, the enemy eventually strikes. Be vigilant and pray.
prayer: Thank You Lord for always answering me when I pray. I thank You for the divine promptings of Your Spirit. As I pray, I am being strengthened in my spirit to withstand and overcome the snares of the enemy. I will always devote myself to prayer and be watchful and thankful. In Jesus name, amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Peter 5:8 KJV, Ephesians 6:18 KJV, Romans 8:26 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Firm Trust in God
verse: ...Yet I want your will to be done, not mine...
body: Our opening scripture is the ultimate expression of submission to the will of the Father. It also points out that believers should have firm trust in God's plan, regardless of how they feel. It takes prayer and obedience to have firm trust in the Lord.

When you have firm trust in God's plan, you will not be moved when you face diverse troubles. Isaiah 43:2 KJV says, “When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.” Here, God assures you of His commitment to be with you. The Bible never said troubles will not rise against you, but God assures you of His presence and expects you to trust Him.

When you go through challenging moments, you should know for sure that all the things you are faced with will work together for your good. Romans 8:28 KJV says, “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to His purpose.” God has said that all things will work for your good, and that settles it. Even if the
pressure increases, tell yourself, “In all these things I am facing, I am more than a conqueror, for God is with me. This condition is temporary. I am coming out of this with testimonies.”

Job 13:15 KJV says, “Though He slay me, yet will I trust in Him: but I will maintain mine own ways before Him.” Job was expressing his trust in God, even in the face of suffering and possible death. Remain strong and unshaken in your trust in God, and everything will work for your good. He will not leave you nor forsake you.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You for Your love and providence towards me. You are too faithful and ever merciful. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil and I shall not be perturbed, for You are with me. I will always trust You. Amen. FURTHER
furtherStudies: Daniel 3:17-18 KJV, Isaiah 12:2 KJV, Romans 8:35-39 KJV, Habakkuk 3: 17-18 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Make Right Decisions
verse: ...that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.
body: Choices are not merely about physical life and death. They also encompass spiritual and eternal effects. It is important to consider our choices before making a decision, because each one might lead to life or death.

Do not be compelled to make the wrong decisions, regardless of the pressure you may face. This is especially true for those in leadership or positions of authority, because the effects of their decisions can either build or destroy lives.

Matthew 27:24 KJV says, “When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.” Pilate knew Jesus was innocent, but the Jews threatened to accuse him of rebelling against Caesar (John 19:12). Even though he washed his hands, he was still guilty. That act alone was not enough. He should have stood his ground to ensure Jesus was exonerated. Do not make excuses. Be responsible for your decisions.

Herod beheaded John the Baptist because of Herodias' influence, even though he knew it was wrong (Mark 6:14-29). King Ahab accepted his wife's schemes, Jezebel's manipulation, to murder Naboth and take his property (1 Kings 21). Many others in authority failed to oppose injustice and to stand for what was right. Make up your mind to be bold enough to make the right decisions, no matter what happens.
prayer: Father, I thank You for strengthening my faith through Your word. You give me wisdom, and I will always make the right decisions. I will stand for the truth and for justice. I will defend and speak for the voiceless in my society, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Daniel 3:16-28 KJV, 2 Samuel 11:14-26 KJV, Esther 3:5-15 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: how to Receive God’s Word
verse: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.
body: J ohn 6:63 KJV says, “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” God's word is not merely informative or directional. It carries power and life. If anyone receives His word, it begins a work in their life and produces the result of what it speaks.

The word of God is living and active (Hebrews 4:12). It is not static. It is powerful and dynamic. God's word has a catalytic effect on anyone who receives it rightly. “Such as hear the word and receive it,” as seen in our opening verse, refers to those who hear the word with their hearts and receive it with faith. Not those who analyse it with mere sense knowledge. That kind of analysis creates doubt and stands in the way of faith. Receive God's word with your whole heart like a child (Matthew 18:3), and position yourself to receive more.

As you hear God's word, your faith grows and helps you to receive even more. Faith is a vital element that makes the word of God produce what it says. “For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not
profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it” (Hebrews 4:2 KJV).
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You for the power in Your word. I thank You because Your word is alive and active, always working in me. It brings life, shapes me, and guides me. My heart is always open to receive Your word with faith, in Jesus name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Psalm 19:7-8 KJV, 1 Thessalonians 2:13 KJV, 2 Timothy 3:16-17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: how to Retain your Miracle
verse: Jesus asked, Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine? Has no one returned to give praise to God except this foreigner? Then he said to him, Rise and go, your faith has made you well.
body: The story of Jesus healing ten lepers, and only one returning to thank Him, highlights the importance of thanksgiving. Jesus' response to the one who returned was unique. He made him well. Being made well means a state of restoration and perfection. It is one thing to receive a miracle, it is another to retain and walk in the fullness of it.

For example, imagine a blind man who begins to see partially during a church service. That is already a miracle. He should not stay quiet. He should rejoice and boldly come out to share his testimony. This glorifies God and can lead to the perfection of that miracle, bringing full restoration to his sight. Also, by testifying, he secures and retains his miracle.

In Mark 5:8-20, Jesus healed the mad man of Gadarenes and then told him to go home and tell everyone what the Lord had done for him and how merciful God had been. The man obeyed and began to tell people about Jesus. When God saves or heals you, He wants you to share your testimony so that others can believe and be saved too.

Finally, when God heals you or gives you a miracle, He expects you to have a change of heart. You should begin to serve Him, grow in your commitment, and not return to your old ways of life or sin. This is how to retain your miracle and walk in its fullness.
prayer: I declare that I am a doer of the word of God. I hear God's word and I do all it says. Lord, I thank You for all You have done for me. I will go about telling others of Your goodness, Your mercy, and saving power, in Jesus name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Matthew 12:43-45 KJV, Hebrews 6:4-6 KJV, John 5:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: obedience is Better than Sacrifice
verse: ...Obedience is better than sacrifice, and submission is better than offering the fat of rams.
body: t here are situations where people knowingly disobey God for one reason or the other, and then later return to sow seeds. One common example is what some describe as “robbing Peter to give Paul”. That is, someone steals or engages in wrongdoing just to give to the house of God. Such acts are not obedience but disobedience followed by sacrifice, and they are not accepted by God. These kinds of offerings do not show love for God.

Obedience is an act of submission to God's will and purpose. When you obey, you are yielding to a higher authority. To submit to God means to honour Him. Your obedience is proof that you love Him. It comes from the heart, and God desires those who worship Him with sincerity and not mere show. He seeks worshippers who obey from the heart, not those who only offer outward sacrifices like the Pharisees, whom Jesus called hypocrites.
Your sacrifice will only be acceptable to God if your obedience has already been tested and proven. Cain's offering was

rejected by God because of his disobedience. He did not bring the right kind of offering as instructed (see Genesis 4:1-7). Disobedience is simply refusing to do what God says, and Samuel compared it to idolatry in 1 Samuel 15:23. Idolatry means allowing something or someone to take the place of God in your heart. It is also linked to seeking help from evil spirits. That may sound extreme, but it does not change the truth of scripture. Satan, the father of rebellion, was the first to disobey God. Anyone who follows his path is counted among the disobedient (Ephesians 5:6-7 KJV, Colossians 3:6 KJV).
As a child of God, maintain your true identity by being obedient to His word. Obedience honours God and keeps you in His will.
prayer: I am a child of God and I have the nature of God in me. Flesh and self-will will not rule over me. Nothing will ever take the place of God in my life. I am an obedient child of God. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Psalms 51:16-19 KJV, Jeremiah 7:21-23 KJV, 1 Samuel 15:22-23 NIV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: the Lord Needs Your Attention
verse: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out and departed into a solitary place, and there he prayed
body: Do not get too busy doing the work of the Lord that you no longer have time for the Lord of the work. This popular quote reminds us of the need to balance our Christian service with our personal relationship with God. Your Christian service includes all your commitments and acts of service to God, while your relationship with Him is about making time to truly be with the Lord.

Many times, believers get caught up in being active in service and committed to ministry work, yet they begin to neglect the quiet time they should spend in fellowship with God. But God longs for fellowship with you. He needs your attention. Even though your labour in the Lord is not in vain (1 Corinthians 15:58), the Lord who owns the work desires much more from you than just service.

When you give God your attention, you become more effective in your work for Him. From Mark 1:35, we learn how Jesus Himself gave special attention to God. We can easily get so involved in ministry that we begin to neglect prayer, worship,
Bible study, and quiet time. If this continues, you will burn out. Your strength is renewed in the place of fellowship.

Giving God the attention He needs is essential if you want to be effective in Christian living and ministry. To achieve this, you must rearrange your daily schedule to include time for God. Create a specific time for Him, remove distractions, and spend quality time in fellowship. Study the Bible and meditate on His word.
prayer: Dear Lord, thank you for your faithfulness in calling me into fellowship with Jesus Christ. I declare that I will prioritise you above everything else. Daily, as I study your word, I will continue to grow stronger and stronger in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: READINGBIBLE Psalm 31:20 KJV, Luke 5:16 KJV, Matthew 6:6, 1 Corinthians 1:9 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Overcoming Temptations
verse: After the devil had finished tempting Jesus in every possible way, the devil left him until another time
body: After the baptism of Jesus, He was led into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. The tempter, being the devil, tried Jesus in three major areas, and all the temptations we face also fall into these three categories: the lust of the eyes, the pride of life, and the lust of the flesh. 1 Samuel 2:9 KJV says, “…for by strength shall no man prevail.” This simply means human wisdom and strength are not enough to confront the tempter. Human strategies are limited.

Matthew 6:13 KJV says, “And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.” Jesus was showing us the importance of depending on divine guidance and strength. Trust in the Lord with all your heart and not in your own understanding (Proverbs 3:5). When Adam and Eve were tempted in the garden of Eden, they failed. But Jesus, being the second Adam, was also tempted and He overcame.

Adam ate freely from everything in the garden, and perhaps because fasting was not part of his life, he lacked spiritual strength and revelation. Jesus, however, fasted and prayed, and was well positioned when the devil came to tempt Him.
Fasting and prayer are vital resources that will quicken your spirit, discipline your flesh, and prepare you for the day of trial.

1 Peter 5:8 KJV says, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” The enemy is always searching for vulnerable people to tempt and attack. Make fasting and prayer a consistent part of your life, as they will help you overcome temptation.
prayer: I declare that I will always watch and pray. I will not be vulnerable to the strategies and attacks of the enemy. I am strengthened by Your Spirit and as I resist the devil, he flees from me. Lord, continue to lead me not into temptation and deliver me from all evil, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 10:13 NLT, James 1:13-14 KJV, 2 Peter 2:9 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: understanding Spiritual warfare (1)
verse: For though we walk in the flesh as mortal men, we are not carrying on spiritual warfare according to the flesh and using the weapons of man
body: Although we are in a physical body and living in a three- dimensional world, the battles we face on earth are not to be fought with physical weapons or human strategies. Attempting to fight spiritual battles with human effort leads to futility.

Understanding spiritual warfare begins with acknowledging the existence of spiritual battles and equipping yourself with the necessary armour to resist the forces of darkness and live a victorious life in Christ. These essential armours are referred to as the whole armour of God. You need to put on all the armour without leaving any part out. This is what gives you full protection against the weapons the enemy may use against you.
Ephesians 6:10-18 outlines these armours:

· The belt of truth: This means grounding yourself in the truth of God's word. · The breastplate of righteousness: This represents living a holy life, as it protects your heart and soul. · The gospel of peace: This refers to the readiness of a believer to share the good news of salvation. It helps you stand firm in spiritual warfare. · The shield of faith: Your faith is used to quench the flaming arrows the enemy throws at you. It is a symbol of your trust in God. · The helmet of salvation: Just as a helmet protects the head, the helmet of salvation protects your mind from anything the enemy may throw at you. It gives you assurance of your salvation. · The sword of the Spirit: This is the word of God. With God's word, you cut off anything projected by the enemy. KJV, "You have not chosen me, but I have chosen you and ordained you, that ye should bring forth fruit...”
All these armours work together. As you engage in spiritual warfare, ensure you have every part of the armour in place, and exercise your authority in Christ. God will make you victorious always.
prayer: Iprecious Father, I thank You because our weapons of warfare are not ordinary but mighty through You. I thank You for the power of attorney in the name of Jesus. Whenever I mention the name of Jesus, the adversary and situations must conform. I thank You, Lord, for the victory I have in You. Amen.
furtherStudies: Ephesians 1:19 KJV, 2 Corinthians 10:4-6 TPT, 1 John 2:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: understanding Spiritual warfare (2)
verse: Then Jesus came to them and said, 'All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me
body: Beyond the armour of God, there are important areas of knowledge that every believer must understand in order to be victorious in spiritual warfare. These resources serve as forms of training. Without them, it is like a soldier who is well armed but untrained in certain military tactics.
These knowledge areas include:

(1) The Finished Works of Christ: This refers to what Christ has already accomplished. When you engage in spiritual warfare, you are not trying to defeat the devil all over again. You are standing on the victory that Jesus already secured over Satan. You are standing on an existing protocol, and that protocol is Jesus. Colossians 2:15 AMP says, “When He had disarmed the rulers and authorities (those supernatural forces of evil operating against us), He made a public example of them (exhibiting them as captives in His triumphal procession), having triumphed over them through the cross.”
(2) The Believer's Authority: Luke 10:19 AMP says, “Listen

carefully! I have given you authority that you now possess to tread on serpents and scorpions, and the ability to exercise authority over all the power of the enemy; and nothing will in any way harm you.” When you gave your life to Christ, you received the authority to use the name of Jesus. This authority is activated as you put your faith to work through prayer, obedience to God's word, and the leadings of the Holy Spirit.

(3) Watch and Pray: Ephesians 6:18 KJV says, “Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit…” This emphasizes the importance of being guided by the Holy Spirit in your prayers because praying in the flesh will not profit you much. Romans 8:26 supports this truth. You must always be spiritually sensitive and alert.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for being my firm foundation. The authority is in Your name. I exercise that authority over every onslaught of the enemy. Thank You for making me more than a conqueror. Regardless of the plans of the enemy, I am victorious in You, in Jesus name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 16:20 KJV, Ephesians 6:10-18 KJV, Hebrews 4:16 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: How to Obtain God’s favour
verse: But the Lord was with Joseph, and showed him mercy, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison
body: Until God favors you, man will not favor you. It is a futile effort to seek the favor of man because you might be humiliated and faced with compromising options. This is not to say that you should be prideful or arrogant. The key point here is that you should rather focus on finding favor with God, who in turn will cause men to favor you (Proverbs 21:1 AMP).

God's favor can be described as a clear proof that a person has God's approval. This approval brings evident beauty and blessings into your life. Favor is not hidden; it is obvious and reflects outwardly too.

Daniel 1:9 ESV says, “And God gave Daniel favor and compassion in the sight of the chief of the eunuchs.” The favor Daniel received is similar to Joseph's experience. It is important to note that this kind of favor is not just human kindness but is divinely inspired. It is not dependent on your circumstances; rather, it is usually a divine intervention.
Jesus and Samuel obtained favor from God, according to Luke 2:52 and 1 Samuel 2:26. There was something common with all these people; they all feared the Lord, and this made them find favor with man.

Psalm 147:11 AMP says, “The Lord favors those who fear and worship Him (with awe inspired reverence and obedience), those who wait for His mercy and loving kindness.” The fear of the Lord does not mean to be afraid of God. Instead, it means to have a reverential respect for Him and to honor Him. Anyone who fears the Lord will definitely obtain favor from Him.
prayer: The Spirit of the fear of the Lord is at work in me. It makes me to reverence the Lord in all my ways. I produce fruits of righteousness, and I will live my life to please You, Lord. Amen.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 16:7 KJV, Psalm 103:13 KJV, Psalm 34:9-10 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Resistance in the Evil Day
verse: Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand
body: In Mark 14:38, Jesus commanded His disciples to watch and pray in order not to enter into temptation. Temptation could be enticements to sin, tests, or trials. These trials are attacks against your faith, the things you believe in Christ, and against God's provisions and inheritance for you in Christ. The evil day is the day the enemy unleashes these attacks on you.

The attack itself is not the main issue, because we already know that we are in an ongoing spiritual warfare. The real question is: are you able to resist the attacks or will you be vulnerable? This is what Apostle Paul was emphasizing to us: to put on the whole armour of God in order to develop resistance when the evil day shows up (Ephesians 6:13).

From Mark 14:38, the scripture emphasizes that being spiritually vigilant and prayerful are protective measures against falling into the snares and attacks of the enemy. In addition to the protective power of prayer, Ephesians 6:13-18 outlines the spiritual armours that enable a believer to develop resistance against the enemy and the evil day. Ephesians 6:16
KJV says, “Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.”

The shield Paul referenced was the Roman shield, and it was large enough to protect the entire body of a soldier. This Roman shield provided an overall resistance to the enemy's attacks during warfare. Faith in God and in His word serves as a shield that provides all-round protection and nullifies the enemy's attacks, rendering them ineffective.
Strengthen your faith by giving more attention to God's word. Faith comes by hearing God's word (Romans 10:17).
prayer: I declare: my faith is alive and active. I submit myself to God's word, and it strengthens my faith. My faith is firm. I am vigilant and prayerful. My walls of defense are well protected. I am immune to Satan's attacks in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 16:13 KJV, 2 Corinthians 10:4-5 ESV, James 4:7
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Power of Testimonies
verse: Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God
body: Romans 1:16 KJV says, “For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believeth.” The gospel is the good news of the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus and all He has done for you. The word testimony means a solemn declaration or attestation to the truth of God's goodness. Do not be ashamed to declare who God is and what He has done.

When you testify of God's goodness, not just to you but to humanity, God's power is made available to turn people's hearts and lead them to salvation. This simply means testimonies lead people to Christ.

Testifying of God's goodness is an act of thanksgiving that reflects a heart of gratitude. Doing this brings wholeness and perfection to your life, just as seen in the story of the ten lepers. Only one returned to testify, and his healing was made complete (Luke 17:17-19).
Revelation 12:11 KJV says, “And they overcame him by the
blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony.” This reveals the believer's victory over Satan through the blood of Jesus and their declaration of the finished works of Christ.

Satan does not want you to testify of your rightful inheritance in Christ because he knows how powerful it is. In all you do, do not stop declaring the good news of God and your realities as a new creation.
prayer: I testify: I am a new creation in Christ Jesus. I am the seed of Abraham and a partaker of the Abrahamic blessings. I am blessed beyond measure. I walk in victory and dominion. I am favored. I am wonderfully and fearfully made. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: 1 John 5:4-5 KJV, Ephesians 6:11-17 KJV, Matthew 10:32-33 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Dwelling in the Secret Place
verse: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty
body: From our opening verse, it emphasizes the importance of dwelling in the secret place. It did not say he that visits the secret place but he that lives there. Continual habitation in the secret place is what matters. What is the secret place? It is not a physical location but fellowshipping and having an intimate relationship with God.

Think of it this way: in your home, there is usually a private room or chamber which is not meant for visitors. God does not need you to be a visitor; He needs you to become a resident in the secret place. That is why the scripture says, “Come boldly to the throne of grace, that you may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need” (Hebrews 4:16). This shows the need to continuously fellowship with God through prayer and the Word. God sent Jonah to the Assyrian city of Nineveh, but Jonah tried to run from his assignment.
The verse says, “shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty” (Psalm 91:1). The shadow of the Almighty signifies the glory and presence of God. Anyone who dwells in the secret place will
experience God's glory and presence. The weight of God's glory you will manifest is dependent on your commitment to the secret place.

God's presence will protect you from the dangers and challenges of life (Psalm 91:3-16 NIV). James 4:8 ESV says, “Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double- minded.” As you spend more time with God, He will draw near to you by revealing Himself and His glory. This will purge you of all ungodliness, enabling the fruits of the recreated human spirit to take root and grow in your life. You will begin to see life from an eternal perspective.
prayer: Thank you, LORD, for bringing me into fellowship with your dear Son, Jesus Christ. Thank you for granting me access to your throne of grace. Help me, LORD, not to neglect my responsibilities in the secret place. I will continue to totally surrender to your Spirit and will for my life in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:6 KJV, Isaiah 60:1-2 KJV, John 15:4-5 ESV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Resist Ungodly Values
verse: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God
body: The scripture above warns believers against embracing the patterns and lifestyle of this secular world and present age. This world has its system, and it comprises practices that are contrary to the will and purposes of God. The devil is the god of the system of this world and he has set up deceptions in order to cause people to derail from God's will. No wonder 2 Corinthians 4:4 KJV says, “In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.”

There are several societal norms and traditions that conflict with Christian teachings and they cause a lot of moral decay. Practices like polygamy, cohabitation, gay marriage, and many more are against God's will. God warns us to resist and reject societal standards that do not align with His will.

This world's system is very enticing but, in all things, we have to use the principles of God's Word and rely on the Holy Spirit to reject them. God's Word will help you discern rightly in the midst of the cunning craftiness of the devil and this world. It will renew
your thought process as we see in Ephesians 4:23-24 KJV, “And be renewed in the spirit of your mind; and that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”
prayer: In the name of Jesus, I refuse to be conformed to the system of this world, rather I will continue to renew my mind through God's Word. As I study and hear God's Word, I am being transformed and aligned to the character of Jesus Christ, amen.
furtherStudies: 1 John 2:15-17 KJV, Colossians 3:10 KJV, 1 Peter 1:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Endure to the End
verse: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves
body: Matthew 10:5 tells us that Jesus sent his disciples to preach the good news of the kingdom of God. He also warned them about the persecution they would face. In Matthew 10:16, Jesus said they were being sent as sheep in the midst of wolves. Wolves are always ready to devour sheep, which means persecution was certain.

Times of persecution are difficult. They come with pressure, trouble, distress, or adversity. This persecution arises because you believe in and are identified with Christ Jesus and his kingdom. “If you are weak in a crisis, you are weak indeed” (Proverbs 24:10 GNT). Do not grow weary, do not go underground, and do not stop preaching. Do not stop attending church when persecution against God's people arises. Be strong in the Lord and stand firm.

As conveyed in James 1:2 NLT, “Dear brothers and sisters, when troubles of any kind come your way, consider it an opportunity for great joy”. And “Blessed is the one who perseveres under trial because, having stood the test, that person will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised
to those who love him” (James 1:12 NIV). The person who endures persecution to the end has a greater reward than any earthly blessing. The Lord himself will reward such a person with a crown of life.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for your hedge of protection upon my life. I fear no evil and my heart will never grow weary. I will maintain my faith in you always. I will serve you and make your name known till the end of time, in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 24:12 NKJV, Luke 21:19 NLT, Matthew 10:38 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Storing Treasures in Heaven
verse: Store your treasures in heaven, where moths and rust cannot destroy, and thieves do not break in and steal
body: Generally, treasures are valuable items, but in the context of this Bible verse, treasures refer to the activities you perform on earth that have valuable significance to God. He has a reward for you because of those activities. As you serve the Lord and render services to Him, do them wholeheartedly and do not expect rewards from anyone on earth, because your reward awaits you in heaven.

Hebrews 6:10 NKJV says “For God is not unjust to forget your work and labor of love which you have shown toward His name, in that you have ministered to the saints, and do minister.” God is not unfaithful to forget all the things you do for His sake on earth. That is why they are compiled as treasures for you in heaven.

There is such a thing as prayer banks. Prayer is an act of worship, and as you pray, they are stored up as prayer deposits. These prayers can produce results for you on earth. Just as you save money in the bank, you can also store up prayers in the prayer bank. So, keep praying and making deposits as
treasures in heaven.

Your giving for the furtherance of the gospel and your soul winning activities are also treasures. These are valuable to God and He will definitely reward you for them. All that you do for the Lord and the body of Christ is valuable to God. Therefore, continue to store up treasures for yourself in heaven, where no moth can destroy them.
prayer: Thank you, heavenly Father, for the privilege to render services to you. I am grateful that you are not unjust to forsake all my services to your name. I will never grow weary. Rather, I will always do more to the glory and praise of your name, in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 19:20 KJV, I Timothy 6:19 NLT, Isaiah 33:6 LB
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Healthy Spiritual Eyes
verse: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are healthy, your whole body will be full of light
body: To have a healthy spiritual vision means having the ability to see the purposes of God clearly, to see God clearly, and to see things from His point of view. God sees things differently, and it is only through the scriptures and His Spirit that you will be able to have healthy spiritual eyes.

Someone's spiritual eyes can be obscured by self-gratification: self-interest and self-desires (Romans 13:14 NIV). The devil is also an expert in obscuring the spiritual eyes of people. 2 Corinthians 4:4 says “Satan, who is the god of this world, has blinded the minds of those who do not believe…”

Proverbs 14:14 KJV says “A backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways…” A backslider does not see anything wrong in what he or she is doing because their spiritual eyes are obscured. Serving the Lord wholeheartedly is a great way to restore your sight. It will help your desires and gaze to be focused on God, and His illumination will cause you to begin to see through God's lenses.
I pray for you today that the eyes of your understanding be enlightened by the power of God's Spirit, and may any veil that has hindered you from seeing, doing, and becoming all that God
has planned for you be broken, in Jesus' name, amen.
prayer: I arise, I shine, for my light has come. The light of God illuminates my heart, causing me to see from God's standpoint. The eyes of my understanding are enlightened to realize and accomplish God's purpose for my life, in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 6:22-23 KJV, Ephesians 1:17-19 ESV, Acts 26:18 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Concerned about God
verse: These things dominate the thoughts of unbelievers, but your heavenly Father already knows all your needs
body: Matthew 6:33 GNT says, “Instead, be concerned above everything else with the kingdom of God and with what he requires of you, and he will provide you with all these other things.” What are these other things? These are the things people desire to live comfortably on earth. Unbelievers and ignorant people struggle and spend most of their lives trying to acquire these other things, without knowing that God will provide them when they begin to be concerned about His Kingdom and what He requires of them.

God created you, and He also knew that you would need certain things at various stages of your life, so He made provision for them. God does not want you anxious and burdened because of the things you need. That is why He is saying to you, “Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest” (Matthew 11:28 NIV).

God knew that you would need a great family, home, job, material things, peace of mind, healing, miracles, and much more. And He gives you a solution, which is: be more concerned about His Kingdom and how to please Him. For when you do,
He will give you rest by providing everything you need. Christ is your sufficiency, for in Him, you will have all you need.
prayer: Dear Lord, I will continue to press on to seek You and all that concerns Your Kingdom. I will not allow myself to be carried away by the cares of this world, because You care and provide for all my needs, in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 8:18 KJV, 1 Kings 3:11-13 KJV, Matthew 19:29 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: He Makes you Prosper
verse: For I know the plans I have for you,” declares the LORD, “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future
body: The word “prosperity” comes from “prosper”, which means to be happy, to have a successful journey, to be favorable, to be blessed, and to have continued success. God wants you to prosper. The Beatitudes talk about being blessed (see Matthew 5). Prosperity is being favored and flourishing.

It is sad that many have limited prosperity to wealth and material possessions. Those things are not necessarily proof of prosperity. Beyond money and material things, you can prosper in your health, in your academics, in your mind, in your domestic relationships, in your walk with God, and in many other areas of life.

What good is it if you prosper financially and materially, but do not prosper in your health, your mind, and your walk with God? Focusing only on material things as a sign of prosperity is a sign of carnality and reveals the state of your heart as one that loves money. And remember, the love of money is the root of all evil (1
Timothy 6:10).
God wants you to experience all round prosperity in your life.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for blessing me with all things that pertain to life and godliness. I flourish in every area of my life. I am abundantly supplied with all good things of life. In all my getting, I put You first and I will never be covetous.
furtherStudies: 3 John 1:2 KJV, 2 Peter 1:3 KJV, Luke 12:15 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Heirs of Blessings
verse: And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise
body: If you belong to Christ, then you are a seed of Abraham, not by blood but according to the promise. Anyone who is saved belongs to Christ. The question is, what promise?

Romans 4:13 CSB says, “For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants that he would inherit the world was not through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.” Through your faith in Jesus Christ, you have been made righteous and officially a descendant of Abraham, and you are now entitled to inherit all the good things God promised him.

Genesis 22:2 KJV says, “And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing.” Genesis 27:28 KJV also declares, “Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine.”

These are blessings for every believer. There are so many blessings laid up for you. You are too blessed to be cursed. As long as you continue to walk in righteousness and boldly declare the blessings and inheritance you have in Christ, you
will have the full experience of all that belongs to you, because you are an heir of blessings.
prayer: I am an heir of blessing. I am productive and I multiply on every side. I enjoy the dews of heaven and I eat the good of the land. I own and I will always be exceedingly fruitful, in Jesus’ name, amen!
furtherStudies: Genesis 15:5 KJV, Genesis 17:16 KJV, Genesis 27:28-29 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Firm Foundation
verse: Therefore, whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock
body: J esus Christ is the firm foundation. This reminds me of an old hymn from the Graham family: “On Christ the solid rock I stand, all other ground is sinking sand.” Indeed, all other ground sinks because they have no foundation, but in Christ, we have a firm foundation and we remain unshakeable in Him.

Jesus is the Word of God made flesh (John 1:14). Since Jesus is the firm foundation and He is also the Word of God, that means the Word of God is the firm foundation. Matthew 7:24 reveals to us that acting on the Word of God builds your life on a solid rock. When you start acting on the Word of God, your life becomes firm. But the one who hears the Word and does not take action is a person with a shaky foundation and such a person is likened to be foolish.
To build on a solid foundation means to be a doer of the Word. Practicing obedience to God's Word builds a firm foundation and enables you to withstand the pressures and storms of life.
prayer: I am a doer of the Word of God, not a hearer only. The Word of Christ dwells in me richly, and when the enemy rises like a flood, the Word of God in my spirit will rise against it. God's Word is always in me.
furtherStudies: James 1:22-27 KJV, Matthew 7:25-26 KJV, Psalms 111:10 NLT
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Salvation Package
verse: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved
body: To be saved means to be delivered from eternal condemnation and to receive the gift of eternal life. All of this happens when you say the prayer of salvation (Romans 10:9). The gift of eternal life is found in Christ Jesus. When you receive Christ into your heart, you also receive eternal life. Because you are in Christ, there is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:1).

Salvation is a total package. Instead of chasing after other things that can distract you, Jesus advised us to seek Him and all other things will be added. “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you” (Matthew 6:33). To seek means to desire, to search, to press on. In the first place, above everything else, desire the kingdom of God and every other thing will be yours. “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness” (Proverbs 8:18 KJV).
The salvation package contains all you need to live a successful Christian life on earth and to prepare for eternity. It includes

forgiveness and freedom from sin, justification, spiritual authority, divine health and healing, deliverance, protection, assurance of the future, grace, preservation, spiritual blessings and all other great things in Christ (2 Peter 1:3).
prayer: Thank you, Father, for your divine power has given me everything that I require for a godly life. I will continue to desire your kingdom and your righteousness. I refuse to walk in the flesh, but I will always walk in the Spirit, in Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: 2 Peter 1:3-4 NIV, Acts 4:12 NLT, Proverbs 3:16 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: How to Receive God’s Word
verse: The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life
body: This means that God's words are invisible forces and power. If anyone receives His words, they will begin to work in that person's life and produce exactly what the word says.

In Mark 4:9, “And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear”, Jesus wants us to hear His words. There is a special kind of hearing He is referring to. It is not the kind of attention or listening you give when hearing a newscaster, a commentator, or music. Though the ears are for hearing, He wants a deeper kind of listening, one that involves your mind and your heart, in order to gain spiritual understanding from God's words.

To hear God's word is to receive it with faith, base your life on it, and allow it to influence your decisions, attitude, and actions. God's word is filled with His power to produce exactly what it talks about, if you allow it and receive it wholeheartedly with faith.
When you receive God's word wholeheartedly with faith, it

strengthens the faith you already have, renews your mind, helps you recognize God's voice, helps you walk in obedience, and makes you not just a hearer but also a doer (James 1:25). The next time you listen to or study the scriptures, receive them wholeheartedly with faith. The word will produce in you and for you everything it says, and it will make you fruitful unto God.
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for your word. Your word is spirit and life. I declare that I will always receive your word with faith and meekness of heart. Your word will always produce in me what it talks about and make me fruitful unto you. I am a doer of the word. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Matthew 13:23 KJV, John 15:16 ESV, 1 Thessalonians 2:13 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Holy Spirit Dwells in you
verse: Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
body: Ezekiel 37:14 KJV says, “I will put my spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land. Then you shall know that I, the LORD, have spoken it and performed it, says the LORD.” Also, Ezekiel 36:27 NIV says, “I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you will keep my judgments and do them.” This was God's promise to release His Spirit (the Holy Spirit) to dwell in His people. This promise was fulfilled in the new covenant, which began after the resurrection of Jesus (Acts 2:1-13).

The Holy Spirit dwelling in a believer is known as the indwelling presence. This means He has come to abide in you and make your body His abode. That was why Apostle Paul reminded believers that their bodies are the temple of God (1 Corinthians 3:16 NKJV). The indwelling presence of the Holy Spirit in the life of a believer reveals intimacy between man and God. It brings divine empowerment, guidance, assurance, and the fulfilment of all God wants to do in and through a believer.
The indwelling presence serves as a seal on every believer. This is called the seal of Christ, and it guarantees our

inheritance in Christ. This inheritance includes multitudes of blessings: physical, spiritual, and eternal. Ephesians 1:13-14 AMP says, “In Him, you also, when you heard the word of truth, the good news of your salvation, and as a result believed in Him, were stamped with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit (the one promised by Christ) as owned and protected by God. The Spirit is the guarantee (the first installment, the pledge, a foretaste) of our inheritance until the redemption of God's own purchased possession, to the praise of His glory.”

The Holy Spirit you have received came to dwell in you forever, and He will not leave or forsake you (John 14:16). He expects you to nurture the relationship so you can benefit from His ministry in your life.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for the fulfilment of your promise by pouring out your Spirit into my life. Thank you for the amazing blessings the Holy Spirit has brought into my life. As I continue to pray and study your word, I am being transformed and growing in my relationship with you. Amen!
furtherStudies: John 15:26 KJV, Acts 2:4 KJV, Isaiah 11:2 KJV, Ephesians 4:30 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Nurturing the indwelling Presence
verse: Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God?
body: God dwelling in you through His Spirit is the indwelling presence. This is the promise of the Father which has been fulfilled in the life of every believer. God wants an intimate relationship with you. Earthly relationships need to be nurtured. Likewise, our relationship with the indwelling presence must be nurtured.

Nurturing the indwelling presence means making available the right atmosphere that will nourish the presence of God in your life. The Holy Spirit desires to flourish in your life if you permit Him. The full definition of your life and fulfilment of your purpose depends on how much you nurture the indwelling presence.

It is important to understand that the Holy Spirit has a distinct personality. He can be pleased or displeased. It is interesting to know that whatever you do that nurtures His presence makes Him pleased (Acts 15:28 NLT), and whatever steps you take that do not nurture His presence grieve and displease Him (Ephesians 4:30-32 KJV).

Here are a few ways to nurture the indwelling presence of God: (1) Holiness – The Holy Spirit requires you to live a holy and sanctified life. As a believer being the temple of the Holy Spirit, He needs you to live a worthy life that pleases the Lord. Live a godly life and produce fruits of righteousness (Romans 8:9).

(2) Consistent Life of Prayer – Prayer is communication with God, and it leads to intimacy with Him. As communication is vital in marriage, so also is communication with God through prayer. Prayer sharpens your spiritual sensitivity, especially when praying in the Spirit. Praying in the Spirit edifies and strengthens the believer's spirit (1 Corinthians 14:2).

(3) Studying God's Word – God's Word transforms your mind and thought process, allowing you to approach life from God's perspective and understand His precepts. This will foster your relationship with the indwelling presence of God (Romans 12:2).

(4) Total Submission to the Holy Spirit – God is always speaking to us through His Spirit. He wants to lead you in the great path He has planned for you. He needs you to do His will, not yours. Self is an enemy of the Spirit, always wanting to satisfy your desires rather than submitting to God's desires, leadings, and promptings. He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30 KJV).

(5) Christian Service – Learn to serve others with your gifts. Your gifts are to glorify God. Serving with your gifts and abilities is a tangible expression of your devotion to God, and it helps mature the presence of the Holy Spirit in your life (1 Peter 4:10- 11).
prayer: I declare the word of Christ dwells in me richly. It changes my thoughts and my approach to life. The ministry of the Holy Spirit blossoms in my life. I will always submit to the Spirit and His leadership. I declare I shall serve others with my gifts to the glory of your name. In Jesus' name, amen. FURTHER
furtherStudies: Psalm 42:1-2 ESV, Romans 8:14 ESV, James 4:8 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You have the Seal of Christ
verse: ...that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.
body: The seal of Christ is God's mark on a believer. It symbolizes God's ownership, authenticity, and protection on His people. Seals are used to secure documents, letters, and packages to ensure that their contents remain untouched and authentic.

1 Corinthians 6:20 KJV says “For ye are bought with a price: therefore, glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's. As similarly contained in Revelation 5:9 NIV, “And they sang a new song, saying, You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, because you were slain, and with your blood you purchased for God persons from every tribe and language and people and nation”. In the ancient world, to be bought meant being purchased as a slave or as property, and a seal was often placed on them as a brand. As a believer, you were purchased with the precious blood of God's only Son, Jesus. You have been branded by God. You are God's brand, and you have His seal upon you.

You have been redeemed from sin and death through the blood of Jesus Christ. Sin and death are consequences that Satan inflicts on people who belong to him. In fact, all of creation was bound to sin and death because of Adam's sin (Romans 5:17). But God, in His mercy, sent Jesus to die for humanity. The blood of Jesus was the price God paid to free you from sin and death and to claim you as His own. As a believer, you are God's own. You bear the seal of Christ.

Ephesians 1:13 KJV says “In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that Holy Spirit of promise. This seal implies that, as a believer, you have been set apart for God. You have been separated from the domain of Satan and his influences (Colossians 1:13). You are protected by God's sovereign authority as His precious possession.

The Holy Spirit God gave you when He purchased you with the blood of His Son is a guarantee of the full inheritance to come. This signifies the certainty of all God's promises and blessings, which include the future resurrection, glorification, and fulfilment of His redemptive plan (Ephesians 1:14 KJV).
prayer: Thank you, Father, for making me a valuable possession of Yours. Thank you for the Holy Spirit that serves as Your seal upon my life. I am divinely protected, cared for, loved, and guaranteed of the promises which are to come. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: John 6:27 KJV, Ephesians 1:13-14, 2 Corinthians 1:21-22 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Striving for Mastery
verse: And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we, an incorruptible
body: Striving for mastery refers to diligent and lawful efforts required to excel or win during a competition. The phrase every man that striveth for mastery in Greek is agonizomenos, which is where the English word agonise comes from. It refers to deep intensity, fervent and heartfelt effort, such as in prayer.

In general, it points to great commitment, devotion, and dedication to achieve a given task. Apostle Paul is saying that anyone who wants to become a master or a winner must put in great effort. This great commitment involves being temperate in all things: fulfilling all (not just some) necessary conditions.

Being temperate in all things means exercising self-denial and self-control. In ancient Greco-Roman culture, athletics was a popular activity, and the winner was usually honoured with a floral crown. Before the game, contestants had to adhere to strict training routines. This is what being temperate means: being disciplined. They were subject to specific diets, exercise, and mental preparedness. Apostle Paul uses athletic discipline to illustrate the discipline required in our Christian journey,
emphasising the importance of self-control and perseverance.

Hebrews 12:1 KJV says “Let us run with endurance the race that is set before us”. The heavenly race is set before us, and we should run it well so we can win an incorruptible crown when we get to Heaven. Therefore, we must be disciplined in all things. Self is an enemy of this race: self-preservation, self- glorification, self-reward, and so on. Keep your focus on Jesus (Hebrews 12:2 KJV). Exercise discipline, perseverance, and dedication in your relationship with God.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for your word that has brought strength and encouragement to me today. As I run this race, keep my gaze on you. Through your Spirit, I will be dedicated and temperate in all things. I will always be intentional and consistent in my walk with you. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Titus 2:2 KJV, 1 Timothy 6:12 KJV, 2 Corinthians 4:17-18 KJV, Philippians 3:14
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Understanding Divine Order in Relationships
verse: That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed. Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded
body: Divine order in relationships is the structured arrangement established by the sovereignty of God. It reflects God's wisdom and purpose for human relationships. This helps us understand the essence of relationships, family, and moral duty.

Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands as you do to the Lord (Ephesians 5:22 NIV) and Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her (Ephesians 5:25 NIV). In marriage, God's divine order is that the man is the head of the home. He is expected to love his wife as Christ loved the church, and the woman is to submit herself to her husband.

In a marriage relationship, God expects parents to raise their children in godly ways, as we see in Proverbs 22:6 KJV: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old, he will not depart from it. This helps children to develop good morals and

eventually raise their own children in God's way. This is the definition of godly parenting. It also includes the responsibility of the man to provide for his household (1 Timothy 5:8) and the woman being supportive. Children should also honour their parents (Ephesians 6:2-3 NIV).

In Leviticus 18:6-18, God defines sexual relationships with close relatives as forbidden. No matter how much you love a family member, God's divine order does not permit marriage or intimacy with a relative. Also, Leviticus 18:22-24 reveals that God detests sexual relationships between a fellow man, a fellow woman, or with animals. These are defilements of one's self and are outside of God's plan for human relationships.
I pray for you, that you may always recognise God's sovereignty and purpose for creation, and live according to God's will. In Jesus' name, amen.
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for the insight your word has brought to me. I will honour your word above every ungodly cultural or societal practice. I declare that I will not be enticed or led astray by any false doctrine from the enemy. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 11:10 NIV, Genesis 2:18 KJV, Leviticus 20:13 KJV, 1 Corinthians 6:9-10 NIV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Heart: The Seat of Wisdom
verse: For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul
body: t he biological definition of the heart is the muscular organ that pumps blood in the body. However, this is quite different from the scriptural definition. When the Bible says the heart, it refers to the seat or center of human will, emotions, and thoughts. The heart is the seat of wisdom.

From the Hebrew definition, the heart refers to the inner being, and from our opening scripture, wisdom enters the heart, resides there, and influences one's thought process, words, choices, and actions. The quality of your life depends on how much wisdom you allow to enter your heart. The condition of your heart is based on the level of wisdom that is present. God's word is the source of wisdom (2 Timothy 3:15 NLT). How much of God's word do you have in your heart?

Matthew 15:19-20 KJV says, For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornication, thefts, false witness, blasphemies. These are things that defile a man... King Solomon wrote in Proverbs 4:23 NLT, Guard your heart above all else, for it determines the course of your life. It is now your
responsibility to protect your heart because it will determine the progression of your life: either in wisdom or foolishness, life or death.

I admonish you today to open your heart to God's word, for it will grant you divine wisdom to walk in the ways of God and deal wisely in all the affairs of life. I pray for you; may the Lord grant you a new heart that is receptive to His word. May He give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him and so enlighten the eyes of your understanding. In Jesus' name, amen.
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for the spirit of truth and wisdom that you have given me. I thank you for giving me a heart that delights in your word and your precepts. Cause me to continue to grow in wisdom and understanding. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 12:34-35 ESV, Jeremiah 17:9-10 ESV, Romans 12:2 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: How to Handle Depression and Sorow
verse: Why are you depressed, O my soul? Why are you upset? Hope in God! For I will again give thanks to my God for His saving intervention
body: The King James version of Psalm 42:11 says, Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
The psalmist experienced several trials, feelings of abandonment, depression, sorrow, and being downcast. All these affect mental and emotional health. They are all classified as emotional turmoil.

Faith is not the denial of facts. As believers, we have faith in God, and we should not deny that many people are affected by emotional turmoil. We should not shy away from this. It is important to deal with it from the standpoint of God's word, which is the best approach. There are motivational teachings and therapists that have helped many over the years, and that is good. However, the principles of God's word are ever sure and are the most reliable approach, even for dealing with the spiritual aspects of depression and sorrow.
In Matthew 26:38 NJV, Jesus was overwhelmed with sorrow at the point of death. Job was faced with great loss (Job 3:26) and many more. Here are the ways they handled the situation:

(1) Prayer and supplication: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your request be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your heart and your mind in Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:6-7 ESV). The victory of Jesus at the Cross was initiated at the garden of Gethsemane when He was sorrowed in prayer (Matthew 26:38-39). That prayer gave Him strength. He did not give up. Rather, He went on to do the will of the Father. Prayer, even when broken, gives strength. Sorrow and depression will heal quicker through prayer and will help you come out strong.
(2) Trust in God's word: No matter how painful or distressed you are, just trust God's word that all things, including your current situation, will work out for your good (Romans 8:28).

(3) Seek support from Christian community: The Christian community or the local church will be a great support to you. The church is for the edification of God's people (Ephesians 4:12). Galatians 6:2 KJV says, Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. You will receive a lot of resources from the Christian community to encourage you and help you navigate out victoriously.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you, for you are my ever-present help in time of need. I thank you for you are my firm foundation, and I will not be shaken regardless of whatever I face in life. I am and will be victorious at all times. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: READINGBIBLE Romans 15:1-2 KJV, John 14:27 ESV, Psalm 55:22
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Godly Parenting
verse: Train up a child in the way he should go, teaching him to seek God's wisdom and will for his abilities and talents, even when he is old, he will not depart from it
body: Training up a child involves an intentional process of guardianship or parenting. It is an act of consistent commitment to the moral and spiritual upbringing and development of a child in the path that is appropriate for the child. Each child is unique. It is important that parents or guardians understand their unique gifts, personality, and calling.

Parenting consists of long term committed and consistent training which begins in the early stage of the child's life. This involves imparting foundational teachings of wisdom and righteousness. It is easier at this stage because children are open and easily influenced. This is vital because whatever impact or seed you sow will be the fruits they will bear when they grow up.

Parents are primary key players in a child's life, as they are responsible for inculcating discipline and God's instruction in a child. Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger by the way you treat them. Rather, bring them up with the discipline and instruction that comes from the Lord (Ephesians 6:4 NLT). As

parents, it is important not to provoke a child or push them too hard, which may lead to anger. Rather, they should patiently nurture the child in a loving manner, easily forgiving of new mistakes. Endeavour to correct the child in love.

Parents should also be of good influence and be knowledgeable. Proverbs 4:3-4 KJV says, For I was my father's son, tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother. He taught me also, and said unto me, Let thine heart retain my words; keep my commandments, and live. This reveals a personal transfer of wisdom, instruction, and discipleship from parents to children. A child can only embrace wisdom if the parents have wisdom to offer.
In today's fast-paced and innovative world, parents should endeavour to embrace self-development. This will enhance their parenting skills, improve communication, and increase resilience.
prayer: Lord, continue to grant me guidance, grace, and wisdom to be a good parent and guide to children in our society. I declare that I will love children, be patient, nurturing, and influence them positively and in the ways of the Lord. In Jesus' name, amen.
furtherStudies: Deuteronomy 6:6-7 KJV, Proverbs 22:6 KJV, Deuteronomy 4:5-9 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: engaging Actively with Scriptures
