Souls are perishing and because of the short time left to reach the unsaved and the unchurched, the Lord is in need of people whom He will send as messengers to share His saving grace. Whenever you have needs, you ask God and He answers you. Now, God has a need. He needs you to witness for Him. Are you going to turn Him down or will you say, “Send me Lord?”

Psalm 67:2 TPT says, Send us out all over the world so that everyone, everywhere will discover your ways and know who you are and see your power to save. This was the prayer of David. Say this same prayer and ask God to send you as His oracle and mouthpiece.
You are the light of the world. You cannot be hidden and quiet anymore. Sit up and shine. Reflect the glory of the Lord by availing yourself to be used by Him. Isaiah 52:7 NLT says, How
beautiful on the mountain are the feet of the messenger who brings good news, the good news of peace and salvation, the news that the God of Israel reigns!

When you received the Holy Spirit, you received divine enablement to proclaim the gospel to everyone around you. Therefore, go out in the fullness of this power of the Holy Spirit and be that messenger for the Lord.
prayer: I affirm that I am God's messenger to the world. I go about proclaiming the gospel and the saving power of Jesus. I am bold and courageous for the Lord. I preach this gospel in and out of season by the enablement of the Holy Spirit. Thank you, Lord, for you are with me always. Amen!
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 15:3-4, Romans 1:16
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Your Confidence is in Christ
verse: For the Lord shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken.
body: The Oxford Dictionary defines confidence as the feeling or belief that one can rely on something or someone. Many people only place their confidence in material things, wealth, connections, or even in other people. But until you face a situation where those things and individuals fail you, you may not truly understand what it means to trust in the Lord alone.

At times, God allows you to come to a point in life where the things you once relied on fail, so that you can run to Him and trust Him fully. Everything about your life should give glory to God (Isaiah 43:7). If all things always go smoothly for you, you may develop a sense of self-reliance. But when faced with situations beyond your ability, it becomes easier to depend on God and glorify Him in the end.

This is not a call to low self-esteem or cowardice. As believers, our confidence is rooted in our trust and assurance in the person and finished work of Christ. His redemptive work on the cross and His continual intercession for all who believe in Him (Romans 8:34) give us boldness. Knowing all Christ has done for us, He expects us to allow His finished work to change the way we think, speak, and act.

Philippians 4:13 KJV says, I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. This should be the way we speak, because we have full confidence that Christ living in us strengthens us and gives us the ability to face any task. This confidence in Christ gives you a positive picture of hope and encouragement.

In all things and circumstances, always know that God's faithfulness is certain. He started a good work in you and will complete it. I am convinced and confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will continue to perfect and complete it (Philippians 1:6 AMP).
prayer: Thank you, Jesus, for your sacrificial and finished work that has given me boldness to come before your throne of grace. Thank you for the confidence we have in you, knowing that you will finish every good work you have started in me. This I pray in Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Philippians 1:6 KJV, Hebrews 4:16 ESV, 1 John 5:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Working Out your Salvation
verse: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
body: The Scripture above does not suggest that salvation is achieved through numerous human efforts. Salvation is a gift received through faith in Jesus Christ, as revealed in Ephesians 2:8 KJV: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God. A gift is something freely given.

One receives salvation by confessing Jesus as Lord (Romans 10:9). After that, God expects us to work out our salvation. This means pursuing spiritual maturity and living in accordance with the salvation we have received. The good news is that God works in us, giving us both the desire and the ability to do what pleases Him (Philippians 2:13).

Working out your salvation is not a passive experience. It requires deliberate effort and must be done with reverence and awe towards God. While salvation is received once, it must be nurtured, maintained, and expressed in fruitful living. Jesus Himself warned that unfruitfulness leads to rejection (Matthew 7:21). Salvation is not once saved, always saved. A life of
constant sin without repentance shows a person is not truly working out their salvation.

The ultimate goal of salvation is eternity with the Father in heaven. Working out your salvation through faith, obedience, Bible study, prayer, service, and spiritual growth makes you fruitful to God and keeps you aligned with His purpose.
prayer: Thank You, my Heavenly Father, for saving me. Thank You for always working in me both to will and to do Your good pleasure. I declare that I will work out my salvation with reverence and godly fear. My life will bear fruits unto You, and I will live for the praise of Your name, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 6:9-10; Isaiah 26:13; James 2:14
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Can Be Healed Now
verse: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight.
body: Healing is the bread of God's children. In Matthew 15:26, Jesus reveals that healing belongs to those who are His. Bread is essential for survival; in the same way, healing is essential for life. Sickness and infirmities come in many forms: diseases, afflictions, and even torments caused by demonic influence.

Jesus, moved by compassion, healed all manner of diseases and infirmities. His mercy endures forever, and that same mercy is available to you today. Hebrews 13:8 NIV declares: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever. This means He has not changed. The same Jesus who healed in Bible days is still healing today.

From Matthew 15:26, healing is the bread of God's children. Just as bread is necessary for survival, so is healing. God desires to give you healing. Even as you read this devotional, the healing power of God is available for you. All He requires is your faith.

Lift your right hand as I pray for you. In the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of the Living God, I declare the healing power of God rests upon you right now. I command every demon of infirmity and affliction to depart from you. I command every symptom of sickness to disappear now. Be healed in the name of Jesus! Amen. Congratulations, you are healed. Go ahead and thank God.
prayer: Lord, thank You for healing me. I affirm that I am free from every pain, sickness, and infirmity. The Holy Spirit lives in me. He quickens and vitalizes my mortal body daily. I am impregnable to diseases and sickness. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: James 1:17 KJV, Luke 11:11-13 KJV, Acts 10:38 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: There is no condemnation Against you
verse: He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
body: The key to being free from condemnation is to believe in Jesus Christ as the Son of God and Saviour. Your justification is not based on your works but on your faith in Christ Jesus. John 3:18 NIV declares: Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe stands condemned already because they have not believed in the name of God's one and only Son.
In simple terms, the one who believes in Jesus is justified. He is acquitted. But the one who refuses to believe in Him is already condemned. Unbelief results in separation from God.

According to Romans 8:1 KJV, There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. Condemnation means judgment and penalty for sin. However, because you are in Christ Jesus (because you are born again), every charge and accusation against you has been blotted out by the blood of Jesus, making you free and justified. Colossians 2:14 KJV
says: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.

The devil, described as the accuser of the brethren (Revelation 12:10), always seeks to remind people of their past mistakes and shortcomings. He tries to make them feel that their sins are too big and unforgivable, leading to regret, depression, and self- condemnation. But always remind yourself that Jesus has already paid for all your sins. Therefore, boldly declare: Jesus has permanently set me free; I am free from guilt, and there is no condemnation against me because I am in Christ Jesus.
prayer: I am a child of God. Jesus has set me free from my past, every guilt, and every accusation. My mind is sound. The weapons of the enemy will not prosper against me. The blood of Jesus speaks on my behalf always. The devil has no hold on me. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: John 3:36 KJV; John 3:18 AMP; Romans 8:1–2; Colossians 2:14
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Be Spiritually Minded
verse: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace
body: The sinful nature of humanity has its consequences. The flesh is in opposition to the Spirit, and the flesh also has its influence on life. To be carnally minded means to have a mindset that is dominated by self and fleshly desires.

To be spiritually minded refers to developing a mindset that is transformed by the Spirit of God. This also means having a mindset that is dominated by God's will and purpose. Genesis 2:17 KJV says, But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it, for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die. Death here is not just physical but also spiritual, which is separation from God. This means being carnally minded leads to separation from God.

Separation from God as a result of carnal mindedness leads to fleshly living and bearing fruits of the flesh. It is enmity with God (Romans 8:7). This separation hinders your ability to partake in the divine nature of God.
To be spiritually minded is life and peace. This life and peace begin here on earth. Life refers to eternal life, which is the life

and nature of God. Through the Holy Spirit, you are connected to your source, enabled to bear fruits according to the desires of God. You also experience the peace of God that comes with spiritual mindedness. That is why Isaiah 26:3 KJV says, You will keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee.

Finally, open your heart to learn, study, and meditate on the word of God. God's word will fill your heart, regulate your thought process, and shift you from being carnally minded to being spiritually minded. Then you will experience the life and peace of God in abundance.
prayer: I have the life of God. My mind is regulated by the Holy Spirit and the word of God. God's word renews my mind. I refuse to conform to the systems of this world; rather, God's word transforms me always. I have the mind of Christ.
furtherStudies: 1 Corinthians 2:14 KJV, Galatians 5:16-17 KJV, Ephesians 4:23 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Law of the Spirit of Life
verse: It was for this freedom that Christ set us free (completely liberating us); therefore keep standing firm and do not be subject again to a yoke of slavery (which you once removed).
body: Romans 8:2 AMP says, For the law of the Spirit of life [which is] in Christ Jesus [the law of our new being] has set you free from the law of sin and death. The word law as used in the scripture above refers to a principle or power. The Spirit of life refers to the Holy Spirit, who imparts divine life into a believer.

The Holy Spirit is the life-giving Spirit. He brings life into dead and dry situations. He makes whole, quickens, restores, and even brings healing to the sick body. This Spirit of life gives eternal life to everyone who receives Christ, making them a new creation in Him.

On the other hand, the law of sin and death refers to the principle that leads to death. This came as a result of Adam's disobedience (Romans 5:19). Because of this principle, mankind could not attain righteousness by their own efforts. Even the Law of Moses could not make people righteous before
God; instead, it revealed sin and placed humanity under bondage.

But glory to God! Romans 3:25 NIV says, God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, through the shedding of His blood – to be received by faith. Jesus became the perfect sacrifice. Now, through faith, anyone can receive the benefits of His atoning sacrifice. The moment we accept Christ, the Holy Spirit comes into our lives and breaks the power of sin and death, making us free.
Now, in Christ, you have become the righteousness of God. Sin and death no longer have dominion over you (Romans 6:9). Hallelujah!
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being the perfect sacrifice for my sins. Thank You for making me the righteousness of God in You. I testify that the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death. Therefore, sin and death have no dominion over me. Hallelujah!
furtherStudies: Galatians 3:25 KJV, Matthew 28:6 KJV, 1 Corinthians 15:45 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Outpouring of the spirit
verse: And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules
body: The book of Joel 2:28 KJV says, And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions. This is God's abundant release of His Spirit upon all people.

In the book of Acts chapter 2, on the day of Pentecost, the promise of the Holy Spirit was fulfilled. Acts 2:2-4 says, And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

From the day of Pentecost till now, the Holy Spirit has been poured out upon all believers. The Holy Spirit brings divine empowerment and enables Christian living. The outpouring of the Holy Spirit has no cultural, social, gender, or ethnic
restriction.

The Holy Spirit is your teacher, advocate, comforter, counselor, helper, and standby. He has also made your body His abode (1 Corinthians 3:16). The Holy Spirit is the gift of the Father to humanity. When His presence is in your life, you are never alone. Perhaps you have been desiring that God should fill you with the Holy Spirit and enable you to benefit from all the blessings the Spirit offers, I would like to pray for you. Kindly repeat after me:

Thank you, Lord, for the gift of the Holy Spirit which you freely give to all who ask and believe in you. I ask you Lord to fill me with the Holy Spirit and enable me to speak in tongues right now in Jesus' name. Amen.
prayer: Thank you, Lord, for the outpouring of your Spirit in my life. I testify that I am full of the Holy Spirit. Lord, have your way and full expression in my life in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: John 14:17 KJV, John 16:13 KJV, Jeremiah 31:33 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Don’t Underestimate God’s Abilities
verse: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh; is there anything too hard for me?
body: Not underestimating God means trusting that He can do far more than you can imagine. It means refusing to limit your expectations of Him to your own understanding. God's love and power are limitless, and His ability goes beyond human reasoning.

In Matthew 14:13–21, when Jesus asked Philip where they could buy bread to feed the 5,000, Philip immediately started calculating the cost. That's what many of us do; we analyze situations with human logic and forget that God is not bound by our limitations.

Jesus went on to feed over five thousand people (excluding women and children) with only five loaves of bread and two fish. Not only were they all satisfied, but twelve baskets of leftovers remained. That miracle defied every human calculation.
When a situation looks too big, too costly, or beyond human effort and science, remember that God is sovereign. Just because you don't understand how it will happen doesn't mean
it's impossible with Him. Don't put God in a box. As Mark 10:27 teaches, With man, it is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.

Proverbs 3:5 reminds us: Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding. Even when you don't see the process, God wants you to trust His ability to bring about the miraculous in your life.
prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for Your supremacy. Thank You because nothing is impossible with You. I am grateful for Your power to do exceedingly, abundantly above all I could ever ask or imagine. I choose to trust in You completely. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Psalm 46:10 NLT, Job 42:2 KJV, Ephesians 3:20 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You are Healed
verse: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
body: The physical suffering of Jesus during His crucifixion brought both spiritual and physical healing to every believer. Isaiah 53:4 NET says, But he lifted up our illness, he carried our pain; even though we thought he was being punished, attacked by God, and afflicted for something he had done. Our focus here is: He lifted up our illness, He carried our pain. This is not a future promise; it has already been done.

During the crucifixion, there was a divine exchange. Jesus took your place. He carried your sicknesses, pains, afflictions, sorrows, burdens, and weaknesses. He did not want anyone who believes in Him to suffer sickness and affliction, so He took them away.

The punishment He endured was for your sake; so that you could have peace, wholeness, and reconciliation with God. By His stripes (the wounds from His scourging), you were healed. Because of this, you have no reason to remain in sickness. Hallelujah!
God does not see you as sick; He sees you as healed. The one for whom Jesus bore sickness and sin. The moment you gave your life to Christ, that exchange became your reality. So, what next?

Meditate on this truth until it renews your mind. Declare it boldly to yourself daily, even if symptoms linger. Continue this way until you experience the physical evidence of your healing. Glory to God!
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for taking away my sins, sicknesses, pain, diseases, afflictions, sorrows, and suffering. I declare that I am healed spiritually, mentally, and physically. The stripes of Jesus have healed me. I am totally whole, in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: Isaiah 53:6–12 KJV, 1 Peter 2:24 KJV, Matthew 8:17 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Love: A Proof of a True Disciple
verse: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
body: In His teaching to the disciples, Jesus emphasized that the love they show toward one another is the evidence to the world that they belong to Him. Love is the proof of true discipleship. The love Jesus referred to is the God-kind of love. It is unconditional, selfless, and sacrificial. This is called Agape love.

Sadly, in today's church, we often see pastors against pastors, believers competing with one another, and churches filled with jealousy, malice, and quarrels. Such behavior does not reflect the life of true disciples. 1 John 4:7 NIV says: Dear friends, let us love one another, for love comes from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God. Verse 8 continues: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

Love is not merely a profession with words; it is revealed in our actions, patience, and kindness towards one another. As 1 Corinthians 13:4-8 teaches, Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud. It is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrongs…

Paul also wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:5: Examine yourselves to see if your faith is genuine. Test yourselves. Surely you know that Jesus Christ is among you; if not, you have failed the test of genuine faith. If love is absent in your life, your faith is questionable. Moreover, Irrespective of the offense, past hurt, or misunderstanding you may have had with another believer, remember that even while you were lost in sin, God still loved you. He continues to love you unconditionally. Therefore, let go of bitterness and allow the love of God to flow through you by loving others.
prayer: Dear Lord, I affirm that love is my nature, for Your love is shed abroad in my heart by the Holy Spirit. I choose to walk in love always. In my heart, there is no space for hatred, bitterness, or unforgiveness. The love of God flows through me continually. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Corinthians 13:4-8 KJV, 1 John 3:16 NIV, 1 John 4:16 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: God’s Word Has a Curative Ability
verse: …for they are life to those who find them and health to one's whole body.
body: Psalm 107:20 reveals that God sent His Word and healed the people, delivering them from destruction. God's Word brings healing and deliverance only to those who embrace it. He will not force His Word on anyone, but the moment you accept it wholeheartedly and without doubt, your healing and deliverance will manifest.

The key is God's Word. It doesn't matter how many times or how many people have prayed for you; if you do not receive the Word with faith, it will not produce healing in you. Before the aspect of receiving God's Word comes into play, you must first hear the Word or study it for yourself. That is why Proverbs 4:22 says, God's words are life to those who find them and health to their whole body. You have to find it by making yourself available to it.
The word health in Proverbs 4:22 is from the Hebrew word Marpe, which means healing or medicine. Just like medicine has curative ability when taken properly, God's Word also has
spiritual and physical ailments, completely bringing restoration and wholeness.
prayer: The Holy Spirit lives in me; therefore, I am not susceptible to infirmity. The life of God in me keeps me in perfect health. Every day of my life is filled with God's glory, beauty, excellence, and grace. I exercise dominion over sickness and death. My body is infused with divine health and strength, in Jesus' name. Amen! FURTHER
furtherStudies: Psalm 107:20 KJV, John 6:63 KJV, Hebrews 4:12 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: He Vitalizes your Body
verse: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you. -
body: There is an influence of alcohol on the consumer. In that same way, the Holy Spirit has an influence not only on your spirit but also on your body. It is important to know your body is the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit.

1 Corinthians 6:19 NLT says, Don't you realize that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, who lives in you and was given to you by God? God wants you to be fully aware and understand clearly that His Spirit in you is not dormant. He is actively working and influencing all areas of your life, including your body. Until you accept this truth, you might not experience His full impact.

The word quicken as used in Romans 8:11 KJV means to make alive, to vitalize, to strengthen. This is the active and ongoing role of the Holy Spirit in you, ensuring that you are energized, revitalized, and strengthened at all times. Hallelujah!

Normally, no one can put his or her finger into a moving fan blade without being cut off by its active rotation. In the same manner, because of the active influence of the Holy Spirit in you, every germ, virus, or disease that tries to attack your body is cut off. Glory to God!
Not only are you supposed to think this way, but you must also make faith declarations of divine health over your body always.
prayer: I am a well-watered garden, and streams of healing waters flow from me. I don't contract or transmit diseases. Divine health is working in me. The presence of the Holy Spirit in me quickens, strengthens, and replenishes my body. I am always healthy and sound in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 8:9–11 KJV, Romans 4:14 KJV, 1 Corinthians 6:14 KJV, 2 Corinthians 4:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Don’t Give in to Satan’s Deception
verse: As soon as Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him. So Jesus told him, 'What you are about to do, do quickly.
body: Before Satan can use anyone to execute his agenda, he usually begins by giving that person a prompting. These promptings come as lies and deceptions. If he succeeds in gaining control of your mind, then it becomes easy for him to use you.

From John 13:27, the phrase when Judas took the bread means Judas had finally made up his mind to betray Jesus. The enemy had been prompting him repeatedly until he fully accepted the idea. Once he yielded, Satan entered into him.

In the same way, I have heard people say they heard voices telling them to do wrong things, or that their minds told them to commit suicide. These are promptings of Satan; they are direct attacks on the mind. Things like unforgiveness, hate, envy, jealousy, lies, and depression are also his promptings. Once they are accommodated in the heart, they crystallize into real actions that harm both you and others, eventually leading to regret, just as Judas experienced.
We see the same in the case of Ananias. Acts 5:3 NLT says,

Then Peter said, 'Ananias, why have you let Satan fill your heart? You lied to the Holy Spirit, and you kept some of the money for yourself.' Satan prompted him, and he yielded to the thought. That deception eventually led to his death. The enemy is always trying to use his manipulative skills to push believers against the will of God. This is why discernment is vital.

As a believer, you have the responsibility to resist these attacks and lies against your mind. Proverbs 4:23 CEV says, Carefully guard your thoughts because they are the source of true life. Be deliberate about rejecting thoughts that are not aligned with God's will. If you notice your mind being flooded with ungodly or unpleasant thoughts, rebuke them immediately and they will cease. In this regard, James 4:7 KJV stresses, Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
prayer: I declare that my mind is anointed. The Holy Spirit broods over me and regulates my thoughts. I do not accommodate evil or unwholesome ideas. I have the mind of Christ. I walk in love, power, and a sound mind in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Romans 12:2 NLT, Romans 8:6 KJV, 2 Corinthians 10:5 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Your Confession Brings the Manifestation
verse: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
body: The Word of God becomes most effective in your life not only when you believe it, but when you confess it. That is why, at salvation, it was not enough to believe in Jesus as the Son of God; you also had to open your mouth and declare it.

The Greek word for confession is homologeo, which means to express the same thing, to agree with, or to acknowledge. Your confession is the outward expression of your inward belief; it is the release of your faith.

Jesus said, All things are possible to him that believeth (Mark 9:23). Yet many believe without seeing results. Why? This is because, often times, the confession is missing. Faith is both believing and speaking.
When you confess, you are affirming what God has already said concerning you. This is why Joshua 1:8 instructs, This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth… You would observe
that it says mouth, not just heart.

Your life will always move in the direction of your words. The circumstances you experience today are largely the result of the words you spoke in the past. Words are nothing but seeds. When you confess God's Word, you are sowing seeds that must germinate and produce fruits that look exactly like your words (Galatians 6:7; Hebrews 4:12).

Paul said in 2 Corinthians 4:13 KJV, We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak. This is a strong reminder that faith speaks. Begin to boldly declare what you have seen and believed in Scripture. As you do, those words will shape your reality.
prayer: The Word of God is alive in me. My words are full of power. I confess that I am who God says I am. I am not moved by what I see; I am only moved by the Word of God. The Word is gaining ascendancy over my mind, my body, my words, and everything I do. I grow daily in the knowledge of God's Word. Glory to God!
furtherStudies: Deuteronomy 30:14 KJV, Proverbs 18:21 KJV, James 3:5 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Renew Your Mind
verse: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect will of God.
body: Abeliever should not imitate the fleeting patterns and lifestyles of this present world, but instead be wholly transformed by the renewing of the mind. Your mind is the seat of your reasoning, thoughts, and understanding.

When you came into the world as a baby, your mind was neutral. Over time, it absorbed information from your environment; some good, some evil. When the mind is filled with worldly principles, it becomes an instrument for evil. But when it is informed and guided by the Spirit, it becomes an instrument for good and for God's works.

That is why God needs you to renew your mind. Through education and experiences, the mind learns to distinguish between good and evil. But true renewal comes by replacing all the old, corrupt, and negative information with God's Word.

Think of it like a computer: when you delete corrupt files and install new ones, the system runs better. In the same way, when you replace negative thoughts and worldly patterns with the Word of God, your life takes on a new outlook. This new outlook is called transformation.

Whatever kind of change you want to see in your life begins from your mind. When you feed your mind with God's Word, it will influence your life from the inside, and eventually, it will show on the outside.

Ephesians 4:23 NLT says, Instead, let the Spirit renew your thoughts and attitudes. Renewal is not a one-time thing; it is a continuous process. Each time God's Word comes to you, don't resist it or argue with it. Receive it with meekness, allow it to shape your thought process, and the Holy Spirit will cause true transformation. Over time, you will see this change reflected in your words, actions, and lifestyle.
prayer: God's Word is alive in me. It is transforming my life daily. I do not resist the Word of God; I receive it with meekness and gladness. I yield myself to the Spirit of God and His work of transformation in me. The Holy Spirit is renewing my thoughts, shaping my attitude, and causing my life to reflect God's glory. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: John 2:15-17 KJV, Colossians 3:10 KJV, Psalm 51:10 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Stop the Accusation
verse: I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and remembers your sins no more.
body: God alone has the power to blot out sin, and He did so fully through the sacrifice of Jesus on the cross. But notice the second part of that verse: remembers your sins no more. This is not only God's posture toward us; it should also be our posture toward others and ourselves.

To remember someone's wrongs means to keep a record of them, to rehearse them continuously in our minds, or to use them as a weapon when hurt lingers. But true forgiveness means letting go of hurt completely. It signifies restoration of relationship and freedom from accusation.

The Bible says in 2 Corinthians 5:19 NIV: ...not counting people's sins against them... To count someone's sins against them is to accuse them, and when we do, we are not reflecting the nature of God. Forgiveness does not wait for apologies; it flows from the love of God within us.
The one whose nature is to accuse vehemently is the devil.

Revelation 12:10 calls him the accuser of God's people. Satan constantly accuses believers before God, but at the same time, Jesus is interceding and advocating for us. Colossians 2:14 NLT tells us: He canceled the record of the charges against us and took it away by nailing it to the cross.

Beloved, Jesus has already erased the record of your sins. That means you must first forgive yourself. Stop replaying your past failures. Then, extend that same forgiveness to others. Don't remind them of their wrongs. Don't wait for them to apologize before you release them in your heart.
I pray for you: May the Lord purge your heart of every trace of self-accusation, bitterness, pain, and unforgiveness, in Jesus' name.
prayer: The Holy Spirit is working on my mind right now. He is flushing away every file of resentment, offense, trauma, unforgiveness, and condemnation. I let them go. I experience the love of Christ lavished upon my heart. My heart is healed, free, and at peace in Jesus' name. Amen!
furtherStudies: READINGBIBLE Romans 4:7-8 KJV, Colossians 2:13-14 KJV, Romans 5:17-19 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Your Faith Moves God
verse: But let him ask in faith, with no doubting…
body: To doubt means to have a divided mind; to not be fully convinced. It means you are not completely sure it will happen. Many people often doubt because they feel unworthy, or they feel their sin disqualifies them, or maybe they think they haven't prayed enough. Some even believe they are not God's favorites, or that their challenge is too big for Him to answer.

The good news is, faith is not about how you feel. It is about what God's Word has said. God wants you to simply believe. Don't try to figure out how it will happen. Just trust what His Word has declared concerning your situation.

Mark 11:23 ISV says, I tell all of you with certainty, if anyone says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' if he doesn't doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, it will be done for him. There is so much audacity, assurance, and confidence in the words of Jesus in the scripture above. That means it is not a probability. It is a law.
Faith is that law. Speaking to a challenge you are facing, without
doubting in your heart, ensures your words will come to pass. Afflictions and challenges do not move God. It is your faith that moves Him. Faith is a catalyst; it activates God's intervention.

Hebrews 11:2 KJV says, By faith the elders obtained a good report. The great people of old were commended for their faith. By faith, they achieved very great things, overcame obstacles, defeated enemies, and obtained victories. You too can apply your faith, achieve great things, and have testimonies.

Zechariah 4:7 boldy declares: What are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel? You shall become a plain… What is that great obstacle, affliction, sickness, or challenge before you? Speak to it, and the hand of God will take it away, in Jesus' name, Amen!
prayer: In the name of Jesus, I speak to every obstacle against my health, my family, my ministry, and my finances. Be removed completely and made into a plain ground for me to thrive and advance. I am making progress in every area of my life in the name of Jesus. Amen.
furtherStudies: Mark 11:23 KJV, Hebrews 11:6 KJV, Matthew 14:31 KJV, Romans 4:18–25 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: His Word Heals
verse: He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.
body: The Good News Translation renders Psalm 107:20 as, He sent his word, and healed them; he rescued them from the grave. The Word of God is not just a spoken language; it is a totally dynamic force that accomplishes God's purpose. There is great power and authority in God's Word.

Romans 1:16 KJV says, For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believeth… God's Word is very powerful. Anyone who believes God's Word will experience the same power contained in it.

From the beginning of creation, as recorded in Genesis, God spoke His Word, and everything He said manifested physically. When the Scripture says, He sent His word, it means God spoke His Word. The effect of that spoken Word was healing and deliverance.
Sickness and disease are incipient forms of death. Every sickness is an early stage designed to lead to death. So, when Scripture declares, He delivered them from the grave, it means
God's Word rescued them from sicknesses that were meant to take them to the grave. God's Word crystallizes into what was spoken. As declared in John 1:14, The Word became flesh.

You may be in dire need of healing right now. The key is to hold on to God's Word concerning your health and believe strongly in what He has said. 1 Peter 2:24 says, By his stripes you were healed. Do you believe what God's Word says about you? If your answer is Yes, then no matter what is happening in your body, declare to yourself, I am healed, and thank you, Father, for healing me in Jesus' name. Amen.

I pray for you: May the healing anointing of the Holy Spirit come upon you right now. I proclaim that you are healed of every disease, sickness, and infirmity. May you receive wholeness in your body in Jesus' name. Amen.
prayer: Thank You, Lord, for healing me from every disease. I affirm that I am healed and whole in Jesus' name. I thank You, Lord, because whom You set free is free indeed. I declare that I am free from every disease, every virus, and every malfunctioning in my body.
furtherStudies: Isaiah 55:11 KJV, Matthew 8:8 ESV, Matthew 15:28 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Where is your Faith?
verse: And He said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for He commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey Him.
body: Where is your faith? Is your faith placed in the wrong things? Is your confidence rooted in riches because of what they can acquire for you? Is your faith in yourself? Your beauty, intelligence, eloquence, skills, and hard work or is your faith in God?

The disciples of Jesus, as seen in Luke 8:25, did not exercise faith in God despite all the wonders and miracles they had seen Jesus perform. Some of them were fishermen and could swim; perhaps they had always relied on their swimming skills. But the moment they faced a storm beyond their abilities, they became afraid. If their faith had been anchored in God, no matter the occasion, they would not have been shaken.

The winds and the waters obeyed the command of Jesus. This is not only applicable to Him; the winds and the waters can obey you too when you have faith and do not doubt. Doubt is the enemy of your miracle. The winds and waters represent the storms and turbulence of life. You can speak to any storm or challenge you are facing, and it will cease. Mark 11:23 NIV says, Truly I tell you, if anyone says to this mountain, Go, throw
yourself into the sea,' and does not doubt in their heart but believes that what they say will happen, it will be done for them.
Now, use the mighty name of Jesus to speak to that seemingly insurmountable challenge or obstacle before you. Do not doubt in your heart, and God will cause it to be removed from your way.
prayer: My faith is alive in God. I am strong in the Lord and in the power of His might. My faith is steadfast and unmovable. Therefore, I speak peace into my home, my finances, my health, and all that concerns me. I declare that every storm ceases right now, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Matthew 8:26 KJV, Romans 10:17 KJV, Nahum 1:4
author: Apostle Chuks

title: He Keeps you in Perfect Peace
verse: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
body: It is God's responsibility to cause you to experience peace. The world cannot give you true peace. Perfect peace is from God, and it surpasses human understanding. In Hebrew, the phrase perfect peace is translated as shalom shalom, a repetition that signifies all-round peace.

2 Thessalonians 3:16 KJV says, Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. God, who is the Lord of peace, can give you peace in your spirit, soul, and body. Peace in your body means health, wholeness, and a life free from infirmity. The Holy Spirit, who dwells in you, vitalizes your mortal body, ensuring that every cell, organ, hormone, and system functions perfectly (Romans 8:11).

3 John 1:2 NIV says, Dear friend, I pray that you may enjoy good health and that all may go well with you, even as your soul is getting along well. God desires that you live in perfect health. This is available to those whose minds are fixed on Him. Do not allow sickness to dominate your thoughts or shift your attention. God requires undivided focus on His Word.

When Peter walked on water in Matthew 14:22-23, he began to sink only when he allowed the wind to distract him. You become whatever captures your attention. Keep your focus on God's Word concerning your health. Meditate on it, confess it, and speak it boldly to your body. The result will be perfect peace in your health. Glory to God!
prayer: Lord, I trust You with all my heart, and I keep my mind stayed on Your Word. I experience perfect peace in my body. I am healthy and totally sound. The life of God flows in my blood and sustains me in divine health, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Isaiah 53:5 KJV; 1 Thessalonians 5:23; Matthew 8:17 AMP
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Advancing His Kingdom through Prayers
verse: Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning: thou hast the dew of thy youth
body: The Amplified version of Psalm 110:3 says, Your people will offer themselves willingly [to participate in Your battle] in the day of Your power… Every effort the body of Christ puts in for the work of the Lord is an opposition to the kingdom of darkness. Evangelism, prayer, Bible study, visitation, giving to the needy, loving one another, encouraging others, and many more are all efforts to cause the kingdom of God to prosper. Yet Satan and his kingdom have always opposed the advancement of God's work. In the day of His power, God's people will be willing to put in efforts towards the expansion of His kingdom.

Matthew 11:12 KJV says, And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom of heaven is God's sovereign rule, which Jesus came to establish on earth. Everyone who receives salvation has been ushered into God's kingdom. But the kingdom of heaven on earth has always faced opposition and persecution. John the Baptist, Jesus, and His disciples encountered violence, and this opposition continues today. These attacks may come from individuals or groups,
including religious leaders and political authorities, but they are ultimately engineered from the kingdom of darkness.

This clearly shows the ongoing spiritual warfare between God's kingdom and the forces of evil. The obvious violent reaction to the advancement of God's kingdom was evident in the hostility toward Jesus and His message, the martyrdom of His disciples, the present-day killings of Christians, and the attacks against the church. The enemy seeks to silence the gospel and distract God's people from their inheritance and their responsibility to advance His kingdom.

From the scripture above, the violent refers to men whose minds are made up, men who are ready to employ spiritual force to advance God's kingdom. They take it by force, grasping it as decisively as bandits snatch their prey. Our Lord Jesus was pointing to the energy and determination required to press into God's kingdom, urging us to show the same if salvation is to be obtained and worked out (Philippians 2:12).

You may speak to people all day without making an impact, but when you minister in the place of prayer, the Spirit of God compels them to listen and receive the message of salvation. Prayer is what sets people on fire for the Lord. Prayer ignites revival. Through prayer, the Holy Spirit convicts unbelievers of sin, stirs believers to greater devotion, and quickens the church and the nations to turn to God. This is how the kingdom of God prospers and advances in our time.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for the work of your Spirit in my life. Thank you for the light and revelation your word has brought to me today. I declare that I am a burning and shining light. As I pray, men and women are set on fire for you, turning to repentance. The nations are saved, and your will is done on earth in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Hebrews 11:33-34 KJV, Jeremiah 20:9 KJV, Job 32:18-20 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Enablement of Divine Skills
verse: Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation. And he informed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding
body: The skill in the context of our opening Bible verse refers to wisdom. This skill comes with discernment and insight into the complexities of life. It is an enablement to see beyond the surface level. The involvement of an angel from God shows that this wisdom is divine and not intellectual.

Proverbs 4:7 KJV clearly teaches us: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore, get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding. Wisdom is a divine attribute that reveals God's character. The Hebrew word for wisdom is chokmah, which entails not just knowledge but also the skillful application of knowledge. Wisdom is supreme. It is of greater value than riches and earthly power. This is why it is important to prioritize wisdom above all else.
The scripture tells us to acquire wisdom, not fame or riches. With wisdom, riches and other necessities of life will follow. Wisdom is not automatic; it must be diligently pursued. This
pursuit is likened to a treasure hunt, as Proverbs 2:4 describes wisdom in relation to silver and hidden treasures. King Solomon understood this principle, which is why he asked God for wisdom.

In the Book of Daniel, divine intervention went beyond the impartation of wisdom and skill. When Daniel set his heart to seek God through prayer and fasting, his request was heard immediately. God dispatched the angel Gabriel to deliver the answer, but Gabriel was resisted and delayed for twenty-one days by the spiritual force of the Persian kingdom. Because Daniel remained steadfast, God sent Michael, a higher-ranked angel, to assist Gabriel and ensure the message was delivered. This shows the reality of spiritual warfare behind answered prayer and the layered nature of divine intervention. Daniel did not only receive wisdom; he also received angelic help, revealing that God's response matched both the resistance faced and the persistence shown (Daniel 10:12-13 KJV).

Are there areas in your life where you need divine wisdom, understanding, solutions, or intervention? Do you wonder why certain situations have lingered? Often, unseen forces are at work behind the scenes. What you truly need is divine skill. Divine skill brings wisdom, progress, breakthrough, direction, and deliverance. Make time to seek the Lord earnestly through prayer and fasting, and He will intervene.
I pray for you today: May the Lord strengthen you, guide you, and send His angels to minister to you. In Jesus' name, Amen.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for the divine enablement of your Spirit in my life. Thank you for increased wisdom and revelation. I declare that I am filled with divine wisdom and understanding in all matters of life. I am divinely guided by your Spirit. I have insight into all things. As I seek your face, I will continue to grow in wisdom. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Proverbs 9:10 KJV, Ephesians 1:17 KJV, Colossians 1:9 ESV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: You Have Received a Royal Calling
verse: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
body: In the Old Testament, the tribe of Levi was set apart as priests to serve Israel. This was known as the Levitical priesthood, and their duties included offering sacrifices, maintaining the tabernacle, and acting as mediators between God and the people.

In Genesis 14:18–21, we are introduced to Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the Most High God. He blessed Abram, showing us a foreshadow of a priesthood that was both royal and spiritual. This pointed forward to Christ.

The New Testament clearly confirms this in Hebrews 7:17 KJV: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec. Christ's death and resurrection brought a new covenant, establishing Him as our eternal High Priest. Because of Him, all believers now share in this royal priesthood, a reality often called the priesthood of all believers.

This means you are no longer ordinary. In Christ, you are both a king and a priest. You have direct access to God's presence and carry spiritual authority. You don’t need a human mediator at all; Jesus has already made the way open. As part of this royal calling:

· Your prayers, worship, and service are powerful and meaningful. · You represent God on earth, offering spiritual sacrifices such as thanksgiving, praise, fervent worship, obedience, and the joyous sharing of His Word. · Your life is to reflect God's character, goodness, and glory daily.
Don't let feelings of insignificance hold you back. You have been set apart by God Himself. Walk in the dignity and responsibility of your calling, serving Him with boldness and devotion
prayer: Father, thank You for calling me into Your royal priesthood. Thank You for making me a competent minister of Your name. Today I declare that I will continually offer to You my sacrifice of praise, my body, and my substance. Use me as a vessel to reflect Your light in my world, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Revelation 1:6 (KJV), Isaiah 61:6 (KJV), Ephesians 3:12 (KJV)
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Test of your Obedience
verse: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, once your obedience is complete.
body: Every believer will encounter moments where obedience is tested. These are times that demand alignment with God's will, even when it totally feels uncomfortable, inconvenient, or unpopular. These tests reveal more than just outward behavior; they uncover the posture of your heart.

All through Scripture, we see that God allows His people to pass through seasons that prove their loyalty and devotion, whether they will walk in His ways or yield to the desires of the flesh. These tests are never meant to destroy, but to refine and strengthen faith. As James 1:3 teaches, The testing of your faith produces perseverance.

Obedience is not mere compliance; it is worship. It is declaring, Lord, not my will, but Yours be done. Each step of obedience is a seed that produces growth, maturity, and favor with God. It positions you for divine promotion.

On the other hand, disobedience creates cracks in your spiritual wall. It opens the door for the enemy to creep in. Ecclesiastes 10:8 KJV says, He that breaketh the hedge, the serpent shall bite. Persistent rebellion absolutely weakens your defenses, while obedience fortifies them. God has declared, I will make you a wall to this people, a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to rescue and save you (Jeremiah 15:20).

Remember, the enemy who tempts you is the same one who accuses you before God. Don't let him trap you in cycles of guilt and defeat. Victory is possible through Christ. You can resist temptation. You can obey. You are not a child of disobedience. You are a child of God. Let this truth guide your choices daily.
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for the grace to walk in obedience. By Your Spirit, I choose Your will over mine and honor You in my thoughts, words, and actions. I am a child of God. I completely walk in obedience. My walls are fortified. The enemy has no hold on me, in Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Isaiah 5:5 KJV; Job 1:6–12 KJV; Zechariah 2:5 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Rendering Diligent Services
verse: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
body: In the Bible, diligence is a virtue that means to work hard, persevere, and pay close attention to one's duties. To be diligent basically involves being intentional. Diligence is characterized by careful attention to detail, a commitment to excellence, completeness, and persistence. It is a quality that connects with wisdom and prosperity. Proverbs 10:4 KJV says, He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

From our opening scripture, we see that a life of diligence is expected from every believer in everything they do, including the workplace. Diligence and skill were highly regarded both in Bible days and in our present times. In Exodus 31:1-6, during the construction of the Tabernacle, God specifically chose skilled and diligent artisans. The Hebrew word for skilled refers to expertise and proficiency, showing that God values excellence in your profession.
People who are highly diligent in whatever they do often find themselves and their services required by royalty and people of influence. God usually rewards diligence with opportunities for

leadership and impact. In Genesis 41:38-42, Joseph rose to prominence in Egypt because of his diligence. In Daniel 1:19- 20, Daniel's wisdom and ability to interpret dreams elevated him before the king of Babylon. David moved from being a shepherd boy to a king. Nehemiah rose from a cupbearer to a governor.

Honor and recognition come with excellence. Obscure men are those without influence or recognition, but God elevates those who are faithful, skilled, and diligent. Do not be the one who is committed in church but performs poorly in school or at work. You have an excellent spirit. Therefore, strive to be diligent, for the Lord will give you opportunities for greater service and impact. Ecclesiastes 9:10 KJV says, Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.

You can also be diligent in your thoughts, words, and actions. Joshua 1:8 KJV says, This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. This verse emphasizes the importance of intentionally keeping God's Word in your mouth, speaking it consistently and purposefully. It also calls for guarding your heart and mind by meditating on His Word day and night so that your actions align with His will.

Such consistency in speech, thought, and conduct requires diligence. Therefore, remain diligent in all things, continually aligning your life with God's truth, and you will walk in prosperity and good success. Finally, in your service to God, be diligent in carrying out all He has planned for you.
prayer: Thank you, Father, for the gift of the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit has brought wisdom and excellence into my life and causes me to produce excellence in all things. I declare that I will always be diligent and never lazy or slothful in business. There is no mediocrity in my life. I make all things beautiful and excellent, hallelujah.
furtherStudies: Colossians 3:23 KJV, Proverbs 4:20-27 KJV, Proverbs 13:4 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Revival in the Church
verse: Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning: thou hast the dew of thy youth
body: In the day of His power, God's people will be willing. Willing to do what? Willing to serve God in Spirit and in truth, to be committed and consistent, to be discipled and actively involved in His work. The willingness of the people reveals a readiness to serve and support the agenda of the Lord. This is an indication of a transformation of hearts and minds leading to revival.

I have heard and seen cases where brethren do not want to get committed in church or support the work of the Lord. As a shepherd or leader of such people, you do not have to get frustrated or compel them to be actively involved in the vision. Simply learn to win behind closed doors. I mean, you should win not behind the pulpit but on your knees in prayer. Except you pray, you might struggle, complain, and even get discouraged. Their willingness is not dependent on your eloquence or human effort but by the Spirit.
In the church today, our major opponent is not human beings. We are not battling with man but against spiritual forces of darkness that veil and bend the minds of people. 2 Corinthians

4:4 KJV says, In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. This blinding of minds is an intense spiritual blindness that prevents people from understanding and accepting the truth of the gospel.

Satan does not blind the minds of unbelievers only. He tries to stop them from believing the gospel and also distracts believers to ensure the gospel does not take root in them. His plan is to make them unfruitful and unestablished in God. That is why some new converts find themselves drifting back to worldliness. We wage this war and obtain victory through prayer.

Galatians 4:19 KJV says, My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you. To travail in prayer until Christ is formed in others implies a deep, often painful form of intercessory prayer, where you intensely pray for others until they reveal the character and nature of Christ. It is a spiritual labor compared to childbirth, reflecting the intense effort and longing for spiritual growth in those being prayed for.

This is an ongoing process, revealing that spiritual maturity is not instantaneous but requires time and effort. The labor continues until Christ is completely and permanently formed in the hearts of the brethren. During this process, the Lord will put His word in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts (Jeremiah 31:33). Then they will become willing to accept the counsel of God and be vitally involved in the Master's agenda.
prayer: Dear Lord, I thank you for the light of your word that has shined upon my heart today. I thank you for the divine awakening of my heart by your Spirit. I will remain on fire for you and continue to intercede for others. I declare that the influence of the devil over my mind, family, and nation is broken. May the light of your word shine brightly upon their hearts, leading to a great revival in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Ephesians 2:2 CSV, John 8:44 KJV, Ezekiel 36:26 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Lord is with you
verse: Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD will personally go ahead of you. He will be with you; He will neither fail you nor abandon you.
body: Discouragement and fear are natural ways humans respond to challenges or uncertainties. As believers, the reverse is the case. Because of the abiding presence of the Holy Spirit in our lives, we have an advantage. The Holy Spirit counters fear and discouragement by giving us divine assurance.

In 1 Samuel 17, we find the account of Goliath and David. Goliath was a skilled and experienced giant warrior. He used divination and worshipped Dagon, and even had to invoke his god when he cursed David (1 Samuel 17:43). On the other hand, David was a young shepherd with no military experience. He could not even use the armor. But he confronted Goliath, defeated him, and the rest of the Philistines ran away.

David was not afraid, and he was not discouraged because his confidence was in God. He did not try to quantify or evaluate the opposition. The more you evaluate the challenge, the more it occupies your mind and magnifies fear. At that point, faith dwindles and you will miss out on the grace and victory God has
made available to you (Jonah 2:8 KJV).

Anytime fear arises within you, just know it is not from God. 2 Timothy 1:7 says, For God has not given you the spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind. God knows that there are things that will show up to discourage and plant fear in your path of destiny. That is why He assures you of His presence with you, with His unfailing faithfulness and commitment never to forsake you. Be assured that God is with you.
prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for Your presence in me and with me at all times. I am grateful that You go ahead of me to make every crooked way straight. I declare that I glide through a smooth path in life. Every challenge bows before me because the Lord is with me. I am fearless and courageous always, in Jesus' name. Amen.
furtherStudies: Hebrews 13:5 KJV, Matthew 28:20 KJV, Isaiah 41:10 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: The Blessings of Corporate Worship
verse: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
body: Christianity is not a solitary journey. From Genesis to Revelation, Scripture consistently presents the life of faith in the context of community. God's design has always included people walking together supporting, strengthening, and worshiping as one. The church is described using collective imagery: a body with many parts (Romans 12:4-5), a spiritual house built with living stones (1 Peter 2:5), a holy nation (1 Peter 2:9) and a flock under one Shepherd. These metaphors remind us that no believer is meant to live out their faith alone.

Jesus made a profound promise in Matthew 18:20: when even a few gather in His name, He is present among them. This is not merely a poetic idea; it is a spiritual reality. The presence of God intensifies when His people gather with unified hearts. This is often called the corporate anointing, the unique grace and power released when believers come together in worship and purpose. In a world where opposition is often organized and widespread, the church must not be scattered or disconnected. It is much harder for a single person to stand against spiritual opposition alone, but in unity, believers find strength (Ecclesiastes 4:9-12). As an army moves as one, so too should God's people. Therefore, do not separate yourself from the house of God. Be actively involved in the church.

The prophet Isaiah offers a vision of peace and security for God's people: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities (Isaiah 33:20 KJV). Here, Zion refers to God's dwelling with His people, a place of worship, celebration, and stability. It is a prophetic image of the church as a spiritual home where God's presence abides.

We see a powerful example of seeking refuge in 1 Kings 2:28. Joab, fearing judgment, ran to the tabernacle of the Lord and caught hold of the horns of the altar. In Israel, holding the horns of the altar was a recognized way of seeking protection or sanctuary (see Exodus 21:13-14). Today, while we may not cling to physical altars, we abide in Christ, our true Altar (Hebrews 13:10) and in His body, the church, for covering, restoration, and spiritual safety. When we engage in corporate worship, we are not merely attending a service; we are entering a divine space where God moves among His people.
prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for the gift of the church, a place of strength, peace and Your abiding presence. Teach me to value the blessings of gathering with other believers. Draw me into deeper fellowship and unity within the body of Christ. I affirm I am established in Your house and my heart will always be anchored in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
furtherStudies: Psalm 133:1-3 KJV, Hebrews 10:24-25 KJV, Romans 12:4-5 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Your Identity in Christ
verse: And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
body: When you got saved, you were not just forgiven; you were born anew with a new identity and repositioned from where you used to be to a place called Christ. You stepped into a new identity that heaven recognizes and hell fears. Scripture tells us that God wants the eyes of your understanding opened, so you fully grasp the hope, inheritance and power available to you as His child (Ephesians 1:18-19). You are not just walking on earth; you are spiritually seated with Christ in heavenly places, a position of authority and dominion.

This new status means you are no longer subject to spiritual defeat. Ephesians 2:6 reveals that God raised you up with Christ and seated you with Him far above any demonic power, fear or stronghold. If Jesus is enthroned above all and you are seated with Him, then, you operate from victory not for it. You are empowered to walk in boldness, overcome temptation, and influence your world for God's kingdom. Dominion is your birthright.

Your strength is not self-made; it comes from the indwelling presence of the Holy Spirit. 1 John 4:4 reminds us that greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world. You do not face life alone. God lives in you, equipping you to handle challenges and resist the enemy. That power enables you to live a life marked by peace, righteousness and spiritual effectiveness.

Being in Christ means you no longer live under limitation. Philippians 4:13 KJV says, I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. You have access to divine strength, supernatural wisdom and endless grace. You are not defined by your past or your struggles. Your identity is found in the one who overcame death and sin. You have overcome the world through your faith (1 John 5:4-5). This is your present reality.

As a child of God, your life is meant to reflect His authority and goodness. You carry the name, power and image of Christ. Heaven sees you as victorious. The more you grow in the knowledge of your identity, the more you will operate in confidence, walk in your spiritual inheritance, and fulfill your calling. You are no longer a victim of circumstance; you are a vessel of glory and a bearer of light.
prayer: I am seated with Christ in a place of authority. I live from a position of victory not defeat. God's Spirit within me empowers me every day. I am not who the world says I am; I am who God says I am. My life reflects the glory and dominion of Christ.
furtherStudies: Romans 8:16-17 KJV, Colossians 2:10 KJV, Galatians 2:20 ESV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Halloween is not for Christains
verse: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.
body: Halloween is widely viewed as a fun and harmless celebration filled with costumes, candy and spooky decorations. However, its origins trace back to the ancient festival of Samhain where people believed the boundary between the living and the dead was blurred, leading to occult rituals and communication with spirits. These practices are not merely historical or cultural artifacts; they reflect spiritual darkness that Scripture warns us to avoid. As believers, God calls us to live distinctly, rejecting anything that associates us with darkness and instead, walking as children of light.

The Bible is very clear on this point. Ephesians 5:11 urges us not to have fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness but rather to reprove them. The imagery associated with Halloween (witches, ghosts, and demons) is not just playful fantasy; these symbols represent real spiritual forces opposed to God's holiness and purity. In 1 John 1:5, we are reminded that God is light and that in Him, there is no darkness at all. When we engage in customs that glorify evil, fear or death, we risk stepping away from God's light and inviting confusion or spiritual harm. Scripture also warns against adopting pagan or occult practices. Jeremiah 10:2 commands us not to learn the way of the heathen, and Deuteronomy 18:10-12 explicitly forbids divination sorcery and contacting the dead, calling these detestable to the Lord. Choosing to participate in such activities, even indirectly through cultural celebrations, opens doors to deception and compromises our witness. Romans 13:12 exhorts us to cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light. This is a call to live intentionally for Christ and to reflect His holiness in every area of life.

As you consider the season, reflect on your heart and choices. Are there traditions or celebrations that might be pulling you closer to darkness instead of light? This is an opportunity to intentionally choose the path of holiness; to live boldly as a child of light. Instead of Halloween's dark customs, seek ways to shine Christ's light through acts of kindness, prayer and celebrations that honor God. Your life can be a powerful testimony in a dark world, pointing others toward the hope and purity found only in Jesus. Remember, the night is passing and the day is at hand. Put on the armor of light and walk boldly in God's truth.
prayer: I declare that I am a child of light. I reject all works of darkness and stand firm in the armor of God. I will walk boldly in the truth and holiness of Christ, shining His light in every area of my life. My light shines brightly. I cannot be dimmed.
furtherStudies: Jeremiah 10:2 KJV, Deuteronomy 18:10-12 KJV, 2 Corinthians 6:14 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: God is Ushering you into a New Place
verse: Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed she brought forth her children.
body: There are divine seasons when God initiates a shift so dramatic and supernatural that it completely defies human reasoning. These moments signal a rebirth not only of individuals but of communities, territories and even nations. In Ezekiel 37, God brought the prophet to a valley of dry bones: hopeless scattered remnants of a people long forgotten. Yet, by stages, and by the Spirit of God, those bones came together, flesh formed upon them, and breath re-entered lifeless bodies. That vision was more than a metaphor; it was a declaration of national resurrection and restoration.

In Isaiah 66:8, the prophet poses a bold question: can a nation be born in a day? This was a rhetorical challenge to human limitation and a prophetic unveiling of God's sovereignty. It reveals that when God moves, timelines collapse. What would take years in the natural can occur in moments under divine instruction. This is true not only for nations but also for individuals. God can shift your season in a moment, birthing new realities, assignments, and dimensions of destiny.

The covenant promise in Genesis 17:8 clearly shows God's commitment to establishing His people in a place of lasting inheritance. God does not just bring you into a new phase; He gives you the power to thrive in it and influence others through it. Just like the dry bones, there may be areas in your life or family that appear lifeless, scattered or forgotten. Yet, by the word of the Lord and the breath of His Spirit, restoration is coming. Your identity calling and inheritance are being reassembled, and breath is being released into what seemed dead. This is not just a refreshing season; it is a transformational rebirth. It is a nation within you coming alive.

As you align with God's direction in prayer, obedience and faith, be prepared to walk into something radically new. The grave of delay is opening. The burial cloth of past seasons is being removed. It is time to rise to be established and to become the living proof that God's promises do not fail.
prayer: I declare that I am stepping into a new phase ordained by God. Every dry place in my life receives fresh breath. I believe in the God who brings nations and destinies to life in a moment. I arise from every grave of delay and limitation, and I enter into my inheritance. I am a strong part of God's divine rebirth plan, called, chosen, and established to manifest His glory. In Jesus' name, Amen!
furtherStudies: Ezekiel 37:1-14 KJV, Isaiah 66:7-9 KJV, Genesis 17:1-8 NKJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Get to the Boiling Point
verse: The earnest prayer of a righteous person has great power and produces wonderful results.
body: In the natural, the boiling point is the moment when a pure substance like water undergoes a transformation due to intense heat and pressure. It transitions from one state to another; from liquid to vapor. Spiritually, this mirrors what happens when a believer enters into deep, persistent and fervent prayer. The fire of the Holy Spirit, coupled with spiritual pressure through consistent intercession, generates the conditions for supernatural transformation.

A pure substance in this context refers to a life set apart, yielded to God, cleansed from sin, and positioned for encounter. Many believers are unaware that their current spiritual state is far below their prophetic destiny. The enemy thrives in stagnancy but God's purpose for His children is growth, movement and increase. Every significant spiritual transition is marked by divine pressure; a call to deeper, sustained prayer, much like Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3). That moment of divine interruption was a spiritual boiling point leading to national deliverance.

Elijah's life also illustrates this power of boiling point prayer. Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are (James 5:17–18), yet his earnest prayers firmly controlled the rain and released fruitfulness on the earth. His impact was not by mere words but by sustained fiery and Spirit-led prayer. This intensity not only shifted the climate of a nation but also caused the earth to yield its increase. This is what happens when we persist in prayer. Our prayer creates pressure that births transformation. When you consistently engage in prayer, you are digging into the depths of God's presence, and searching out things hidden for you, not from you. As Isaiah 45:3 KJV says, I will give thee the treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places. These are only revealed to those who push past the surface. It is the glory of kings to search out a matter (Proverbs 25:2). Prayer becomes the spiritual tool for excavation, drawing out divine ideas, solutions, revelations and breakthroughs.

Do not settle for shallow encounters. Get to your boiling point: that place where your prayers are absolutely intense, your faith is stretched, and your heart is fully engaged. In that place, God increases your spiritual capacity, entrusts you with more, and causes you to operate in His glory. Fruitfulness, favor, power, and insight await those who are willing to burn with passion in the place of prayer.
prayer: Today, I press into deeper prayer. I refuse to remain stagnant. I will pray until something shifts. I declare that as I reach my boiling point, every limitation breaks, every delay ends, and every hidden treasure is uncovered. My life is changing, and I move from glory to glory in Jesus' name.
furtherStudies: James 5:16–18 NLT, Exodus 3:1–12 ASV, Isaiah 45:3 KJV
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Learn to Forgive
verse: If you forgive those who sin against you, your heavenly Father will forgive you. But if you refuse to forgive others, your Father will not forgive your sins.
body: Forgiveness is not just an act; it is a divine expression of God's heart. As believers, we are called to reflect His character and that includes the grace to release those who have hurt us. It does not mean the pain did not happen or that it does not matter. It means we are choosing to be like our Father in heaven who forgave us while we were yet sinners. Your ability to forgive even when it hurts is a powerful measure of spiritual maturity.

In Matthew 18, Jesus paints a striking picture of a servant who was forgiven an unimaginable debt only to turn around and withhold mercy from another who owed him far less. His refusal to extend the same grace led to severe consequences. This parable reminds us that unforgiveness is a heavy burden that not only traps others, but also binds us. If we who have received much mercy from God are unwilling to forgive, we hinder our own relationship with Him.

Forgiveness is not about keeping score. When Peter asked Jesus how many times we must forgive, expecting perhaps seven to be sufficient, Jesus responded with seventy times; seven not a literal number, but a command to forgive without limit. God does not cap His forgiveness toward us and neither should we toward others. Forgiveness should flow from a heart that has been touched and shaped by mercy.

Many people think forgiveness is for the benefit of the other person but in truth, it sets you free. It opens your heart to healing and allows you to move forward unburdened. Bitterness clogs spiritual growth and leaves little room for the Spirit to move freely in your life. When you choose to forgive, you are walking in obedience, humility and love which are three core pillars of a Christ-like life.

Let forgiveness become your way of life. This does not mean being naïve or lacking wise boundaries. It means releasing resentment and entrusting justice to God. As you do, His peace will guard your heart, His joy will be restored in your soul, and His presence will remain evident in your walk.
prayer: I affirm that I will always walk in forgiveness. I release every offense and every burden I have held onto. I will not allow bitterness or pain to define my heart. Just as I have been forgiven through Christ, I extend forgiveness to others. I am free, whole and full of God's love. His grace empowers me to live above offense and to love as He loves.
furtherStudies: Matthew 18:21–35, Colossians 3:12–13, Ephesians 4:31–32, Luke 6:36–38, Mark 11:25
author: Apostle Chuks

title: Let Love Rule in your Family and Relationships
verse: Dear children let us not love with words or speech but with actions and in truth.
body: God designed the family and marriage as highly sacred institutions to reflect His heart and glory. Within these relationships, love must be more than a feeling it must be a commitment demonstrated through daily acts of sacrifice, patience and truth.
